User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
Content

1

SAP Business One, Web Client

This document guides you through the available features and functions in SAP Business One, Web client.

The Web client runs on both MS SQL Server database and SAP HANA database technology. It offers SAP
Business One core business logic and processes with enhancements in business data analytics, provided in a
new user experience based on the SAP Fiori design concept.

For information about features and functions in SAP Business One, see SAP Business One 10.0.

For information about installation and configuration of the Web client component, see the Administrator's
Guides:

• SAP Business One Administrator's Guide, version for SAP HANA
• SAP Business One Administrator's Guide

1.1  Document History

The document history is a record of additions and major changes to the User Guide for SAP Business One, Web
Client.

Version

Change Date

Change

10.0 FP 2111

2021-12-03

• Home page: When editing the home page ( User Area

 Edit Home

Page

), a Reset button is now available in all predefined groups.

• Filter Bar: Date filters now support date offset formulas for specific days

of the week, specific months, and posting periods.

• A new chapter about the Web client integration with MS Teams is added.
• Purchasing: Goods receipt POs and A/P invoices are also supported in

detailed view, for Edit and Create modes.

• Business Partners:

• You can now create activities, opportunities, service calls and market-
ing documents for the current business partner by clicking the new

Create dropdown list in the upper right corner of the business partner

detailed view.

• A new section about scanning business cards is added.

• General previewing of documents: the options Preview and Choose Layout
are now available in both list and detailed views for sales and purchasing

drafts.

• With SAP Business One Microsoft 365 integration, you can now perform

the following:
• Export sales documents to Microsoft OneDrive as Word files and view
them online by clicking the Share menu and choosing the new Export

to Word option.

• Send emails with sales documents as attachments by clicking the

Share menu and choosing the new Send by Email option.
• Accounting: a new section about the management of journal entries is

added.

• Payments: a new section about the management of incoming and outgo-

ing payments is added.

• Service Calls: minor updates in Managing Service Calls [page 602] and

Working with Service Calls [page 604].

• Human Resources: a new section about the management of time sheets

is added.

• Analytics: a new section about the management of user-defined queries

(UDQs) is added.

• Sales: A/R invoices show electronic document details.

1.2  Getting Started

Getting Started contains general information about the Web client localization support, glossary, access and
login, home page structure, apps and so on.

1.2.1  Localization Support

Currently, the following localizations are supported:

Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Czech Republic,
Denmark, Egypt, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Ireland, Israel,
Italy, Japan, Lebanon, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Oman, Panama, Poland, Portugal, Puerto
Rico, Qatar, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Slovakia, South Afrika, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland,
Turkey, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom (Great Britain and Northern Ireland), and United States
of America.

You can enable support for multiple languages in SAP Business One, Web client.

Related Information

Company Settings [page 703]

1.2.2  Glossary

Terminology

Description

Web client

Abbreviated name for SAP Business One, Web client. Available as follows:

• On top of SAP Business One 10.0, version for SAP HANA; design based on

SAP Fiori concept

• On top of SAP Business One 10.0 using MS SQL Server

SAP Business One

SAP Business One client

Home Page

The page that appears once you log in to Web client. Functions as the “desktop”

of Web client and can be customized by the user.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

35

Terminology

Description

Tile

A shortcut that opens an app. The appearance of a tile depends on the app it

represents. For example, a tile that opens an app of type “List View” shows the

number of open documents of the given object and can be refreshed by the user

at any time. Tiles can open Web client functions and external assets such as “SAP

Business One Product Road Map”. In addition, you can also define your own tiles

as shortcuts to views, searches, or analytical content.

App

Main function. It enables you to perform a single task or multiple tasks related to

a specific object, or to generate reports, for example, create a sales order, close

several drafts and so on.

List View

An app that lists records of a specific object and encapsulates extensive capabili-

ties for filtering, sorting, and grouping the displayed records, as well as applying

certain actions to multiple records, for example, closing several sales orders.

View

A set of filtering, grouping and sorting parameters applied to records in a list view.

Web client is provided with a set of predefined views for the various list views,

for example “My Open Activities”. You can save your own views based on your

preferences and set these views as private or public.

Detailed View

A form that displays and enables you to create a single record of a given object,

for example, a sales order or an item master data record.

Quick View

A dialog that opens when you click a golden arrow and shows summarized infor-

mation related to a detail connected to the golden arrow – such as the “tooltip

preview” in SAP Business One. For example, clicking the golden arrow next to a

customer code displays information about the specific customer.

Overview Page

A page that provides multiple simultaneously filtered analytic views of business

data where each analytic view is presented as an Analytic Card.

Analytic Card

A card that presents an analytic view. An Overview page comprises multiple

Analytic Cards.

Analytic Chart

A page that provides a chart presentation of a filtered analytic view of business

data.

1.2.3  Access and Login

Access Web client from within SAP Business One by choosing the Web Client option under the Administration
module in the Main Menu, or by choosing the Web client icon on the toolbar.

Alternatively, click the URL provided to you by your SAP Business One partner.

36

For an optimized user experience, launch Web client in either a desktop computer or tablet, using one of the
following Web browsers:

• Google Chrome
• Mozilla Firefox
• Apple Safari (Mac and iPad)

In the login screen, choose your company database and enter your SAP Business One user name and
password. You can log in to SAP Business One and to Web client in parallel.

 Note

The SAP Business One client provides an entry to Web client. However, as part of the login process to Web
client, you have to choose the relevant company database in the login screen. If you switch to a different
company database in the SAP Business One client, it will not impact the company database you logged in
to in Web client and vice-versa.

For information about installation, deployment, and upgrade of Web client, see the Administrator’s Guide:

• SAP Business One Administrator's Guide, version for SAP HANA
• SAP Business One Administrator's Guide

Distribution Rules

If the Use Multidimensions checkbox is selected in the SAP Business One client (Cost Accounting tab of the
General Settings window), the list view displays a column for each dimension (Dimension 1, Dimension 2,
Dimension 3…). If you have not enabled multidimensions in SAP Business One client, a single field, Distribution

If you have enabled multidimensions in SAP Business One client, the selection in the Display Distribution Rules

documents (including the freight charges) and payments. In the detailed view, distribution rules for multiple
dimensions are displayed in unified or separate columns according to your settings.

The COGS Distr. Rule column is active at the row level.

defined in the COGS XXX columns, where XXX is the description of active dimensions.

For more information about working with cost accounting, see the online help for SAP Business One.

1.2.5  Home Page

The Home page, the first page that you see after logging in to Web client, displays sets of tiles that allow you to
launch apps or content. You can personalize the home page by adding, removing, or grouping apps.

The tiles are bundled into predefined groups listed in the navigation bar at the top of the page (My Home, Sales,
Business Partners, and so on). If you select a group header in the navigation bar, the page scrolls down to the
selected group. The same group headers are displayed in the Main Menu.

To return to the home page after navigating away from the page, click the SAP Business One logo in the header.

1.2.5.1  My Home

My Home is the first group of tiles displayed in the navigation bar on the home page. My Home allows you to
quickly access frequently used apps or content. It includes a number of default tiles, such as Sales Quotations,
Purchase Orders, and Business Partners, depending on your authorizations. You can modify the tiles that are
displayed in My Home and their order to reflect your needs. The personalization that you make to My Home is
retained after performing an upgrade.

The particular tiles that are visible depend on your authorizations. For example, if you have read-only
authorization for sales orders, the Create Sales Order tile will not be displayed. If your authorizations change,
the relevant tiles will be displayed the next time you log in.

38

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

You can personalize the tiles that appear in My Home by dragging to rearrange tiles directly. You can also use
edit mode to rearrange groups and add or remove tiles as needed. For more information about personalizing
the home page, see Edit Home Page [page 50].

1.2.5.2  Main Menu

A menu with a structure similar to the SAP Business One Main Menu appears on the top left of the page. To
open the main menu, choose  Main Menu.

The structure of the menu reflects the predefined grouping of tiles on the home page. Clicking or expanding a
menu item displays a list of objects related to the group; clicking the object name launches the particular app.

The search box at the top of the menu enables you to enter a search term and find the relevant entry in the
menu.

To hide the menu, choose  Main Menu again.

1.2.5.3

Enterprise Search

This function enables you to search for data across all apps and business objects.

 Note

Enterprise search is only supported by the Web client version for SAP HANA.

Searching for Business Objects and Apps

To display the search bar, choose  Search in the top right corner of the page. On larger screens, the search bar
is automatically displayed in the center of the header and the  Search icon appears within the search bar.

Using the dropdown list in the search bar, you can specify the category of object data that you want to search
in. By default, All is displayed in the type selector, meaning that the search runs through the entire database.
To restrict your search to only apps, choose Apps from the dropdown list. To restrict your search by business
object, choose the business object from the dropdown list (for example, Sales Order).

 Note

When you initiate the search from within an app, the search is applied to the given object by default. If
needed, you can change the search scope manually.

Enter your search term and choose  Search or press  ENTER .

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

39

 Tip

You can use operators such as an asterisk (*) to perform a wildcard search and OR to find results that
contain either of two search terms.

Navigating the Results List

The search results are displayed in a list sorted by relevance. Apps are shown as tiles that you can directly
launch. Business objects are displayed as summaries of the object and include the document number as link
that navigates you to the detailed view of the object.

The tabs at the top of the results list allow you to narrow the results list by the search category (business object
or apps). You can see all results on the All tab, and the search category with the greatest number of results on
the next tab. To view the results of searh categories with fewer hits, select an option from the More menu.

 Note

Tabs are only displayed at the top of the results list if you have not narrowed your search to a specific
category and  Show filters is not selected (in other words, the filter panel is hidden).

If you have not narrowed down the results to a specific category but  Show filters is selected, you can
narrow your search in the Search In area of the left panel. For more information about the filter panel, see
Filtering Search Results [page 40].

If the results are limited to a specific business object, several icons appear on the top right of the results list
that allow you to work with the search results:

• Choose  Export results to download your search results (up to 1000 results) as a comma-separated text

file.

• Choose whether you want the results displayed as a list or as a table using  Display as List and  Display

as Table.

• When  Display as Table is selected, you can choose which columns to display and in what order by

choosing  Select Columns.

Filtering Search Results

You can further filter the results by choosing  Show filters on the top left. A panel opens on the left of the
results list that allows you to apply additional criteria to the filter for a specific business object. Once you have
limited the results to a business object, you can:

• Apply additional filters in the Filter By area of the panel. The possible filters that are displayed are specific
to the selected business object. For example, Contact Person, BP Code, BP Name, Status, and so on, are
displayed for marketing objects.

• Choose whether to display the filters as a list (default) ( Filter display switch; display as: List ), or visualize
them as a bar chart ( Filter display switch; display as: Bar Chart ) or pie chart (  Filter display switch;
display as: Pie Chart ).

40

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client

• For each filter, you can click the Show More option; this opens the Filter Settings dialog box, which enables
you to further fine-tune the specific filter. The dialog box shows a list of all available filters on the left and
the details of the selected filter on the right. The available options depend on the data type of the filter. For
instance, the Define Conditions tab allows you to add one or more filter conditions by selecting Equal to,
Begins with, Ends with, or Contains and entering numbers, letters or words, or a combination of both. For
numbers and dates, you can add custom number and date ranges.

 Note

You can also access the Filter Settings dialog box by scrolling down to the bottom of the filter panel and
choosing the Show All Filters button.

If you want to clear all filters that you have selected for the business object, choose  Reset Filters in the upper
right part of the filter panel.

1.2.5.4  Notifications

To view notifications, choose  Notifications in the upper-right corner of the Web client pages. Here you can
view a list of notifications.

You can choose to sort the notifications by date (default) or by importance.

Choose By Date to display the notifications grouped by date. Choose By Importance to display the notifications

according to priority. The notification types marked as high priority in the Notifications tab under  User

Actions Settings  are labelled in red as Important.

Clicking the notification opens the respective record.

Choosing  Close in the upper right corner of the notification dismisses the notification. Dismissing a
notification removes it from the notification list, but the respective record may still need to be processed.

To change notification settings, see Notifications [page 50].

To open SAP Companion, choose   in the upper-right corner of the Web client pages.

SAP Companion is a web-based help system to provide you with context-sensitive in-app help. It enables you to
get started quickly and to find all relevant information easily without needing to leave the Web client.

1.2.5.6  Set Up a Default Branch

If you are assigned to more than one active branch, you can set up a default branch for the current logon.

To set up a default branch:

1. Choose  (Set Up a Default Branch) in the upper-right corner of the Web client pages.

The icon also shows how many branches are assigned to you. If you have not selected a default branch, the
number of branches is displayed in red.

2. The Select Default Branch window displays the active branches to which you are assigned.

3. Select a branch and set it as the default branch.
The default branch is displayed in the header.

 Note

The option to set up a default branch is available if Enable Multiple Branches is enabled under

Administration Configuration General Company Settings .

When a default branch is set, then while creating documents, the branch is prefilled with the default branch
value. You have the option to change the branch.

1.2.5.7.1

Recent Activities & Frequently Used

Web Client maintains a dynamic list of the 30 apps you have most recently used, and the 30 apps you most
frequently use. The lists allow you to find your most used apps or open a recently used app.

To access the lists, choose Recent Activity or Frequently Used in the user actions menu. The Quick Access
dialog box shows the tracking on two tabs. The most recent activities or most frequently displayed apps are
displayed first in the list. You can navigate directly to any of these apps by clicking the entry.

 Note

You can stop tracking your user activity or clear the history at any time in the Settings dialog box.

1.2.5.7.2

App Finder

Context

The app finder is a convenient tool for finding apps and adding new apps to your home page. You can also
remove apps you do not need from your home page and launch less-frequently used apps directly.

To access the app finder, choose App Finder in the user actions menu. The app finder lists all the apps that
you may need in your daily work that are available for your user authorization. The app boxes with the  Edit
assignment icon are already added to at least one group on your home page. The  Add tile icon indicates that
the app has not been added to a group.

Apps are organized according to the grouping in the navigation bar and Main Menu.

• To browse all the apps, in the left side panel, choose All.
• To view apps by group, in the left side panel, choose the group name (for example, Sales).

You can also search for an app by manually entering the title or a keyword in the search box.

Adding Apps to the Home Page in the App Finder

Procedure

1. Choose App Finder in the user actions menu.

2. Find the app that you want to add to your home page using the groups listed in the left side panel or using

the search option.

3. Choose  Edit assignmentor  Add tile below the app.

 Note

The  Edit assignment icon is shown when the app is already assigned to a group. The  Add tile icon is
shown when the app has not yet been assigned to a group.

4. To add the app to one or more groups, in the Add to Group popover, select the checkboxes for the groups to

which you want to add the app.

 Tip

You can also remove an app from a group by deselecting the checkbox in the popover.

To move an app to another group, select the checkbox for the desired group and deselect the selected
one.

 Note

You can also add apps directly from the home page by choosing Edit Home Page in the user actions
menu. For more information, see Edit Home Page [page 50].

Creating New Groups for Apps in the App Finder

Procedure

1. Choose App Finder in the user actions menu.

2. Choose  Edit assignment below the app for which you want to create a new group.

3. At the top of the Add to Group popover, choose the New Group option.

4. Enter a group name and choose OK.

Results

On the home page, the new group is added as the last group in the navigation bar. The app is displayed as a tile
in the relevant group.

1.2.5.7.3.1  Appearance

Use the Appearance tab of the Settings dialog box to change your theme, display settings, and predictive text
settings.

Theme Tab

On this tab, you can set the visual theme for the user interface. Choose between the default Belize Deep
(dark theme), Belize (light theme), or Belize High Contrast Black (high-contrast theme). For a fresh, modern
theme with round corners, you can choose Morning Horizon (light theme), Evening Horizon (dark theme), or the
Horizon theme in high-contrast black or white styles.

Display Settings Tab

When using a hybrid device that combines touch and mouse events, you can enable the Optimized for Touch
Input option, which increases the size and spacing of controls to better enable fingertip interaction.

By default, SAP Business One Suggest is enabled in Web client. When this option is on, Web client gives
suggestions as you type in fields that have an option list, such as codes, names, and descriptions. If you
primarily use the keyboard to enter values for option list fields, you can switch off this option to optimize for
faster data entry.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

47

1.2.5.7.3.2  Home Page

On the Home Page tab of the Settings dialog box, you can decide how content is displayed on the home page.
The selected option also affects the navigation within detailed view pages.

Choose from one of the following options:

• Show all content (default) – all content is displayed on a single page with an anchor bar at the top. On the
home page, tiles belonging to all groups are shown and the group names in the navigation bar serve as
anchors that scroll you down to the selected group. In detailed view, the whole record is displayed so you
can scroll the page or use the tabs as anchors to the desired section.

• Show one group at a time – the content of single groups is shown and is accessed using a tab bar. On the
home page, each group of tiles is shown separately, and the group names serve as tabs. In detailed view,
only the content of the header and current tab are displayed; you can access the content of other tabs by
choosing the tab name.

1.2.5.7.3.3  User Activities

Web client automatically tracks recent activity and frequently used apps based on your activity. For more
information, see Recent Activities & Frequently Used [page 44].

The User Activities tab of the Settings dialog box allows you to turn off this function. If tracking is switched off,
the Recent Activity and Frequently Used options are not displayed in the user actions menu.

You can also clear your usage history in Web client by choosing the Clear my history button to empty these lists.

1.2.5.7.3.4  Language & Region

On the Language & Region tab of the Settings dialog box, you can view and change the display language of Web
client. By default, the display language of Web client is identical to the display language in SAP Business One.
Choosing a different language in Web client affects the display language in SAP Business One and vice versa.

The date format and time format displayed in Web client are taken from SAP Business One. If you modify
the time or date format in SAP Business One, the date or time format in Web client is changed accordingly.
However, you cannot change the date and time format directly in Web client.

1.2.5.7.3.5  General Settings

The General Settings tab of the Settings dialog box allows you to maintain the following settings:

Display
Quick View

Content
Security
Policy

By default, when you click a golden arrow ( ) in front of an object in list view or detailed view,
a quick view containing a concise overview of the object details is displayed. The Display Quick
View option allows you to turn on or off the display of quick views.

Enables you to configure the Content Security Policy (CSP) settings. A default CSP header is
used. Superusers can override the default value to set a different response header in the field.

If you work with tile links and extensions in the Web client, you must first add your extension links
in the CSP setting, otherwise the extensibility will be blocked. For more information about how
to configure CSP settings and troubleshooting for your extensions, see the guide How to Develop
Web Client Extensions.

 Note

For users with no authorizations, this field is not displayed.

1.2.5.7.3.6  Message Preferences

While performing a specific business process, you can choose to avoid certain system messages, such as
warning and information messages, from being displayed in the future by selecting the checkbox Remember
my answer and do not show this message again. If you select this checkbox, the message will not be displayed
again in the same situation, and your saved answer will be automatically performed. As a result, the message
and your chosen response are listed in the Message Preferences form.

The Message Preferences tab of the Settings dialog box allows you to manage the display and response options
of messages for which you have selected the checkbox Remember my answer and do not show this message
again. In the Message Preference tabel area, messages are categorized according to functional area and app
name. The Display field shows whether the message is currently displayed or not. To modify the display setting
for a message, use the Yes/No switch in the Display field. The Answer field displays the saved answer to the
system message. You can modify the saved answer by using the dropdown in the Answer field. If the Display
field is set to Yes, the Answer field shows the default option.

If you modify the message display settings in Web client, the settings will be applied to the corresponding
messages in SAP Business One client, and vice versa.

 Example

You perform an action in Web client that triggers a warning message. You select the checkbox Remember
my answer and do not show this message again and then choose the Yes button to answer the system
message. As a result, the message is displayed in Message Preferences in both Web client and SAP
Business One client. In Web client, the switch in the Display field is set to No and the Answer field is
set to Yes. Later, you want to continue hiding the message but want the answer to be set to No. In Message
Preferences, you change the value in the Answer field for the particular message to No.

1.2.5.7.3.7  Notifications

On the Notifications tab of the Settings dialog box, you can set your preferences for notifications:

• Define the number of days for which notifications are displayed in the Show Notifications for Last Number

of Days field (the default is 30 days).

• Select the Show High-Priority Notification Alerts checkbox if you want to show high-priority notification

alerts from the notification panel.

You can set your preferences for the following notification types:

• Activity reminders
• Recurring transactions execution
• Daily exchange rate entry
• Approval decisions
• Approval requests
• Service call assignments
• Blanket agreement renewal reminders
• Wizard tasks

 Note

The list of available notification types may vary according to user authorizations. For example, if the user
has no authorization for service calls, the notification type Service Call Assignments is not available.

You can choose whether to display alerts for a notification type from the notification panel in the upper-right
corner of the Web client pages. You can set notification types as high priority. If the Show High-Priority
Notification Alerts checkbox is also selected, the notification type is labelled as Important on display from the
notification panel.

For more information about notifications, see Notifications [page 41].

1.2.5.7.4

Edit Home Page

This function allows you to customize the home page by controlling the visibility and location of apps and
groups.

To make changes to the home page, such as moving groups and removing tiles, you need to switch to edit
mode. To switch to edit mode, choose  Edit Home Page in the user actions menu.

In edit mode, you can perform the following:

Creating New Groups

To create a new group, choose the Add Group button that is displayed between groups.

50

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Adding Tiles to Groups

To add more tiles to a group, choose  Open App Finder on an empty tile in a group to launch the app finder.
For more information about the app finder, see App Finder [page 44].

Editing Groups

• To hide a group, on the top-right side of the relevant group, choose the Hide button. You can choose to

display the group again later by choosing the Show button.

• To reset a predefined group to its original state, on the top-right side of the relevant group, choose the

Reset button.

• To rename a custom group or predefined group, click the group name and modify the text in the text box.

 Note

If you rename a predefined group, the original predefined group remains visible, but the tiles belonging
to the predefined group appear under the new group. To reset the predefined group, choose the Reset
button displayed in the original predefined group.

• To delete a custom (non-predefined) group, on the top-right side of the relevant group, choose the Delete

button.

Moving and Removing Tiles

• To move a tile to a different group, click   in the lower-right corner of a tile, and then choose Move.

Alternatively, you can drag tiles on the home page to place them in the desired location.

 Tip

You can drag and drop tile and links without switching to edit mode.

• To remove a tile, choose  Remove in the upper-right corner of a tile.

Once you have completed your editing, exit edit mode by clicking Close at the bottom of the page or choosing
Exit Edit Mode in the user actions menu.

 Note

After adding new extensions or upgrading SAP Business One, new extensions and apps are displayed as
the last tile in the respective group even if you have customized your home page.

External Apps

Clicking a tile that represents a web site or a document opens the respective asset. The following tiles are

1.2.6.2  Apps for Managing Records

Apps for managing records are named according to the business object, such as Sales Orders and Items, as
well as user-defined objects.

The tiles for managing marketing documents display useful app content such as the number of open records
in the app for the current user and when the app was last updated. Next to the  Refresh icon, you can see
the last time this KPI was refreshed. Choosing the  Refresh icon on the bottom-left of the tile updates the app
content displayed on the tile.

1.2.6.2.1  Working with List Views

When you click a tile of an app for managing records, it displays a list view of the existing records of the app's
business object. To view the details of a specific record, click  Details on the row of the relevant record (or
anywhere on the record's row).

The list view is divided into the following main areas:

Header
area

Content
area

• Views

Views determine the type of content displayed in the table area. Each view consists of saved
filter bar values and View Settings values set in the table toolbar.

• Filter Bar

The filter bar allows you to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area.

• Table Toolbar

The table toolbar includes: table action buttons (to perform operations), the  View Settings
icon (which allows you to select columns, sort the data, apply additional filters, and group
the data in the table area), the  Export to Microsoft Excel icon, and table/chart/card view
selectors.
• Table Area

The table area displays the records of the business object according to the settings in the
header area (view and filter bar) and in the View Settings dialog. The data is listed as a table,
or visualized as chart or card, depending on the view selected in the table toolbar.
If the records filtered in a list view or choose from list exceed the threshold maximum of 5000
records, the Select All checkbox is not available. You can still select individual records or a
range of records. A Deselect All control lets you clear all selections. If the total number of
records is less than or equal to 5000, the Select All checkbox is available. It operates as usual,
allowing both selection and deselection of all records.

1.2.6.2.1.1  Header Area

The header area at the top of list view screens contains the following components:

• Views [page 54]
• Filter Bar [page 54]
• Header Tools [page 65]

1.2.6.2.1.1.1  Views

The views menu is displayed in the top-left corner of the header area above the filter bar. Views display records
in the table area according to the filter bar setting in the header and table parameters set in View Settings.
Clicking the dropdown arrow opens the list of available views for the business object.

Each business object has a number of predefined views (for example, My Open Sales Orders, All Sales Orders,
My Sales Orders). You can change the default view that is displayed when you open the list view by choosing
the dropdown arrow next to the view title and clicking Manage. In the Manage Views dialog, select the view
you would like to set as the new default view. You can also set the view as public or private. Public views are
available to all users who have access to the app.

 Note

Predefined views provided by SAP cannot be changed or removed.

If you change the parameters for the current view (for example, by adding filters or grouping), the view is
marked with an asterisk (*) to indicate that there are unsaved changes to the view. To save the view, in the My
Views dialog, choose Save As. In the Save View dialog, specify a name for the view and set the view as default or
public, if desired.

You can save the currently selected view as a tile by clicking Save as Tile in the Share menu. For more
information, see Header Tools [page 65].

 Note

The data displayed in views depends on user authorizations and data ownership rules. For example, if you
do not have authorization for BP Balance, the Account Balance column is not displayed when you open the
Customers view in the business partners list view. Or, when working with sales orders, in the Open Sales
Orders view, you can only see the open sales orders related to those customers for which you have data
ownership.

1.2.6.2.1.1.2  Filter Bar

The filter bar consists of horizontal filter fields in the header area. These filters allow you to control which
records appear in the table area.

54

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Basic Search

You can enter a keyword to filter the data currently displayed in the table.

Filter
Fields

You can use the filter fields manually or with the help of a filter dialog box.

If you want to retain your customized filter settings, see Views [page 54].

• Manual Entry

In the relevant filter field, manually enter one or more valid values.
When entering multiple values in a filter field, you can use the following syntax:
• To enter a few specific values, such as multiple customer codes in the Customer Code filter
field, type the first value, press the  Enter  key, and repeat for the next customer codes.
For example, to filter by customer codes C20000, C30000, and C40000, type C20000 and
press  ENTER , type C30000 and press  ENTER , type C40000 and press  ENTER .
• To enter a range of values, type the first and last values separated by two dots. For

example, if you want to specify a range of BP codes from C20000 to C40000, enter
C20000...C40000.

• To enter a range of values that are smaller/greater or earlier/later than a certain value, use
the < and > signs. For example, to set a range of dates later than September 1, 2021, type
>09012021.

• When setting filter dates and date ranges, you can manually enter date offset formulations.
A date offset is a formula that adds or subtracts periods from the current system date to
calculate the filter date. If a saved view contains filters with a date offset, the filter is valid
every time the view is opened. Some basic examples of date offset formulas are as follows:
• Month: Begin: The first day of the current month.
• Quarter 3: Begin: The first day of quarter 3 of the current year.
• Year: End: The last day of the current year.
• +12 Day: 12 days from today’s date.
For more information, see Manually Entering Date Offset Formulas [page 57].

• Filter Dialog

Choose the   icon in a field to open its filter dialog box, where you can apply a filtering
condition to the field's values.
• For text type fields, in the dropdown field to the right of the field name, choose a condition

such as Equal to, In range, Less than, or Greater than, then specify the value in the next field.
Example:
To filter the data for open opportunities with a potential amount (LC) greater than 2,500.00
$, in the Potential Amount (LC) dialog, choose Greater than from the dropdown list, then
enter 2500.00 in the value field.

• For date type fields, the condition is set to Equal to. Choose   in the next field, and in the

Time Period popover, select a value such as Today, Last X days, This quarter, Next X years, or
Last X posting periods. If your selection includes a value (“X”) or you selected Date Range,
specify a positive integer or date range in the next field.
Example:
To filter the data for deliveries within the last 3 months, in the Delivery Date dialog, choose
  in the field next to Equal to, select Last X months in the Time Period field, and enter 3
in the Month field. The result is displayed in the filter field (in this example, 3 Month…Today
(6/8/2021…9/8/2021)).
For more information, see Using the Filter Dialog to Enter Date Offset Formulas [page 63].

You can define additional conditions for the field by choosing  Add .

Adapt
Filters

The default filters displayed in the filter bar are a subset of the fields that can be used as filter fields
for the current object. The Adapt Filters dialog allows you to personalize the filter bar. You can do the
following:

• Add new filters and hide filters that you rarely use.
• Specify single or multiple values or define conditions for any of the fields.

Choosing the Adapt Filters button on the bottom right of the header opens the Adapt Filters dialog
box, which lists all fields that can be used as filter fields for the current object.

• To search for a particular field, type the field name in the search bar at the top of the dialog.
• To add or remove filter fields, select or deselect the checkbox in the Show on Filter Bar column

to the right of the particular field.
Example:
To display a specific year and quarter of a date type field, you can select the checkbox for its
aggregated field: <Date field> (Year and Quarter).

• To specify values for a field or apply conditions on a field, choose   in the field to open a filter

dialog.

 Note

You can set filters for a specific field without displaying the field in the filter bar.

To apply your settings, choose Go.

1.2.6.2.1.1.2.1  Working with Date Offset Filtering

A date offset is a formula that adds or subtracts periods from the current system date to calculate the filter
date. You also can specify offset date ranges by including a prefix for the From date and a suffix for the To date
(for example, to start 1 month before the current system date and end 3 months after the current system date).
If a saved view contains filters with a date offset, the filter result is updated with respect to the current system
date every time the view is opened.

When setting filters for date type fields, you can specify date offset formulations either manually in the filter
field or with the help of the filter dialog.

1.2.6.2.1.1.2.1.1  Manually Entering Date Offset Formulas

The basic formula parameters that can be manually entered in a date offset formula are as follows:

• Current Date

Today

The current system date.

• Day

<+/-> <X> Day

A positive (non-zero) integer (“X”) representing the number of days.

 Note

This phrase must have the prefix “+/- integer” to indicate whether the result is to go forward or
backward by the specified number of days.

 Example

+12 Day

12 days from today’s date.

• Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday…

The name of a specific day of the week, such as “Monday”, “Tuesday”, “Wednesday”, “Thursday”. You can
also use the 3-letter abbreviation ("Sun", "Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat").
<+/-> <Name of the Day of the Week>

 Note

This phrase must have the prefix “+” or “-” to indicate whether the result is to go forward or backward
to the specified day of the week.

 Example

+Tuesday

The next Tuesday.

• Week

A positive (non-zero) integer (“X”) representing the week.

 Note

If this phrase does not have a prefix, it must specify the specific week (“Week X”) or have a suffix
parameter.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

57

Week <X>

The same day of the week in a specified week.

 Example

Week 38

The same day of the week in week 38.

Week:Begin

The first day of the week.

 Example

Week:Begin

The first day of the current week.

Week:End

The last day of the week.

 Example

Week:End

The last day of the current week.

<+/-> <X> Week

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
weeks.

 Example

+12 Week

The same day of the week in week 12.

<+/-><X> Week:Begin

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
weeks, and then to the beginning of that week.

 Example

-1 Week:Begin

Backward 1 week to the beginning that week. For instance, if the current system date is December 15,
2018 and the week begins on a Monday, the filter result is December 3, 2018.

<+/-> <X> Week:End

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
weeks, and then to the end of that week.

 Example

+2 Week:End

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Forward 2 weeks and then to the end of that week. For instance, if the current system date is December
15, 2018 and the week begins on a Monday, the filter result is December 30, 2018.

• Month

A positive (non-zero) integer representing months.

 Note

If this phrase has no prefix, it must specify the specific month (“Month X”) or have a suffix parameter.

Month <X>

The same day in a specific month.

 Example

Month:End

The last day of the current month.

Month:Begin

The first day of the month.

 Example

The first day of the current month.

Month:End

The last day of the month.

 Example

Month:End

The last day of the current month.

<+/-> <X> Month

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
months.

 Example

+1 Month

The same day of the month in the next month.

<+/-> <X> Month:Begin

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
months, and then to the beginning of that month.

 Example

- 1 Month:Begin

Back 1 month to the beginning of that month. For example, if the current system date is December 15,
2018, the filter result is November 1, 2018.

<+/-> <X> Month:End

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
months, and then to the end of that month.

 Example

+2 Month:End

Forward 2 months and to the end of that month. For instance, if the current system date is December
15, 2018, the filter result is February 28, 2019.

• January, February, March …

The name of a specific month, such as “January”, “February”, “March”, “April”. You can also use the 3-letter
abbreviation ("Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec").
<+/-> <Name of the Month>

 Note

This phrase must have the prefix “+” or “-” to indicate whether the result is to go forward or backward
to the specified month.

 Example

+ October

From the current day of the month to the same day of the month next October.

<+/-> <Name of the Month> :<Suffix>

The suffix parameter “:Begin” or “:End” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward to the
specified month, and then to the beginning or end of the month.

 Example

+ October:End

From the current day of the month to the next October 31.

• Quarter

This phrase must have the suffix “:Begin” or “:End” to indicate whether the result is to go to the beginning
or end of the quarter.
Quarter:Begin

The first day of the quarter.

 Example

Quarter:Begin

The first day of the current quarter. If the current system date is December 15, 2018, the filter result is
October 1, 2018.

Quarter:End

The last day of the quarter.

 Example

Quarter:End

The last day of the current quarter. If the current system date is December 15, 2018, the filter result is
December 31, 2018.

<+/-> <X> Quarter:<Suffix>

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of
quarters.

 Note

If this is the first phrase in the formula, it must have a prefix.

 Example

-1 Quarter:End

Backward 1 quarter to the end of that quarter. For instance, the current system date is December 15,
2018, the filter result is September 30, 2018.

• Year

The calendar year.

 Note

If this phrase does not have a prefix, it must either have a suffix parameter or specify the specific year
(“Year X”).

<Year> <X>

The current day of the month and current month in a specific year.

 Example

Year 2018

The current day and month in the year 2018.

Year:Begin

The first day of the year.

 Example

Year:Begin

The first day of the current year.

Year:End

The last day of the year.

 Example

Year:End

The last day of the current year.

<+/-> <X> <Year>

The prefix “+/- integer” indicates whether the result is to go forward or backward by a specified number of

You can use the filter dialog to easily set a number of limited date offset formulas. In the filter dialog for date

After selecting this option, you can either enter the From and To date manually or use the date range picker.
The resulting formula is MM/DD/YYYY… MM/DD/YYYY.

 Note

The date format depends on your date format definition in SAP Business One client.

1.2.6.2.1.1.3  Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of list view screens provides you with various options for sharing
content.

Send by
Email

More
Email
Options

To share the URL of a list view with a colleague, from the Share menu, choose Send by Email. The
Send by Email option is available in all list views, including user-defined objects and tables, and
analytics views. The body of the email draft contains a link with the URL of the displayed view, and
the subject line indicates the object and view names. Only recipients with relevant authorizations
can access the data.

If Microsoft 365 integration is not set up, the Web client will use the default email app of your
operating system instead.

There are five options available in the Email Options window based on different conditions:

• Draft Email with Microsoft Excel Attachment: available for table view and chart view. Select this
option to draft an email with a Microsoft Excel attachment of all the records. Microsoft 365
integration must be set up.
This option only appears for users who have authorizations for MS-Excel under General

in the Authorizations window in the SAP Business One client ( Administration System

Initialization Authorizations General Authorizations ).

• Draft Email with Hyperlink in Email Body: available for table view, chart view, and card view.
Select this option to draft an email with the URL in the email body pointing to the list of
records. This is the same as the Send by Email option mentioned above.
If Microsoft 365 integration is not set up, Web client will use the default email app of your
operating system instead.

• Draft Email with PDF Attachment: select this option to draft an email with a PDF attachment of

your selected records. Microsoft 365 integration must be set up.

• Draft Multiple Emails with PDF Attachments: select this option to draft multiple emails, each of
which contains one PDF attachment for each of your selected records. The maximum number
of records that the system can process is 20. Microsoft 365 integration must be set up.
After you send the emails for marketing documents, you can check the corresponding email
log in the E-mails Sent window for the documents in the SAP Business One client.
For the Web browser to open multiple email draft pages successfully, add the Web Client
root URL to be allowed to send pop-ups and use redirects. Please make sure that the root
URL includes only one server address and one port number (if there is a port number). For

example, in Google Chrome, follow the path  Settings Privacy and security Site Settings

Pop-ups and redirects Allowed to send pop-ups and use redirects Add .

• Send Multiple Emails with PDF Attachments Directly to Document Emails: select this option
to have multiple emails sent out directly to the document email addresses, with each email
containing one PDF attachment for each of your selected records. The maximum number of
records that the system can process is 20. Microsoft 365 integration must be set up.
Once you select this option and choose OK, emails with the selected documents are
submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending. To check the results, log in to your Microsoft 365

1.2.6.2.1.2.2  Table View

Table view ( ) displays a list of records for the business object. On the left side of the table toolbar above
the table, a record counter displays the number of records selected and the total number of records for the
business object.

The data in table view is displayed according to the filters set in the filter bar and the table parameters set in
View Settings.

Table view allows you to:

• Easily view and act on a large number of records or search for a subset of records.
• Perform actions on records by selecting the checkbox next to one or more records. For more information

on the action buttons in the table toolbar, see Table Toolbar [page 68].

• Display a quick view of an object by clicking the golden navigation arrow ( ) next to an object in a row. The

popover contains a concise overview of the object.

• View a record's details by clicking the row or using the navigation arrow  Details at the end of the row.

You can personalize the table view by setting additional sorting and grouping options on column headers.

1.2.6.2.1.2.3  Chart View

Chart view ( ) visualizes the data in list view as charts. As in table view, you can filter data by using the filter
bar in the header. To apply your changes, choose the Go button.

There are three dropdown fields in the upper-left corner of the chart area. You can use them to customize your
chart attributes based on fields from the list view.

The first dropdown groups all measurable numeric fields, which contain quantitative values, such as Document
Total.

The remaining two dropdowns to the right group dimensional non-numeric fields, which contain qualitative
values, such as Customer Name and Posting Date.

In the All Sales Invoices list view, you group your invoices by Customer Name using the  View Settings

The line chart displays the total number of all sales invoices for each customer, with Record Count
selected automatically as the measure on the vertical axis, and Customer Name as the dimension on
the horizontal axis.

• Line Chart: Comparison of Invoice Values and Gross Profit

Profit Total. Keep the first and only dimension Customer Name as is.

1.2.6.2.1.2.5  Viewing Selected Chart Data in List View

When you select specific data points in a chart, you can use the button Open in List View at the bottom of the
Details popover to view a breakdown of the selected data in a list view in a new browser tab. This function is
available for the following charts

• All charts in the chart views of list views
• Charts within the card view cards of list views
• Charts within General Overview cards with data sourced from list views

This function is also available when you create or edit these cards.

This function is unavailable for SAP HANA-specific overview views and charts in the Analytics group, as well as
any other views or charts created from SAP HANA calculation views in any app across all groups.

This feature empowers you to utilize list views for comprehensive drilldown into pre-filtered data, providing
deeper insights and enhanced analysis.

In the topics below, we will show you how to utilize this function, as well as the guidelines for effective data
selections.

Selecting Chart Data and Opening in List View [page 77]

popover to view the breakdown of selected chart data in a new list view.

dimensions.

1.2.6.2.1.2.5.1  Selecting Chart Data and Opening in List View

In this topic, we provide an example to show you how to use the button Open in List View in the Details popover
to view the breakdown of selected chart data in a new list view.

Context

In a line chart, you want to view the breakdown of the Gross Profit Total of all the sales orders for a specific
posting year in a new list view after selecting a data point for the year from the line chart.

Procedure

1.

In the Sales Orders list view, choose the All Sales Orders view.

2. Choose the   icon in the table toolbar and go to the default line chart in the chart view.

3.

In the line chart, choose Gross Profit Total for the measure on the vertical axis and Posting Date (Year) for
the first and only dimension on the horizontal axis.

A blue line appears in the chart, displaying the gross profit total amount by posting year. Each data point in
the chart has a Gross Profit Total value in the Posting Date (Year) dimension.

4. Choose the data point for a specific year, for example, year 2024.

5. Choose Details in the upper right corner of the chart to open a popover.

In the popover, the values of both the year and the gross profit total are displayed, for example, the gross
profit total is 620,000 for the year 2024. The gross profit total is the sum of the subtotal from 2,000 sales
orders, which can be manually filtered from the table view.

6.

In the popover, choose Open in List View at the bottom.

Results

A list view opens in a new browser tab, showing a breakdown of the contribution of 2,000 sales orders to the
gross profit total of 620,000. Each sales order was posted in the year of 2024.

If you choose the  View Settings icon in the table toolbar and choose to display the Gross Profit Total column
in the table, you can see the total amount of 620,000 at the bottom of the table.

If you choose Adapt Filters in the list view header area to display the Posting Date (Year) filter field, you'll see the
text =2024 in the filter field, with the year 2024 being automatically applied as a filter condition.

If you want to view a breakdown of data across multiple years, you can select multiple data points in Step 4 and
then choose Open in List View.

1.2.6.2.1.2.5.2  Guidelines for Data Selections in Charts

In this topic, we provide clear examples of both valid and invalid data selections for charts with two dimensions.

Charts with One Dimension

If your chart has only one dimension, the result will be displayed properly in a list view, regardless of how you
select data points or the number of measures selected.

This rule applies to all types of charts: line charts, column charts, bar charts, stacked column charts, stacked
bar charts, pie charts, donut charts, and heat map charts.

Charts with Two Dimensions

If your chart has two dimensions, the result in the list view may not match your expectations based on how you
select the data points, regardless of the number of measures selected.

As a general rule, due to the filtering mechanism of the list view, you need to ensure the selected data points
meet either one of the following conditions in order to get the expected result:

1. All available values of one dimension have been selected for the values selected in the other dimension.

2. All selected values in one dimension have been paired with all selected values in the other dimension.

This applies to line charts, column charts, bar charts, stacked column charts, stacked bar charts, and heat map
charts.

Let’s take the stacked column chart as an example to explain how to apply the above two guidelines to make
valid data point selections.

Example Scenario

In the All Sales Orders view of the Sales Orders list view, you want to show the gross profit total of each
customer by posting year in the stacked column chart of the chart view. You select Gross Profit Total for the
measure on the vertical axis, Posting Date (Year) for the first dimension on the horizontal axis, and Customer
Name for the second dimension on the vertical axis.

78

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

In the resulting chart as below, each rectangular shaped data point has a Gross Profit Total value in the
Customer Name dimension and in the Posting Date (Year) dimension. You can view the details of the data
points and compare the gross profit total of all color-coded customers across four consecutive years.

Application of Guideline 1

In the examples below, we will illustrate how to apply guideline 1: “All available values of one dimension have
been selected for the values selected in the other dimension.”

Examples of Valid Data Selection

You can choose one or more year labels in the horizontal dimension to select all the data points available in
the Customer Name dimension for these years. The breakdown of the Gross Profit Total values of the selected
customers and posting years can be properly displayed in the list view.

As highlighted in the screenshot below, if you select all the 24 data points available for the posting years of

Examples of Valid Data Selection

all values selected in the Customer Name dimension are paired with all the values selected in the Posting Date

customer names are also automatically applied as filters in the Customer Name filter field.

1.2.6.2.2  Working with Detailed Views

From the list view of an app for managing records, you can navigate to a detailed view of a specific record by
clicking  Details on the row of the relevant record or clicking anywhere on the row.

By default, when you open an existing record, it appears in view mode.

The detailed view is divided into the following main areas:

Header area

• Displays key information about the business record
• Allows you to switch to edit or create mode
• Allows you to perform business actions using the header toolbar

Record
Body

• Displays the record content structured in a series of navigation tabs
• When in edit mode or create mode, the layout of the content area remains the same, but you

can modify an existing record or create a new one from scratch.

After navigating to the detailed view of a business record, you can choose the Edit button to edit the record.

 Note

If you encounter information that cannot be edited in Web client, please edit it in the SAP Business One
client.

In edit mode, the editable fields in each section are outlined with frames for entering or updating the values.
In addition to fields with manual entry or dropdown lists, more complex fields contain one of the following
elements:

• If a value help icon   is displayed in the field, choose the icon to open a dialog box with a list of related

values.

• In fields with object data (for example, Currencies, Languages, Customer Groups), a Define New option is
displayed in the dropdown list as the last value. Choosing Define New displays a definition screen for that
field in which you can define and maintain entries for the object.

 Note

Only users with full authorization for the given object can maintain the object data by selecting the
Define New option.

• For fields with inline table data, an empty row is displayed at the bottom of the table for adding a new entry.

You can also select one of the following options above the table:

 Note

If a   icon exists next to the table field name, you can select a different option from the dropdown list.
The table data is populated with the relevant fields.

Close

Closes the selected open item rows.

Duplicate Duplicates the selected row. The duplicated rows are added after the last row of the table.

Copy,
Paste

Copies selected rows and allows you to paste them in the current record or a different record.
You can also copy and paste to and from Microsoft Excel.

After choosing the Copy button, press  Ctrl+V  to paste the copied data.

Add Row Above,
Row Below

Adds an empty row either above or below the existing selected row. If you select more
than one row, the new row is added above the first row selected or below the last row
selected.

Move Up, Move Down

Moves the selected rows up or down one row.

Delete

Deletes the selected rows from the table.

Settings Opens a dialog box that allows you to personalize the display of the columns in the table. To

show or hide columns, select or deselect the checkboxes of the respective columns. To display

1.2.7  Relationship Map

The relationship map is supported in all localizations according to the respective supported documents.

This feature displays as a flow chart that provides a comprehensive view of the connections between business
objects and their relevant documents (base, target, and reference).

 Example

Displaying the relationship map of a delivery object would illustrate the relationship between the delivery
and its base sales order document and possibly its target documents.

• Choose Relationship Map from the actions bar of a business object to open the dialog with the relationship

map in process flow view.

• All base, target, and reference documents are presented, with their status and other relevant information.
• To see the base documents of a specific business object in a label, choose   located on the connection
line itself. In the pop-up label the base documents details appear, such as document type, document
number, BP code, and document status.

• To show or hide the document references, packages in a packing slip, or pick lists of the main object,

choose Document Referenced To, Document Referenced By, Related Packing Slip, or Related Pick Lists.

Related Information

Relationship Map Settings [page 706]

90

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

1.2.7.1

Layout Structure

The process flow has a layout structure; the default layout contains fixed sections that are filled with content.

Toolbar To show or hide the document references of the main object, choose Document Referenced To or

Document Referenced By.

To show or hide the pick lists or packing slip of the main object, choose Related Pick Lists or Related
Packing Slip.

To zoom in or out the relationship map, choose  Zoom In or  Zoom Out.

To enter the full screen mode, choose  Full Screen .

Header Appears below the bar, consists of multiple steps or categories, each of which is visualized by a

circled icon. Each icon is surrounded by a circular chart to indicate the distribution of statuses per
column.

Categories with no document do not appear in the flow header

Flow map Lies beneath the header. The elements belonging to a certain step are vertically aligned beneath

one another. Arrows point to the next (follow-up) element or multiple elements.

Element

Each element represents a different section:

• Header (mandatory):

• Document description and number, for example: Sales Order 14
• Business partner code and name, for example: (C20000 - ABC)

• Status: indicates by color and icon the state of the document, enabling you to decide how and when to deal

with a particular document:
• Green: Canceled or closed document (nothing to do)
• Natural: Open document which is not due yet (any decision can wait)

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

91

• Yellow: Open document which is due in several days (timely reminder)

 Note

The number of days for this reminder is determined under  Administration Configuration

General Relationship Map Settings . For more information, see Relationship Map Settings [page

706].

• Red: Open document that has passed its due date (deal with this first!)

Display

Specific colors identify objects in the process flow as follows:

• Main document: dark blue
• All documents in the flow: gray
• Document references, packages, and pick lists: light blue, if they exist

Authorization

Access to object details from within the process flow adheres to regular authorization rules.

 Example

If you have authorization for the Sales Order object but not for the Delivery object, when you choose
Relationship Map, you can see only the sales order details but not the details of the delivery document
based on that sales order.

• A message on the object states, “You are not authorized to view Deliveries.”

• If you nevertheless try to open the document, the same message appears as an alert. Choose OK to

return to the flow view.

1.2.7.1.1

Zoom

The process flow reacts to the size of the container into which it is put; detailed information is added or
removed depending on the zoom level. Using the mouse wheel or choosing  Zoom In or  Zoom Out from the
toolbar, you can zoom in or out to affect the amount of information displayed in the container.

Zoom levels:

• Level 1: (largest) Larger elements provide the most space for textual information, however, fewer elements

fit on the screen.

• Level 2: Standard size; provides the best combination of content information and overview.

• Level 3: Elements are reduced to header and status information to provide a better overview for large flows.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

93

• Level 4: The smallest zoom level; provides a maximum overview of the flow while the information about

each element is reduced to a status icon.

1.3.1  Managing Opportunities

To open the Manage Opportunities list view, choose the Opportunities tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for opportunities, see Working with Opportunities [page 97].

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client

Selecting Views

The Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of opportunity records. The views
store filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Opportunities displays a list of open sales and purchasing opportunities of the user who is

currently logged in.
This view is displayed by default.

• All Open Opportunities displays all opportunities with the status of Open.
• All Opportunities displays all sales and purchasing opportunities of the company.
• My Opportunities displays only the opportunities of the user who is logged in.

By default, the opportunities in the table of each predefined view are displayed by Opportunity Number in
descending order. You can change the display order by choosing the respective column header.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

Won or Lost.

1.3.2.1

Creating Opportunities

Context

You can create a sales opportunity for a customer or sales lead, or create a purchasing opportunity for a
vendor.

Procedure

1. Enter the Opportunity page in one of the following ways:

• In the Manage Opportunities app, choose Create.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu CRM Create Opportunity .
• On the Home page, choose the Create Opportunity tile in the CRM group.

2. Select the Opportunity Type.

• To create an opportunity for a customer or sales lead, choose Sales.
• To create an opportunity for a vendor, choose Purchasing.

3. Specify the Customer / Lead or Vendor.

You can enter a business partner code directly in the Customer / Lead or Vendor field. The Web client
automatically suggests the best match.

You can also search for and find a business partner by choosing the  Value Help icon to open the Business
Partners dialogue.

Once a business partner is selected, all other relevant information will be filled in automatically.

4. Enter a descriptive name in the Opportunity Name field.

Fill in the other fields with the related information.

5. Go to the Potential tab, enter the total amount expected for this opportunity in the Potential Amount field,

for example, 100.

The Weighted Amount and the currency are filled in automatically.

The Weighted Amount equals the Potential Amount multiplied by the closing percentage of the last stage.

6.

If you are creating a sales opportunity, enter the expected profit from the final sale in the Gross Profit %
field.

When the Gross Profit % is entered, the Gross Profit Total is calculated automatically, and vice versa.

Gross Profit is calculated from the last linked sales document.

 Note

Gross Profit % and Gross Profit Total are editable and only visible to authorized users.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

101

7. Specify the time span, in number of days, weeks, or months, until the expected close of the opportunity

through the Predicted Closing In field.

Fill in the other fields with the related information.

8. Go to the Stages tab and fill in the information for the first stage.

• To add a new stage for the opportunity, for example, the first meeting, choose Next Stage.
• To duplicate or delete the last stage, choose Duplicate Last Stage or Delete Last Stage, respectively.

You can link a document to a specific stage through the Document Type and Document No. fields.

If you select the Show BPs Documents checkbox, only documents related to the current business partner
can be selected and linked to the stage; otherwise, all documents of all business partners are available for
selection.

The document linked to the last stage of the opportunity is displayed automatically in the Document Type
and Document No. fields of the Summary tab.

9. Go to the Attachments tab, and upload files or emails as attachments.

10. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the current opportunity.
• Add & New: add the current opportunity and open a new Opportunity page.
• Add & Back: add the current opportunity and go back to the Manage Opportunities page.

To open the Manage Sales Quotations list view, click the Sales Quotations tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for sales quotations, see Working with Sales Quotations [page 105].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of sales quotation records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Sales Quotations displays the open sales quotations created by the user who is currently logged

in.
This view is displayed by default.

• All Sales Quotations displays all sales quotations of the company.
• My Sales Quotations displays the sales quotations created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Sales Quotations displays all open sales quotations of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

1.4.1.2.1

Creating Sales Quotations

Context

You create the sales quotation document as an offer or proposal that you send either to a customer or to a lead.

Procedure

1. To create a sales quotation, click the Create Sales Quotation tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer in which you can specify the code of a

customer or a lead, and Valid Until. The document header is updated accordingly.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

110

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and bill-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new sales quotation to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.
