1.4.2.2.1

Creating Sales Orders

Context

The sales order is a commitment from a customer or lead to buy a product or service.

Procedure

1. To create a sales order, click the Create Sales Order tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer in which you can specify the code of a

customer or a lead, and Delivery Date. The document header is updated accordingly.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

119

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
select from a list of all the sales quotations for this business partner and copy the data to the current sales
order.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To check whether a specific item is available in the requested quantity and on the required delivery date,
choose Item Availability Check. If the required quantity exceeds available stock, you can adjust the quantity,
check stock in other warehouses, or select an alternative item.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and bill-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new sales order to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

1.4.3.1  Managing Deliveries

To open the Manage Deliveries list view, click the Deliveries tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for deliveries, see Working with Deliveries [page 124].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of delivery records. The views store filter
settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu:

• My Open Sales Deliveries displays the open sales deliveries created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Sales Deliveries displays all sales deliveries of the company.
• My Sales Deliveries displays the sales deliveries created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Sales Deliveries displays all open sales deliveries of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Creating Deliveries

Context

A delivery is a legally binding document indicating that the shipment of goods or the delivery of services has
occurred. Without this document, goods can only be delivered if an invoice has already been created.

Procedure

1. To create a delivery, click the Create Delivery tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Delivery Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to choose from a list of sales quotations, sales orders, A/R reserve invoices or returns for this business
partner and copy the data to the current delivery.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and bill-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

130

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new delivery record to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the delivery, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the right
side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted to
journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final journal entry
might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter return requests.

1.4.4.1  Managing Return Requests

To open the Manage Return Requests list view, click the Return Requests tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data

For more information on the detailed view for return requests, see Working with Return Requests [page 134].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of return request records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu:

• My Open Return Requests displays the open return requests created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Return Requests displays all return requests of the company.
• My Return Requests displays all return requests created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Return Requests displays all open return requests of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see

1.4.4.2.1  Creating Return Requests

Context

You create a return request as a prerequisite of the return document, to enter the agreed quantities, prices, and
return reason before the goods are returned.

Procedure

1. To create a return request, click the Create Return Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Return Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to select from a list of all the deliveries or A/R invoices for this business partner and copy the data to the
current return request.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, fill in the details of the returned items.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

In the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, bill-to, and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

 Note

Updating the ship-to address only updates the address for the current document; it doesn't affect the
warehouse address, the user defaults address, or the company details address.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

139

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new return request to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an
email with the document as your selected attachment type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending
to the document email address. For more information, see Sales and Purchasing Settings [page 724].

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.4.5.2.1

Creating Returns

Context

You create a return document when the customer requests to return items or services.

Procedure

1. To create a return, click the Create Return tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
select from a list of all the deliveries or return requests for this business partner and copy the data to the
current documents.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, bill-to, and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

 Note

Updating the ship-to address only updates the address for the current document. It doesn't affect the
warehouse address, the user defaults address, or the company details address.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new return to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New, Add

& Back.

 Note

Before you add the return, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the right side
of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted to journal
entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final journal entry might
differ from the one previewed.

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

1.4.6.1  Managing A/R Invoices

To open the Manage A/R Invoices list view, click the A/R Invoices tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for A/R invoices, see Working with A/R Invoices [page 153].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of A/R invoice records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu:

• My Open Sales Invoices displays the open A/R invoices created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Sales Invoices displays all A/R invoices of the company.
• My Sales Invoices displays the A/R invoices created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Sales Invoices displays all open A/R invoices of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide general information about the A/R invoice.

Email The document email address. It is obtained from the default contact person of the business partner.
If the default contact person does not have an email address, the business partner's email address is
used instead. If neither has an email address, this field remains empty.

The document email address will be used for the following options and scenarios involving drafting and
sending emails.

• Options Draft Multiple Emails with PDF Attachments and Send Multiple Emails with PDF

Attachments Directly to Document Emails in the Email Options window from the Share menu of
list view.

and Draft Email with PDF Attachment in the Email Options window from the Share menu of detailed
view.

Due Date Expected due date of the items or services.

The default date is 30 days after the posting date. You can change it manually, or choose a different
payment term in the Payment Terms field.

more details.

1.4.6.2.1

Creating A/R Invoices

Context

The invoice is a legally binding document. When an invoice is received, the posting is made to the related
customer accounts in the accounting system.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

159

Procedure

1. To create an A/R invoice, click the Create A/R Invoice tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
select from a list of all the sales quotations, sales orders, or deliveries for this business partner and copy
the data to the current A/R invoice.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

To check whether a specific item is available in the requested quantity and on the required delivery date,
choose Item Availability Check. If the required quantity exceeds available stock, you can adjust the quantity,
check stock in other warehouses, or select an alternative item.

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new A/R invoice to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

1.4.7.2.1

Creating A/R Credit Memos

Context

The credit memo is the clearing document for the invoice and returns.

Procedure

1. To create an A/R credit memo, click the Create A/R Credit Memo tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
select from a list of all the A/R invoices, returns, or return requests for this business partner and copy the
data to the current A/R credit memo.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, bill-to and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

 Note

Updating the ship-to address only updates the address for the current document. It doesn't affect the
warehouse address, the user defaults address, or the company details address.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

171

5. On the Accounting tab, specify relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

8. To add the new A/R credit memo to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/R credit memo, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the
right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted
to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final journal entry
might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an
email with the document as your selected attachment type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending
to the document email address. For more information, see Sales and Purchasing Settings [page 724].

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.4.7.3

Linking Paid Down Payment Requests/Invoices

Context

When creating an A/R credit memo based on an A/R invoice, you can view and edit the linked paid down
payment requests/invoices copied from the A/R invoice.

Procedure

1. Create an A/R credit memo and specify the required fields.

2. On the Contents tab, in the Total Summary area, click the Total Down Payment field.

The Down Payments to Draw screen displays all the business partner’s paid down payment requests/
invoices.

3.

In the Down Payments to Draw table, select the required down payments and specify values in the Net
Amount to Draw and the Gross Amount to Draw fields.

4. Choose the Update button.

 Note

When you select the down payment and then deselect it, the document total may be incorrect. As a
result, adding the document may fail. You need to exit the document and create it again.

For more information about down payments, see the online help for SAP Business One.

currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data

default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

1.4.9.2.1

Creating A/R Down Payments

Context

Down payments allow businesses to secure customer commitment and improve cash flows by collecting
partial payment before delivering goods or services. To request advance payments from customers, you can
create A/R down payment requests or invoices. Once the down payment is received, you can deduct the down
payment amount from the final invoice.

188

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Procedure

1. To create an A/R down payment, click the Create A/R Down Payment Invoice or the Create A/R Down

Payment Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to select from a list of all the sales quotations, sales orders, deliveries, or blanket agreements for this
business partner and copy the data to the current A/R down payment.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an existing item or create a new one.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and bill-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign an address to the sales document that is different to those already defined for the

business partner, or you can define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant details.

7. To add the new A/R down payment to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add

& New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add an A/R down payment invoice, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in
the toolbar on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If
transactions are posted to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry
preview, the final journal entry might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

Viewing Key Record Information

Below the blanket agreement record number, the header displays key information about the business record.

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Status Displays the status of the current blanket agreement. The following statuses are provided.

• Draft: The agreement is not approved, and you cannot create sales or purchasing documents

based on it. You can update the draft status to Approved.

• On Hold: The agreement is set to inactive, and you cannot create sales or purchasing documents

based on it. The agreements on hold can be updated to Approved or Terminated.

• Approved: The agreement is approved, and you can create sales or purchasing documents based

on it. You can set the approved agreements to On Hold or Terminated.

• Terminated: The agreement is concluded. Once you set the blanket agreement as terminated,
regardless of the termination date you define, the agreement is ended, and you can no longer
create sales or purchasing documents based on it.

• Canceled: The agreement is canceled.

Planned Amount
(LC)

Displays the total amount that is expected to be sold or bought within the validity of
the blanket agreement.

Cumulative Committed/
Ordered Amount (LC)

Displays the total of the sales or purchase orders in blanket agreements that
have not been copied to other documents.

Cumulative Amount (LC) Displays the total of the fulfilled amount in the blanket agreement for a business

partner.

Fulfilled % Displays the percentage of delivered quantity out of the planned quantity.

For blanket agreements using the item method, fulfillment percentage = cumulative quantity /
planned quantity.

For blanket agreements using the monetary method, fulfillment percentage = cumulative
amount / planned amount.

Performing Business Actions

You can perform the following actions using the toolbar on the right side of the header:

 Note

Copy To Choose this button to copy the current blanket agreement to other sales or purchasing documents.

The following sales documents are supported: sales quotations, sales orders, deliveries, and A/R
invoices.

The following purchasing documents are supported: purchase quotations, purchase orders, goods
receipt POs, A/P invoices, and A/P reserve invoices.

Working with the Record Content

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide general information about the blanket agreement, including vendor details,
document details, and payment preferences.

Renewal

You can set a date and a notification will appear as the date approaches.

Contents Tab

The fields on this tab provide information about the items and the agreement.

Agreement
Method

• Items Method: It serves as an agreement to sell or buy specific items to reach a predefined
planned quantity within a predefined date range, and you can set the unit price for sales or
purchasing for each item. This one is selected by default.

• Monetary Method: It serves as an agreement to sell or buy goods to reach a predefined

planned amount within a predefined date range, and you can set a price list and a discount
in the blanket agreement.

Agreement
Type

• General: General blanket agreements are used to track the fulfillment of terms to obtain a
special bonus at year-end. For example, for selling or purchasing a certain quantity of an
item or for achieving a defined turnover. This one is selected by default.

• Specific: Specific blanket agreements are used to track the fulfillment of terms to obtain
a specific discount for individual sales or purchase transactions. They can also be used to
determine a delivery schedule, for example, by defining at which intervals which quantity of
goods should be delivered.

Ignore Prices
Specified in
Blanket
Agreement

194

PUBLIC

If the agreement type is General, this checkbox is selected. When you link a blanket
agreement to other sales or purchase documents, the Unit Price field is not populated by

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

the unit price from the blanket agreement, and you can update the price according to your
business needs.

If the agreement type is Specific, this checkbox is deselected. It means that when you
link a blanket agreement to other sales or purchasing documents, the Unit Price field is
populated by the unit price from the blanket agreement, and therefore you cannot update
the price.

Price
Mode

Choose the price mode to include or exclude taxes in the prices.

 Note

This field is available only when you select the checkbox Separate Net and Gross Price Mode

under  Administration Configuration

 Sales and Purchasing Sales and Purchasing Settings

Sales and Purchasing .

• Net: On the Contents tab, the Unit Price column is enabled, and the values you enter here

exclude taxes.

• Gross: On the Documents tab, the Gross Price column is enabled, and the values you enter here

include taxes.

 Note

This field is not available for the Brazil, India, and Israel localizations.

Close Enables you to set one or more document rows to the Closed status. This button is available for draft

or on-hold blanket agreements of the item type.

After you close the rows:

• You can add the same items to the same blanket agreement.
• You can add the same items to a different blanket agreement with the same period.
• New documents cannot be linked to the closed rows.
• The existing linked documents remain linked and are displayed on the Documents tab.
• Open quantities and open amounts are set to zero, but planned quantities, cumulative quantities,

and cumulative amounts stay unchanged.

Price List Displays the price list.

It is only available when the agreement method is monetary. When the agreement type is general,
the price list is ignored.

Delivery
Plan

Choose the   icon to open a dialog box, where you can define the details of the delivery plan
for the blanket agreement. If the blanket agreement has the status Canceled or Terminated, you
cannot edit the delivery plan.

Frequency

Enables you to specify the period of item release. You can choose from the following: Daily,
Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Annually, Annually, and One Time.

From Date, To Date

Enable you to specify the start and end dates for the delivery plan. This date range needs to be

Date of the delivery plan cannot be later than that of the blanket agreement.

Release

Consume Forecast

This checkbox enables you to decide whether to consume the quantities in the material
requirements planning (MRP) run. If you select the checkbox, the open quantities of the specified
item are subtracted from the MRP's forecast quantities. If you do not select the checkbox, the
MRP's forecast quantities do not change based on this item.

You can work with the MRP run in the SAP Business One client.

Documents Tab

The fields on this tab provide information about the documents associated with the blanket agreement.

The documents are displayed according to their posting dates, with the most recent one at the top. If the
posting dates are the same, the documents are organized according to document numbers in ascending order,
with the smallest number at the top.

Attachments Tab

This tab shows the attachments of the current business partner.

You can add attachments after you define an attachment folder path at the company level. You have access
permissions to the attachment folder when you are granted the relevant authorization in the SAP Business One
client.

When a default attachment folder is assigned to each user in the SAP Business One client, the attachments are
uploaded to this default folder.

You can select the uploaded attachment to display or download it.

 Note

Make sure that the attachment size is less than 50 MB. For files that are 50 MB or larger, you can upload
them through the SAP Business One client.

Attachments are uploaded to the attachment folder through the Service Layer. For a Service Layer running
on SAP HANA on Linux, direct access to the folder is not allowed. For more information about setting up
an attachment folder, see the section Setting up an Attachment Folder in Working with SAP Business One
Service Layer.

Recurring Transactions Tab

This tab enables you to view and link single or multiple recurring transaction templates to the current
blanket agreement, and to view the linked recurring transactions that are executed or await execution. For

more information about recurring transaction templates and recurring transactions, see Managing Recurring
Transaction Templates [page 217] and Managing Recurring Transactions [page 219].

The linked recurring transaction templates are displayed in the tree view, and the recurring transactions are
shown under the template. Two buttons, Expand and Collapse, are provided to change the table layout.

To associate a recurring transaction template with the blanket agreement, make sure that the business

date range of the blanket agreement. Executed recurring transactions cannot be removed from the blanket
agreement.

Remove Enables you to remove a recurring transaction template from the blanket agreement.

You can only remove recurring transaction templates that have no associated recurring
transactions.

Template

Enter the code of the recurring transaction template or choose the  Value Help icon to link a
recurring transaction template to the blanket agreement. You can only choose templates defined
for the same business partner as the blanket agreement.

After adding, the templates are displayed in collapsed mode. You can click the Expand button to
expand the templates.

1.4.10.2.1  Creating Blanket Agreements

Prerequisites

You need proper authorizations to create blanket agreements.

Context

You can create a sales or purchase blanket agreement to record the delivery of goods or services in a specific
period, based on predefined terms and conditions.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

197

Procedure

1. To create a sales or purchase blanket agreement, click the Create Sales Blanket Agreement or Create

Purchase Blanket Agreement tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory information about the business partner, the date, and the

payment preferences.

3. On the Contents tab, enter relevant details in the Preferences section above the table, for example, the

agreement method and agreement type. In addition, enter item-related data in the table, for example, item
number, planned quantity, unit price, and cumulative amount.

4. On the Documents tab, review the documents associated with the blanket agreement.

5. On the Attachments tab, upload the attachments related to the blanket agreement.

6. On the Recurring Transactions tab, specify the recurring transaction templates of the same business

partner and link them to the blanket agreement. You can add more than one template.

7. To add the record to the company database, choose one of the following options: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

1.4.11  A/R Correction Invoices

An A/R correction invoice is a document issued to a customer when one of the following applies:

• Rebates and discounts were given after the original invoice was issued.
• The issued goods were returned.
• The prices of goods and services were changed after the original invoice was issued.
• There was a mistake in price, tax rate, tax amount, net value, gross value, quantity, or unit of measure in

any invoice item.

An A/R correction invoice usually refers to a base document such as an A/R invoice or another A/R correction
invoice. However, you can enter a correction invoice without any reference to a preceding document.

Apps

When working with A/R correction invoices, you can find the following apps:

• A/R Correction Invoices

SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

A/R correction invoices are available only in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Portugal, Russia,
Slovakia, and Ukraine localizations.

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter A/R correction invoices.
• View and manage different views of A/R correction invoice lists.
• View, edit, and create A/R correction invoices.
• Copy an A/R correction invoice to another A/R correction invoice.
• Copy an A/R correction invoice to an A/R correction invoice reversal.
• Create and process A/R correction invoice drafts.

1.4.11.2.1  Creating A/R Correction Invoices

Context

You can create an A/R correction invoice to adjust previously issued invoices by copying data from base
documents and modifying relevant fields.

Procedure

1. To create an A/R correction invoice, choose the Create A/R Correction Invoice tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to select either an A/R invoice or another A/R correction invoice and copy the data to the current A/R
correction invoice.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

206

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

Details

• Was

Displays the content from the base document (original invoice or correction invoice). The fields in this
section are not editable and show the original values for fields such as item number, item description,
quantity, unit price, discount, tax code, and total.

• Should Be

Enter the information that you want to correct. You can edit fields such as quantity, unit price,
discount, tax code, and total to make the necessary corrections. The item number can't be modified.
You can add additional item lines if necessary.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and bill-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the sales document an address different to those addresses already defined for the

business partner, or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current sales document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. To add the new A/R correction invoice to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View,

Add & New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/R correction invoice, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar
on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions
are posted to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final
journal entry might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.4.12.2.1  Creating A/R Correction Invoice Reversals

Procedure

1. To create an A/R correction invoice reversal, choose the Create A/R Correction Invoice Reversal tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Customer and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
select an A/R correction invoice and copy the data to the A/R correction invoice reversal.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a sales
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new customer, choose the   icon in the Customer field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Customer field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

Details

• Was

Displays the content from the base document (correction invoice). The fields in this section are not

price, discount, tax code, and total.

1.4.13.1  Managing Recurring Transaction Templates

Recurring transaction templates can be used to streamline business processes that repeat regularly.

To open the Recurring Transaction Templates list view, choose the Recurring Transaction Templates app on the
home page from the Sales, Purchasing, or Inventory Transactions groups.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of delivery records. The views store filter
settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

217

• My Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays recurring transaction templates that have been

created by the current user and whose validity date is in the future.

• All Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all the recurring transaction templates that are available in

the system for localization, including those with validity dates in the past and in the future.

• Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all recurring transaction templates available in the system

for the localization, with their validity date in the future.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

Performing Business Actions

Use the options in the table toolbar to perform the following actions:

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Table Toolbar [page 68].

BP Properties Choose whether to ignore business partner properties when filtering the templates. The

default selection is Yes. If you select No, select the properties you want to filter from the list
and choose Update.

Select one or more business partner properties as the filtering criteria to display the
templates.

Features of Recurring Transaction Templates List View

You can create new templates, or edit, delete, or duplicate existing templates. With the templates and their
recurrence details, recurring transaction instances are recorded, and execution is based on the templates you

218

define. For more information on executing recurring transactions, see Managing Recurring Transactions [page
219].

Creating Recurring Transaction Template

1. Choose Create located in the table toolbar.

2. On the General tab, specify the relevant information, including the template name, document type,

document number, recurrence period, start date, and valid-until date.

 Note

The valid-until date is optional and can be added later.

Recurrence
Period

Choose the intervals at which you want the recurring transaction to be repeated. The
following options are available: Daily, Weekly, Every 2 Weeks, Monthly, Every 2 Months,
Quarterly, Semiannually, Annually, and One Time.

After you enter the interval and a start date for the transaction, the date for the next

3. On the Contents tab, review the information that was auto-populated.

1.4.14.1  Creating Documents Using Document Generation

Wizard

Context

To generate documents using the wizard, follow this procedure.

Procedure

1.

In the Document Generation Options step, create a new parameter set or select an existing one.

a. Create a new parameter set or select an existing one.

2.

In the Target Document step, configure the target documents and related options.

 Note

In the Base Documents step, filter and select base documents.

c. Choose Next.

In the Consolidation Options step, set consolidation preferences.

a. Select whether you want to consolidate target documents and how you want them to be consolidated.

b. Choose Next.

In the Recommendation Report step, select and modify target document details.

6.

saving.

a. Select one of the following options:

1.4.15  Managing Drafts

You can create and process draft documents of sales documents, purchasing documents, payments
documents, and inventory documents.

To create a draft document, click the Create... tile of the relevant object, for example, Create A/R Invoice or
Create Purchase Quotation, or Create Outgoing Payment for Business Partner, enter all relevant details and then
choose one of the following options in the multi-choice button:

Save as Draft & New Adds the draft document and opens the document detailed view in Create mode for

creating another document in sequence.

Save as Draft & View Adds the draft document and has it displayed for further review.

In the list views of draft documents, such as the Manage Sales & Purchasing Drafts list view, the Manage
Incoming & Outgoing Payments Drafts list view, or the Manage Inventory Transactions Drafts list view, you can
perform the following tasks for single or multiple drafts:

Delete

Deletes the selected drafts from the database.

Close

Sets the status of the drafts as Closed.

Reopen Opens closed drafts and changes the status of open drafts to Closed, as in list view.

Add

Adds the drafts as official documents.

If approval isn’t required, you use the Save as Draft function to save the target document. If

1.4.16  Managing Documents in Approval Process

When trying to add or update a document that triggers an approval process, you see that this document is
saved as a draft. After the authorizers approve the draft in the Manage Approval Decisions list view, you can
continue adding or updating the draft.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales orders, sales quotations, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, returns,
A/R credit memos, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve invoices, goods receipt POs, goods
returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods issues, outgoing payments, inventory transfers, and inventory
transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When creating or updating a document in Web client, you are notified by the system that an approval is

required.

2. You become the originator of the approval process and a draft is created.

3. The authorizers review the draft and either approve or reject the request in the Manage Approval Decisions

list view.

4. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer.

5. To view the approval status and proceed with the process, click the Docs in Approval Process tile; the
Manage Docs in Approval Process list view opens. (Alternatively, you can access the draft from the
notification as well.)

 Note

For the outgoing payments approval process, there is a separate list view: Manage Outgoing Payments
in Approval Process.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

225

In the list view you can:

• Filter, sort, group, and access the relevant drafts
• Add approved drafts
• Cancel approval processes for selected drafts
• Restore approval processes for selected drafts

6. Depending on the approval status, you can either generate a document (choose  Edit Add & View ) or

update the draft (choose Edit) to trigger a new approval process.

Related Information

Approval Decisions [page 226]

1.4.17  Approval Decisions

When a user triggers an approval process, as the authorizer, you can see all the draft documents for approval in
the Approval Decisions list view and decide what to do with those requests.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales quotations, sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, return
requests, returns, A/R credit memos, purchase requests, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve
invoices, goods receipt POs, goods return requests, goods returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods
issues, goods receipts, inventory transfers, and inventory transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When a user that is creating or updating a document triggers an approval process, you as an authorizer are

notified by the system that your approval is required.

 Note

You can choose to also get those notifications by email. See Approval Process Settings [page 715]

226

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

2. You become the authorizer of the approval process for the draft that was created.

3. To review the requests for approval, click the Approval Decisions tile; the Manage Approval Decisions list

view opens. The requests for approval that match the selected view are displayed. The default view is My
Pending Requests for Approval.

4. You can perform the following actions:

• Choose another view or apply different filters and view settings to fine tune the displayed list.
• Select one or more requests for approval and apply the relevant action. You can choose to approve or

reject the request.

5. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer and can

proceed with the process. See Managing Documents in Approval Process [page 225]

1.4.18  Managing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations

You can work with batches, serial numbers and bin locations in relevant marketing documents and inventory
documents.

In this case, both outgoing and incoming batches, serial numbers and bin locations are available.

There are two scenarios where you work on the outgoing side:

• Inventory issue documents, for example, deliveries.
• Inventory issue lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an incoming document. For example,

on a line of a goods receipt PO, the quantity is minus 100.

For more information, see Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 227].

Likewise, there are two scenarios where you work on the incoming side:

• Inventory receipt documents, for example, A/P invoices.
• Inventory receipt lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an outgoing document. For example,

on a line of an A/R invoice, the quantity is minus 50.

For more information, see Incoming Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 229].

1.4.18.1  Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin

are relevant to serial/batch numbers and bin location allocation.

In the dialog box, you can:

shows a list of your selections, and it’s possible to remove the selected bin locations from the list.

The  Value Help icon in this column leads to the same dialog box as that in the Serial/Batch
Numbers and Bin Location Allocation fields.

1.4.18.2.1  Automatically Creating Batches and Serial

Numbers

When you need to create a large amount of batches or serial numbers, you can use the automatic creation
function. For inventory counting transactions, the newly created serial/batch numbers are stored in the system
as drafts.

Prerequisites

You are working with items managed by batches or serial numbers.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

231

Context

To access the Automatic Creation button, you can do either of the following:

• On the Contents tab of the detailed view in relevant documents (except inventory counting transactions),

choose the  Value Help icon in the Serial/Batch Numbers field.

• On the Counting tab of the detailed view in inventory counting transactions, choose the  Value Help icon

in the Counted Qty field.

 Note

• For A/R returns and A/R credit memos, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Serial/Batch

Numbers field, and then in the center right of the opened dialog box, select the Create button.
If bin location-enabled warehouses are selected on the line, you can also choose the value help icons in
the Bin Location Allocation and Bin Locations fields.

• For inventory counting transactions, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Counted Qty

field, and then in the center right of the dialog box, select the Create button.
When you work with team counters, the dialog box is also accessible through the value help icon in the
Team Total Counted Qty field.

Procedure

1. Click the Automatic Creation button. A dialog box opens up.

2. (Optional) In the Bin Location field, specify the bin location to store your batches or serial numbers.

3. For batch items, in the field No. of Batches, specify how many batches you want to create.

4.

5.

6.

7.

In the Batch or Serial Number field, choose the value help icon. The dialog box Automatic String Creation
opens up.

Input strings for batches or serial numbers.

In the Type column, choose String or Number.

If you choose the Number type, in the Operations column, you can define one of the following operations
for the numbers: No Operations, Increase, and Decrease. The operations are performed during the
automatic creation process. If you choose the String type, the column isn’t editable. The format is
displayed in the Final String field.

8. To save your actions, choose OK.

9. To start the automatic creation, choose Create.

Results

The newly created serial/batch numbers are displayed in the dialog box. You can review and update relevant
information. To save all data and close the dialog box, choose OK.

1.5  Purchasing

The apps in the purchasing group covers the entire purchasing process, from requesting purchase quotations
from your vendors, through the processing of the A/P invoices, save document drafts, and printing.

The Purchasing group includes apps that allows you to work with the following purchasing documents:
purchase requests, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve invoices, goods receipt POs, goods
return requests, goods returns, A/P invoices, and A/P credit memos.

1.5.1.1  Managing Purchase Requests

To open the Manage Purchase Requests list view, click the Purchase Requests tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for purchase requests, see Working with Purchase Requests [page
236].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of purchase request records. The views
store filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine
which records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views
menu in the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Purchase Requests displays the still open purchase requests created by the user who is currently

logged in.
This view is displayed by default.

• All Purchase Requests displays all the purchase request records of the company.
• My Purchase Requests displays all the purchase requests created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Purchase Requests displays the still open purchase requests of the company.

1.5.1.2.1

Creating Purchase Requests

Context

You create the purchase request document to be sent to several vendors to indicate their terms and conditions,
such as price or delivery date for the supply of materials or the provision of services.

Procedure

1. To create a new purchase request, click the Create Purchase Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Valid Until date, Required Date, and Requestor.

The requestor can be either a user or an employee in the company. By default, the current user appears in
this field.

The relevant information, such as requester name, department and email address are filled in
automatically.

Select the Send Email if PO or GRPO is Added checkbox to send an email to the requester once a purchase
order or goods receipt PO is created based on this purchase request. When this checkbox is selected, the
Email Address field is mandatory.

 Note

The default setting of the checkbox is determined by the settings of the Send E-Mail When PO or

Goods Receipt PO is Created checkbox in the

 System Initialization

 Document

Settings

 Per Document

 Purchase Request

.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

You can choose a vendor for a specific row. If a preferred vendor is defined for the specific item in the

Item Master Data

4. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

5. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

6. To add the new purchase request to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

1.5.2.2.1

Creating Purchase Quotations

Context

You create the purchase quotation document after requesting quotations for items or services from your
vendors.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

249

Procedure

1. To create a new purchase quotation, click the Create Purchase Quotation tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor code and Valid Until date. The document header

is updated accordingly. You can also add other relevant information.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to choose from a list of all the purchase requests for this business partner and copy data to the current
purchase quotation.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in other details.

The Total Payment Due field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and pay-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new purchase quotation to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add

& New, Add & Back.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

1.5.3.1  Managing Purchase Orders

To open the Manage Purchase Orders list view, click the Purchase Orders tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for purchase orders, see Working with Purchase Orders [page 254].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of purchase order records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Purchase Orders displays the open purchase orders created by the user who is currently logged

in.
This view is displayed by default.

• All Purchase Orders displays all purchase orders of the company.
• My Purchase Orders displays the purchase orders created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Purchase Orders displays all open purchase orders of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

252

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

Performing Business Actions

Use the options in the table toolbar to perform the following actions:

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Table Toolbar [page 68].

Copy
To

Choose this button to copy one or more purchase orders to a goods receipt PO, A/P reserve invoice,
or A/P invoice.

The default value from the related business partner master data is used when you copy a purchase
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

When selecting multiple purchase orders, you can only select documents with the same business
partner, document type (Service type or Item type), and price mode (Net or Gross price mode).

 Note

The icons in the table toolbar enable you to manage and customize the data in the table, such as to sort,
filter, and group the data ( View Settings), export records ( Export to Microsoft Excel), and control how
the data is displayed in the table ( Table View,  Chart View, and  Card View). For more information, see
Table Area [page 68].

Features of Purchase Orders List View

When managing records in table view, a total value is displayed at the bottom of the column in bold text for the
amount-related fields. You can also filter the purchase orders with numbers against them.

Filters in the filter bar, and enter >100 in the Document Total field.

1.5.4.2.1

Creating A/P Reserve Invoices

Context

You create an A/P reserve invoice to document an A/P invoice you receive from a vendor before the goods
arrive. A/P reserve invoices enable you to create relevant postings in the accounting system only and do not
affect inventory and inventory values.

Procedure

1. To create an A/P reserve invoice, click the Create A/P Reserve Invoice tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Due Date. The document header is updated

accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to choose from a list of all the purchase quotations or purchase orders for this business partner and then
copy data to the current A/P reserve invoice.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

You can also add other relevant information.

3. On the Contents tab fill in other details.

The Total Payment Due field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

In the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and pay-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

266

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new A/P reserve invoice to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add

& New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/P reserve invoice, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar
on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions
are posted to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final
journal entry might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an
email with the document as your selected attachment type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending
to the document email address. For more information, see Sales and Purchasing Settings [page 724].

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.
