1.5.5.2.1

Creating Goods Receipt POs

Context

You create the goods receipt PO document when you receive goods from your vendors.

Procedure

1. To create a new goods receipt PO, click the Create Goods Receipt PO tile.

2. On the General tab, fill in the mandatory fields: Vendor code and Due Date. The document header is

updated accordingly. You can also add other relevant information.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
choose from a list of all the purchase quotations, A/P reserve invoices, purchase orders, and goods returns
for this business partner and copy data to the current goods receipt PO.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor master data, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business
Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in other details.

The Total Payment Due field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

1.5.6.2.1

Creating Goods Return Requests

Context

The Return Material Agreement describes a scenario where the supplier of a good or product agrees to have a
customer ship that item back in exchange for a refund or credit.

The purpose of adding a goods return request is to enable the creation of prerequisites for the goods return
document to enter the agreed quantities, prices, and return reason before the goods are actually returned.

Procedure

1. To create a goods return request, click the Create Goods Return Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Return Date date. The document header is

updated accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
choose from a list of all the goods receipt POs or A/P invoices for this business partner and copy data to
the current goods return request.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business Partners
dialog box, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant fields and
choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the document.

This feature applies to items as well.

You can also add other relevant information.

3. On the Contents tab, fill in the other details.

The Total Credit field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

In the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

In the Return Action field you can choose the relevant return action from the return actions list. The default
return action is Return. You can choose other actions from the list, such as: Repair or Replace, according to
the values set in the Return Actions - Setup window in the SAP Business One client.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

285

In the Return Reason field you can choose the reason why you want to return the goods to your vendor. You
can choose any return reason according to the values set in the Return Reasons - Setup window in the SAP
Business One client.

Select the Without Qty Posting field if there is no inventory movement involved, meaning the goods return
request does not affect the inventory quantity of the item. By default, this checkbox is not selected.

For a standalone goods return request, selecting this checkbox or not affects the target document that
could be created based on the goods return request. If it is selected, you can create a goods return or
credit memo based on the goods return request, and if it is not selected you can only create a credit memo
based on the goods return request.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, pay-to and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

 Note

Updating the ship-from address only updates the address for the current document. It doesn't affect
the warehouse address, the user defaults address, or the company details address.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new goods return request to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View,

Add & New, Add & Back.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an
email with the document as your selected attachment type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending
to the document email address. For more information, see Sales and Purchasing Settings [page 724].

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.5.7.1  Managing Goods Returns

To open the Manage Goods Returns list view, click the Goods Returns tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for goods returns, see Working with Goods Returns [page 289].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of goods return records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Goods Returns displays all the still open goods returns created by the user who is currently

logged in.
This view is displayed by default.

• All Goods Returns displays all the goods return records of the company.
• My Goods Returns displays all the goods returns created by the user who is currently logged in.The default
value from the related business partner master data is used when you copy a purchase document from
multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

• Open Goods Returns displays the still open goods return records of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

copy data to the current goods return.

Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to Items as well.

The Total Credit field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, pay-to and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

to the current purchase document only.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your

default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for A/P invoices, see Working with A/P Invoices [page 300].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of A/P invoice records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open A/P Invoices displays the still open A/P invoices created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All A/P Invoices displays all the A/P invoices of the company.
• My A/P Invoices displays all the A/P invoices created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open A/P Invoices displays the still open A/P invoices of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).

1.5.8.2.1

Creating A/P Invoices

Context

The invoice is a legally binding document. When an invoice is received, the posting is made to the related
customer accounts in the accounting system.

Procedure

1. To create an A/P invoice, click the Create A/P Invoice tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Due Date. The document header is updated

accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to
choose from a list of all the purchase quotations, purchase orders, and goods receipt POs for this business
partner and copy data to the current A/P invoice.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor master data, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business
Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to Items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in other details.

The Total Payment Due field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

305

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and pay-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new A/P invoice to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/P invoice, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the
right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted
to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final journal entry
might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

After you have selected the E-Mail Document checkbox in the When Adding Document section through

Administration System Initialization Print Preferences Per Document

 in the SAP Business

One client and set up Microsoft 365 integration, an email draft will appear with the document as a
Microsoft Word attachment when the document is added manually in add mode, added as an official
document in the approval process, or added as an official document from the draft. You can check the
corresponding email log in the SAP Business One client. To set up Microsoft 365 integration, see How
to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration. For more information about this feature, see
SAP Notes 3143036

 and 3626978

.

If you further select the Send Email Directly to Recipient When Email Document Is Selected in Print
Preferences in SAP Business One checkbox on the Sales and Purchasing tab of the Sales and Purchasing

Settings page through  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and Purchasing , an
email with the document as your selected attachment type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending
to the document email address. For more information, see Sales and Purchasing Settings [page 724].

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.5.8.3

Linking Paid Down Payment Requests/Invoices

Context

When creating an A/P invoice, you can link paid down payment requests/invoices.

Procedure

1. Create an A/P invoice and specify the required fields.

2. On the Contents tab, in the Total Summary area, click the Total Down Payment field.

The Down Payments to Draw screen displays all the business partner’s paid down payment requests/
invoices.

3.

In the Down Payments to Draw table, select the required down payments and specify the values in the Net
Amount to Draw and the Gross Amount to Draw fields.

4. Choose the Update button.

 Note

When you select the down payment and then deselect it, the document total may be incorrect. As a
result, adding the document may fail. You need to exit the document and create it again.

For more information about down payments, see the online help for SAP Business One.

1.5.9.2.1

Creating A/P Credit Memos

Context

The A/P credit memo is the clearing document for the A/P invoice.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

315

Procedure

1. To create an A/P credit memo, click the Create A/P Credit Memo tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Due Date. The document header is updated

accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to choose from a list of all the A/P invoices, goods returns, and goods return requests for this business
partner and copy data to the current A/P credit memo.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor master data, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business
Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to Items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in other details.

The Total Credit field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

To view item availability across warehouses, choose Available to Promise. The report displays available
quantities based on In Stock, Committed, and Ordered quantities across all warehouses.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-from, pay-to and ship-to addresses, and other settings under

the Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

 Note

Updating the ship-from address only updates the address for the current document. It doesn't affect
the warehouse address, the user defaults address, or the company details address.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

8. To add the new A/P credit memo to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/P credit memo, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the
right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted

1.5.10  Landed Costs

When importing goods, companies incur additional costs, such as customs, transport and insurance fees, or
taxes. You can use the landed costs to allocate these costs to the imported items and reflect them in the
accounting system.

Apps

When working with landed costs, you can find the following apps:

• Landed Costs
• Create Landed Costs

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter landed costs.
• View, edit, and create landed costs.

1.5.10.1  Managing Landed Costs

To open the Manage Landed Costs list view, click the Landed Costs tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of landed costs records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Landed Costs displays the still open landed costs created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Landed Costs displays all the landed costs of the company.
• My Landed Costs displays the landed costs created by the user who is currently logged in.
• Open Landed Costs displays all the open landed costs of the company.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

Customs
and Fixed
Costs

Projected
Customs

Customs

Displays the estimated customs costs based on the customs percentage
defined for the items. This amount is calculated automatically before actual
customs costs are entered.

Displays the actual customs costs incurred for the shipment. You can enter
this amount manually after the customs invoice is received. This value
replaces the projected customs in the final cost calculations.

Total Fixed
Costs

Displays the sum of all fixed costs (such as freight, insurance, and other landed
costs) allocated to the items in this document. This amount is distributed
among the items based on the defined allocation method.

Amount to
Balance

Displays any remaining difference between the total allocated costs and
the actual costs entered. When this field shows zero, all costs have been
properly allocated to the items.

Costs Tab

The fields on this tab display information on fixed costs allocated to the items.

Fixed Costs Lists all the landed cost types (such as freight, insurance, handling charges) that are allocated

to the items in this document. You can add multiple cost types, each with its own allocation
method.

Allocation
By

Determines how the fixed cost is distributed among the items. Options include:

• Cash Value Before Customs allocates costs proportionally based on the item values before

customs.

• Cash Value After Customs allocates costs proportionally based on the item values after

customs.

• Quantity allocates costs evenly based on item quantities.
• Volume allocates costs based on item volume.
• Weight allocates costs based on item weight.

Factor Displays the percentage rate of each landed cost out of the total FOB (Free On Board) costs of

the shipment. This factor can help you determine the shipment efficiency in comparison to other
shipments or certain standards.

Procedure

1. To create a landed costs document, choose the Create Landed Costs tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the vendor, and fill in other details. You can add one or more vendors. The

document header is updated accordingly.

Broker Select the business partner associated with the document. If multiple broker invoices are

enabled, the broker you select here is used as the default.

Bill of Lading No.

Enter the bill of lading number associated with the shipment.

Transport Type

Specify the shipping type.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the upper right corner of the header
to choose from a list of all the goods receipt POs, A/P invoices, or other landed costs documents for this
business partner and copy data to the current landed costs document.

 Note

A/P Invoices only appears for companies with a perpetual inventory system.

3. On the Items tab, review the following sections.

Customs
Details

This section defines how customs-related costs are calculated and posted for the landed
cost.

• Customs Date

Review the customs date. If the vendor or broker uses a foreign currency, the system
uses this date to determine the exchange rate for customs calculations.

• Customs Affects Inventory

Select the checkbox if customs costs must be included in the inventory value.

Items From the dropdown list in the left corner above the table, you can select from Items and Details

and the table data is populated with the relevant fields.

Costs are allocated automatically to the items from the base document. You can review and adjust
customs and fixed costs information, if necessary.

Items Lists the inventory items included in the landed cost document. The line items are

populated from the base purchasing document.

Details Displays additional cost allocation and price list information.

• Apply Fixed Costs

Select whether to apply fixed costs to the item.

• Price List

4. On the Costs tab, you can add fixed costs to be allocated to the items.

Fixed
Costs

This section records and allocates costs related to procurement and delivery of goods such as
freight, insurance, handling, or other charges.

New Costs

Use this option to define new landed costs in Configuration.

Recalculate If you have made manual changes to costs, this option redistributes the cost

components across item lines using the selected Allocation By method and
updates line and document totals.

For each line item in the table, specify the following:
• The landed cost type (such as insurance, shipping, or storage charges)
• The Allocation By method (such as Cash Value Before Customs, Quantity, Volume, or Weight)
• Whether to Include for Customs in the customs value calculation.

 Note

If you have enabled multiple broker invoices for landed costs, you can select a broker code for each
type of cost.

The factor is calculated automatically.

1.5.11.2.1  Creating A/P Down Payments

Context

Down payments help manage vendor relationships and secure orders when suppliers require advance
payments before shipping goods or providing services. When vendors require prepayment for your orders,
you can create A/P down payment requests or invoices. Once the down payment is made, you can deduct the
down payment amount from the final invoice.

Procedure

1. To create an A/P down payment, click the Create A/P Down Payment Invoice or the Create A/P Down

Payment Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Due Date. The document header is updated

accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to choose from a list of all the purchase quotations, purchase orders, goods receipt POs or blanket
agreements for this business partner and copy data to the current A/P down payment.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create new vendor master data, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business
Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in the relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to Items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

The Total Payment Due field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

If you choose Item, in the Item No. field, you can select an item or create a new one.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and pay-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

332

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

6. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter the relevant details.

7. To add the new A/P down payment to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add

& New, or Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/P down payment, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar
on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions
are posted to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final
journal entry might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

The Save as Draft & New and Save as Draft & View options only appear for users who have

authorizations for Document Draft through  Administration System Initialization Authorizations

General Authorizations Sales Document Draft

 in the SAP Business One client.

1.5.12.2  Working with Blanket Agreements

The detailed view in the Web client allows you to view and work with all relevant details for the record in one
place. The header area contains key information about the specific data record and business action buttons,
while the content area displays related fields structured with a series of tabs. When you open a data record in
the detailed view, it is displayed in view mode.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

Viewing Key Record Information

Below the blanket agreement record number, the header displays key information about the business record.

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Status Displays the status of the current blanket agreement. The following statuses are provided.

• Draft: The agreement is not approved, and you cannot create sales or purchasing documents

based on it. You can update the draft status to Approved.

• On Hold: The agreement is set to inactive, and you cannot create sales or purchasing documents

based on it. The agreements on hold can be updated to Approved or Terminated.

• Approved: The agreement is approved, and you can create sales or purchasing documents based

on it. You can set the approved agreements to On Hold or Terminated.

• Terminated: The agreement is concluded. Once you set the blanket agreement as terminated,
regardless of the termination date you define, the agreement is ended, and you can no longer
create sales or purchasing documents based on it.

• Canceled: The agreement is canceled.

Planned Amount
(LC)

Displays the total amount that is expected to be sold or bought within the validity of
the blanket agreement.

Displays the total of the sales or purchase orders in blanket agreements that
have not been copied to other documents.

Cumulative Amount (LC) Displays the total of the fulfilled amount in the blanket agreement for a business

partner.

Fulfilled % Displays the percentage of delivered quantity out of the planned quantity.

For blanket agreements using the item method, fulfillment percentage = cumulative quantity /
planned quantity.

For blanket agreements using the monetary method, fulfillment percentage = cumulative
amount / planned amount.

Agreement
Method

337

• Monetary Method: It serves as an agreement to sell or buy goods to reach a predefined

planned amount within a predefined date range, and you can set a price list and a discount

Agreement
Type

• General: General blanket agreements are used to track the fulfillment of terms to obtain a
special bonus at year-end. For example, for selling or purchasing a certain quantity of an
item or for achieving a defined turnover. This one is selected by default.

• Specific: Specific blanket agreements are used to track the fulfillment of terms to obtain
a specific discount for individual sales or purchase transactions. They can also be used to
determine a delivery schedule, for example, by defining at which intervals which quantity of
goods should be delivered.

Ignore Prices

If the agreement type is General, this checkbox is selected. When you link a blanket
agreement to other sales or purchase documents, the Unit Price field is not populated by

business needs.

If the agreement type is Specific, this checkbox is deselected. It means that when you
link a blanket agreement to other sales or purchasing documents, the Unit Price field is
populated by the unit price from the blanket agreement, and therefore you cannot update
the price.

This checkbox enables you to decide whether to consume the quantities in the material
requirements planning (MRP) run. If you select the checkbox, the open quantities of the specified

MRP's forecast quantities do not change based on this item.

You can work with the MRP run in the SAP Business One client.

date range of the blanket agreement. Executed recurring transactions cannot be removed from the blanket

Remove Enables you to remove a recurring transaction template from the blanket agreement.

1.5.12.2.1  Creating Blanket Agreements

Prerequisites

You need proper authorizations to create blanket agreements.

Context

You can create a sales or purchase blanket agreement to record the delivery of goods or services in a specific
period, based on predefined terms and conditions.

Procedure

1. To create a sales or purchase blanket agreement, click the Create Sales Blanket Agreement or Create

Purchase Blanket Agreement tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory information about the business partner, the date, and the

payment preferences.

3. On the Contents tab, enter relevant details in the Preferences section above the table, for example, the

agreement method and agreement type. In addition, enter item-related data in the table, for example, item
number, planned quantity, unit price, and cumulative amount.

4. On the Documents tab, review the documents associated with the blanket agreement.

5. On the Attachments tab, upload the attachments related to the blanket agreement.

6. On the Recurring Transactions tab, specify the recurring transaction templates of the same business

partner and link them to the blanket agreement. You can add more than one template.

7. To add the record to the company database, choose one of the following options: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

1.5.13  A/P Correction Invoices

An A/P correction invoice is a document issued to a vendor when one of the following applies:

• Rebates and discounts were given after the original invoice was issued.
• The issued goods were returned.
• The prices of goods and services were changed after the original invoice was issued.
• There was a mistake in price, tax rate, tax amount, net value, gross value, quantity, or unit of measure in

any invoice item.

An A/P correction invoice usually refers to a base document such as an A/P invoice or another A/P correction
invoice. However, you can enter a correction invoice without any reference to a preceding document.

Apps

When working with A/P correction invoices, you can find the following apps:

• A/P Correction Invoices
• Create A/P Correction Invoice

 Note

A/P correction invoices are available only in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Portugal, Russia,
Slovakia, and Ukraine localizations.

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter A/P correction invoices.
• View and manage different views of A/P correction invoice lists.
• View, edit, and create A/P correction invoices.
• Copy an A/P correction invoice to another A/P correction invoice.
• Copy an A/P correction invoice to an A/P correction invoice reversal.
• Create and process A/P correction invoice drafts.

1.5.13.2.1  Creating A/P Correction Invoices

Context

You can create an A/P correction invoice to adjust previously issued invoices by copying data from base
documents and modifying relevant fields.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

349

Procedure

1. To create an A/P correction invoice, choose the Create A/P Correction Invoice tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the mandatory fields: Vendor and Due Date. The document header is updated

accordingly.

After you select the business partner, choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header
to select either an A/P invoice or another A/P correction invoice and copy the data to the current A/P
correction invoice.

You can choose to keep the existing rows when copying from base documents.

The default value from the related business partner master data will be used when you copy a purchasing
document from multiple base documents and a discrepancy exists in the header data.

 Note

If you need to create a new vendor master data, choose the   icon in the Vendor field. In the Business
Partners form, choose Create in the right corner of the table, enter the required data in relevant
fields and choose Add. As a result, the newly created BP code is populated in the Vendor field of the
document.

This feature applies to Items as well.

3. On the Contents tab, select Item or Service, and fill in the other details.

Details

• Was

Displays the content from the base document (original invoice or correction invoice). The fields in this
section are not editable and show the original values for fields such as item number, item description,
quantity, unit price, discount, tax code, and total.

• Should Be

Enter the information that you want to correct. You can edit fields such as quantity, unit price,
discount, tax code, and total to make the necessary corrections. The item number can't be modified.
You can add additional item lines if necessary.

The Total field in the header is updated according to the data entered on the Contents tab.

4. On the Logistics tab, you can specify the ship-to and pay-to addresses, and other settings under the

Preferences section.

1. You can assign to the purchase document a different address from the address already defined for the

business partner or define a new address.

2. When defining a new address, you can choose whether to save it to the business partner or to apply it

to the current purchase document only.

5. On the Accounting tab, set payment terms, payment method, and other relevant details.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. To add the new A/P correction invoice to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View,

Add & New, Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the A/P correction invoice, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar
on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions

1.5.14  A/P Correction Invoice Reversals

An A/P correction invoice reversal is a document that is used to cancel an A/P correction invoice.

Apps

When working with A/P correction invoice reversals, you can find the following apps:

• A/P Correction Invoice Reversals
• Create A/P Correction Invoice Reversal

 Note

A/P correction invoice reversals are available only in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Portugal, Russia,
Slovakia, and Ukraine localizations.

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter A/P correction invoice reversals.
• View and manage different views of A/P correction invoice reversal lists.
• View, edit, and create A/P correction invoice reversals.
• Copy an A/P correction invoice to a A/P correction invoice reversal.
• Create and process A/P correction invoice reversal drafts.

1.5.15.1  Managing Recurring Transaction Templates

Recurring transaction templates can be used to streamline business processes that repeat regularly.

To open the Recurring Transaction Templates list view, choose the Recurring Transaction Templates app on the
home page from the Sales, Purchasing, or Inventory Transactions groups.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

360

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of delivery records. The views store filter
settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays recurring transaction templates that have been

created by the current user and whose validity date is in the future.

• All Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all the recurring transaction templates that are available in

the system for localization, including those with validity dates in the past and in the future.

• Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all recurring transaction templates available in the system

for the localization, with their validity date in the future.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

Performing Business Actions

Use the options in the table toolbar to perform the following actions:

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Table Toolbar [page 68].

BP Properties Choose whether to ignore business partner properties when filtering the templates. The

default selection is Yes. If you select No, select the properties you want to filter from the list
and choose Update.

Select one or more business partner properties as the filtering criteria to display the
templates.

SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

361

Features of Recurring Transaction Templates List View

You can create new templates, or edit, delete, or duplicate existing templates. With the templates and their
recurrence details, recurring transaction instances are recorded, and execution is based on the templates you
define. For more information on executing recurring transactions, see Managing Recurring Transactions [page
219].

Creating Recurring Transaction Template

1. Choose Create located in the table toolbar.

2. On the General tab, specify the relevant information, including the template name, document type,

document number, recurrence period, start date, and valid-until date.

 Note

The valid-until date is optional and can be added later.

Recurrence
Period

Choose the intervals at which you want the recurring transaction to be repeated. The
following options are available: Daily, Weekly, Every 2 Weeks, Monthly, Every 2 Months,
Quarterly, Semiannually, Annually, and One Time.

After you enter the interval and a start date for the transaction, the date for the next
execution and the total number of instances are automatically displayed.

3. On the Contents tab, review the information that was auto-populated.

4. To save the record to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New, or Add &

Back.

1.5.15.2  Managing Recurring Transactions

Recurring transactions are business transactions that are regularly entered into the system with the same
frequency, or the customer has a subscription and pays for it regularly (for example, monthly).

To open the Manage Recurring Transactions list view, choose the Recurring Transactions tile on the home page
from the Sales, Purchasing, or Inventory Transactions groups.

List views in the SAP Business One, Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to
restrict the data records currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records.

• My Recurring Transactions on Execution displays recurring transactions created by the current user that

that day.

Features of Recurring Transactions List View

The list view contains all the recurring transactions that are currently due, and those that were due in the past
but are pending execution.

Based on the recurrence information, individual recurring transaction instances are generated in the list view,
so that you can execute the transactions individually or in batches.

Only when you have full authorizations for recurring transactions, and for the related document types, can you
post and create recurring transactions.

You can carry out the following tasks in this tile:

• Execute recurring transactions.
• Choose the system response if data is missing in any of the recurring transaction templates.
• Filter the list view entries based on their start date, valid until date, and business partner details.
• Remove single or multiple recurring transactions.

1.5.16  Managing Drafts

You can create and process draft documents of sales documents, purchasing documents, payments
documents, and inventory documents.

To create a draft document, click the Create... tile of the relevant object, for example, Create A/R Invoice or
Create Purchase Quotation, or Create Outgoing Payment for Business Partner, enter all relevant details and then
choose one of the following options in the multi-choice button:

Save as Draft & New Adds the draft document and opens the document detailed view in Create mode for

creating another document in sequence.

Save as Draft & View Adds the draft document and has it displayed for further review.

Delete

1.5.17  Managing Documents in Approval Process

When trying to add or update a document that triggers an approval process, you see that this document is
saved as a draft. After the authorizers approve the draft in the Manage Approval Decisions list view, you can
continue adding or updating the draft.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales orders, sales quotations, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, returns,
A/R credit memos, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve invoices, goods receipt POs, goods
returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods issues, outgoing payments, inventory transfers, and inventory
transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When creating or updating a document in Web client, you are notified by the system that an approval is

required.

366

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

2. You become the originator of the approval process and a draft is created.

3. The authorizers review the draft and either approve or reject the request in the Manage Approval Decisions

list view.

4. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer.

5. To view the approval status and proceed with the process, click the Docs in Approval Process tile; the
Manage Docs in Approval Process list view opens. (Alternatively, you can access the draft from the
notification as well.)

 Note

For the outgoing payments approval process, there is a separate list view: Manage Outgoing Payments
in Approval Process.

In the list view you can:

• Filter, sort, group, and access the relevant drafts
• Add approved drafts
• Cancel approval processes for selected drafts
• Restore approval processes for selected drafts

6. Depending on the approval status, you can either generate a document (choose  Edit Add & View ) or

update the draft (choose Edit) to trigger a new approval process.

Related Information

Approval Decisions [page 226]

1.5.18  Approval Decisions

When a user triggers an approval process, as the authorizer, you can see all the draft documents for approval in
the Approval Decisions list view and decide what to do with those requests.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales quotations, sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, return
requests, returns, A/R credit memos, purchase requests, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

367

invoices, goods receipt POs, goods return requests, goods returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods
issues, goods receipts, inventory transfers, and inventory transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When a user that is creating or updating a document triggers an approval process, you as an authorizer are

notified by the system that your approval is required.

 Note

You can choose to also get those notifications by email. See Approval Process Settings [page 715]

2. You become the authorizer of the approval process for the draft that was created.

3. To review the requests for approval, click the Approval Decisions tile; the Manage Approval Decisions list

view opens. The requests for approval that match the selected view are displayed. The default view is My
Pending Requests for Approval.

4. You can perform the following actions:

• Choose another view or apply different filters and view settings to fine tune the displayed list.
• Select one or more requests for approval and apply the relevant action. You can choose to approve or

reject the request.

5. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer and can

proceed with the process. See Managing Documents in Approval Process [page 225]

1.5.19  Managing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations

You can work with batches, serial numbers and bin locations in relevant marketing documents and inventory
documents.

In this case, both outgoing and incoming batches, serial numbers and bin locations are available.

There are two scenarios where you work on the outgoing side:

• Inventory issue documents, for example, deliveries.
• Inventory issue lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an incoming document. For example,

on a line of a goods receipt PO, the quantity is minus 100.

For more information, see Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 227].

Likewise, there are two scenarios where you work on the incoming side:

• Inventory receipt documents, for example, A/P invoices.
• Inventory receipt lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an outgoing document. For example,

on a line of an A/R invoice, the quantity is minus 50.

For more information, see Incoming Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 229].

1.5.19.2.1  Automatically Creating Batches and Serial

Numbers

When you need to create a large amount of batches or serial numbers, you can use the automatic creation
function. For inventory counting transactions, the newly created serial/batch numbers are stored in the system
as drafts.

Prerequisites

You are working with items managed by batches or serial numbers.

Context

To access the Automatic Creation button, you can do either of the following:

• On the Contents tab of the detailed view in relevant documents (except inventory counting transactions),

choose the  Value Help icon in the Serial/Batch Numbers field.

• On the Counting tab of the detailed view in inventory counting transactions, choose the  Value Help icon

in the Counted Qty field.

 Note

• For A/R returns and A/R credit memos, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Serial/Batch

Numbers field, and then in the center right of the opened dialog box, select the Create button.
If bin location-enabled warehouses are selected on the line, you can also choose the value help icons in
the Bin Location Allocation and Bin Locations fields.

• For inventory counting transactions, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Counted Qty

field, and then in the center right of the dialog box, select the Create button.
When you work with team counters, the dialog box is also accessible through the value help icon in the
Team Total Counted Qty field.

Procedure

1. Click the Automatic Creation button. A dialog box opens up.

2. (Optional) In the Bin Location field, specify the bin location to store your batches or serial numbers.

3. For batch items, in the field No. of Batches, specify how many batches you want to create.

4.

5.

6.

In the Batch or Serial Number field, choose the value help icon. The dialog box Automatic String Creation
opens up.

Input strings for batches or serial numbers.

In the Type column, choose String or Number.

7.

If you choose the Number type, in the Operations column, you can define one of the following operations
for the numbers: No Operations, Increase, and Decrease. The operations are performed during the

displayed in the Final String field.

1.5.20  Procurement Confirmation Wizard

Apps

When working with the procurement confirmation wizard, choose the Procurement Confirmation Wizard app

on the home page. Alternatively, choose  Purchasing Procurement Confirmation Wizard  or  Production

Procurement Confirmation Wizard  in the Main Menu.

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with this app:

• Create one or more target documents, such as purchasing documents or production orders, directly from
one or more base documents such as sales orders, sales quotations, or production orders. Procurement
documents created using this function can include part or all of the items from the base sales or
production documents.

• Combine several base documents into a single target document for a vendor.

1.5.20.1  Creating Purchase Orders from Sales Orders

Context

You can create a purchase order directly from a sales order following these steps:

Procedure

1. Create a sales order specifying customer and item information. In the Logistics tab, select the checkbox

Procure Non-Drop-Ship Items.

 Note

Alternatively, you can edit an existing sales order and select the Procure Non-Drop-Ship Items checkbox
in the Logistics tab.

2. After you add or update the sales order, the Procurement Confirmation Wizard opens.

3. The wizard displays the Base Document and Business Partners fields, pre-filled with customer details from

the selected sales order. You can add business partners if required.

4. To create purchase orders for all open sales orders with unfulfilled purchase quantities for selected

business partners, select the Include All Open Base Documents checkbox.

5. Choose Next. All open sales orders are listed for you to select.

6.

In the Base Document Lines step, choose Purchase Order as the Target Document. Make sure all items have
a vendor assigned to them. If an item has a preferred vendor, this vendor is already entered in the line. If
required, change the vendor code. The other details are automatically filled in.

7. To save the purchase order as a draft, select the Create Draft Document checkbox.

8. Choose Next.

9.

In the Consolidation step, specify whether to consolidate the purchase requirements from multiple sales
orders into one purchase order, and which consolidation options to apply.

 Note

If you choose No Consolidation, the documents are grouped by vendor, that is, one purchase order is
created per vendor.

10. Specify the system response to errors that may occur in the document generation process in the If an Error

Occurs dropdown list. You can select either Skip to Next Vendor (default option) or Stop Execution.

11. Choose Next. The Results Preview displays the details of all purchase orders that will be created. The

purchase orders are grouped by vendor and the consolidations options you selected.

12. To generate the documents, choose Execute Now.

13. The Summary Report displays all the documents that have been created and any errors that have

occurred.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

375

1.5.20.2  Creating Procurement Documents from Production

Orders

Context

You can create purchase orders, purchase quotations, or purchase requests from a production order.
Alternatively, you can procure components directly for a production order to ensure availability for the
production process. By creating procurement documents based on actual production requirements, you can
better maintain minimum inventory levels and support efficient production planning.

Procedure

1. Create a production order specifying the product information. On the General tab, select the Procure Items
checkbox. The Components tab is updated with the Allow Procurement Doc. column checked for the item
entries.

2. Add the production order, and the Procurement Confirmation Wizard opens.

3.

In the Base Document Type step, the product number and description fields are prefilled based on the
production order. You can select more products for which you want to generate procurement documents.

4. Select the checkbox Include All Open Base Documents to ensure all related open documents for the

selected products are displayed in the next step.

5. Choose Next and select the base documents from which you want to generate procurement documents.

6. Choose Next. In the Base Document Lines step, select one of the following options as the target document

type: Purchase Order, Purchase Quotation, or Purchase Request.

7.

If an item has a preferred vendor, this vendor is already entered in the line. If required, change the vendor
code. The other fields are automatically filled in.

8. To create the procurement document as a draft, select the Create Draft Document checkbox.

9. Choose Next. In the Consolidation step, specify whether to consolidate the purchase requirements from
multiple production orders into one purchasing document, and which consolidation options to apply.

 Note

If you choose No Consolidation, the documents are grouped by vendor, that is, one purchasing
document is created per vendor.

10. Specify the system response to errors that may occur in the document generation process in the If an Error

Occurs dropdown list. You can select either Skip to Next Vendor (default option) or Stop Execution.

11. Choose Next. The Results Preview displays the details of all purchasing documents that will be created. The

purchasing documents are grouped by vendor and the consolidations options you selected.

12. To generate the documents, choose Execute Now.

13. The Summary Report displays all the documents that have been created and any errors that have

occurred.

1.6.1.1  Managing Business Partners

To open the Manage Business Partners list view, click the Business Partners tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for business partners, see Working with Business Partners [page
380].

Selecting Views

The Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of business partner records. The views
store filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, Open) to determine
which records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views
menu in the top-left corner of the header area:

• Customers displays all the customers of the company.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Business Partners displays all the business partners of the company.
• Business Partner Addresses displays all the business partner addresses grouped by business partners.
• Business Partner Contact Persons displays all the contact persons grouped by business partners.
• Leads displays all the leads of the company.
• Vendors displays all the vendors of the company.

1.6.1.2  Working with Business Partners

The detailed view in the Web client allows you to view and work with all relevant details for the record in one
place. The header area contains key information about the specific data record and business action buttons,
while the content area displays related fields structured with a series of tabs. When you open a data record in
the detailed view, it is displayed in view mode.

Viewing Key Record Information

Below the business partner record number, the header displays key information about the business record.

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Account
Balance

It is the bookkeeping balance of the customer or vendor account. The Web client updates the
value automatically whenever an amount is posted to the business partner’s account.

 Note

Not relevant for leads.

Deliveries It is the value of open deliveries that are not yet fully copied into A/R invoices, returns, or closed.
The Web client updates the value automatically whenever a new delivery is added or the status of
existing deliveries is changed.

 Note

Relevant for customers only.

Orders It is the value of open sales orders that are not yet delivered, canceled or closed. The Web client
updates the value whenever a sales order is created or if a delivery or an invoice is created on the
basis of a sales order.

 Note

Not relevant for vendors.

Checks Balance It displays the value of the open checks not yet deposited, endorsed or canceled for the

customer.

Credit Limit
Utilization

This progress bar shows the current progress of credit limit utilization for the customer. It is

only displayed when the Credit Limit checkbox is selected on the  Administration System

Initialization General Settings BP  tab in the SAP Business One client.

380

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

The progress bar shows red with no percentage when:

• The Credit Limit value for this business partner is set to zero.
• And the Account Balance value for this business partner is greatrer than zero.

Performing Business Actions

You can perform the following actions using the toolbar on the right side of the header:

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Delete Deletes this business partners from the company database, but only if no open transactions exist and

the balances are zero.

Create Creates activities, opportunities, service calls, marketing documents, incoming and outgoing

payments for the current business partner.

 Note

If the business partner is inactive, you can only create activities and drafts for marketing
documents and payments. Opportunities and service calls cannot be created for inactive
business partners.

BP Catalog Numbers Opens the Business Partner Catalog Numbers page filtered by this business partner.

Working with the Record Content

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide general information about the business partner.

Currency If you wish to define a multi-currency business partner, in create or edit mode, select All Currencies
in the Currency field. In this case, you can choose the Show All Currencies link and do the following:

• To set the default currency, select the radio button in the Default column of the relevant

currency. The default currency will be set in new marketing documents and payments of this
business partner. If required, you can change the currency in the document itself.

• To define which currencies will be hidden for the specific business partner’s documents,
deselect the check box in the Include column for each currency you wish to hide for this
business partner. Based on this definition, you will see in the specific business partner
marketing documents and payments documents only the included currencies.

When you upload an attachment, it is saved to the default target path folder set by your system

Business One client.

• When default subfolders are assigned per user in User Defaults in the SAP Business One

client, all attachments are automatically saved to that user’s default folder. In this scenario,
the Subfolder Path field is not editable.

• If no default attachment folder is assigned per user, you can manually specify a subfolder

in the Subfolder Path field, and all uploaded attachments for the document will be stored in
that location.

File Name If you upload a file that has the same name as an existing attachment, a timestamp will be

automatically appended to the file name.

File Size View the size of the attachments.

Make sure that the attachment size is smaller than 20 MB. For files with a size equal to or larger
than 20 MB, you can upload them through the SAP Business One client.

1.6.1.2.1

Creating Business Partners

Procedure

1. To create a new business partner, click the Create Business Partner tile.

2. On the General tab, enter all relevant business partner data.

Note that Code is a mandatory field.

3. On the Contact Person tab, enter the details of the contacts and set the default contact person.

4. On the Address tab, enter the bill-to/pay-to and ship-to addresses.

5. On the Properties tab, assign predefined properties to the business partner.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. On the User-Defined Fields tab, enter relevant detailes in the user-defined fields (UDFs) defined for

business partners.

8. To add the new business partner to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back. For more information, see Apps for Creating Records [page 89].

1.6.1.2.2

Verifying VAT Numbers for Business Partners

Prerequisites

 Note

This function is only available in the European Union, Norway, Switzerland, and the UK localizations.

You have done the following in the SAP Business One client.

• You have selected the Verify VAT Numbers for Business Partners and Documents checkbox on the BP tab of

the General Settings window ( Administration System Initialization General Settings ).

• You have full authorization for Verify VAT Numbers under Business Partners in the Authorizations window
( Administration System Initialization Authorizations General Authorizations ). This entry only

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

385

appears after you select the Verify VAT Numbers for Business Partners and Documents checkbox on the BP
tab of the General Settings window.

Context

You can verify business partners’ VAT numbers with VIES in one of the following ways.

• In the list view, in the table toolbar, choose the Verify VAT Numbers button to verify all the VAT numbers for

business partners of your choice.

• In the edit mode of the detailed view, on the General tab, choose the Verify VAT Number button to verify the

VAT number of the default ship-to address for the current business partner.

• In the edit mode of the detailed view, on the Addresses tab, choose the Verify VAT Numbers button to verify

the VAT numbers of the ship-to addresses of your choice.

Results

You can view the verification status or response details from VIES in one of the following ways.

• In the list view, choose View Settings to enable the response-related columns. They provide you with the

response details from VIES for the VAT numbers of the default ship-to addresses.

• In the detailed view, on the General tab, choose the status icon to view the response details from VIES for

the VAT number of the default ship-to address.

• In the detailed view, on the Addresses tab, the VAT Number Verification column provides you with the

verification statuses of the VAT numbers for all the ship-to addresses.

1.6.1.2.3

Preparing a Microsoft Excel Import File for
Business Partners

Context

You can import business partner records from Microsoft Excel files to a company in SAP Business One, Web
client. The data is copied from the Microsoft Excel files to the corresponding fields in Web client.

This feature allows for both single and mass uploads, with each row in the file becoming a distinct business
partner object. You can perform the import using:

• A single file with one sheet, which supports importing the parent object only, or any one child object only.
• A single file with multiple sheets, which supports importing the parent and child objects together, or child

objects only.

386

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Multiple files with single sheets, which supports importing the parent and child objects together, or child

objects only.

You can also export the data shown in the Preview section by choosing the  Export to Microsoft Excel icon.
You can choose to export data for only the current object, which downloads a single‑sheet Microsoft Excel file,
or export data for all available objects together, which downloads one Microsoft Excel file containing multiple
sheets, with each sheet representing a different object.

For more information on the import process, see Importing from Microsoft Excel [page 881].

Fields to Import

When you import data from Microsoft Excel, you can choose to upload the main business partner record,
known as the parent object, or the related child objects that store supporting details. Business Partner Master
Data supports four child objects:

• Contact Person
• Bill-to and Ship-to Address
• Payment Method
• Account Receivable

When you select a child object in the field mapping step, all available fields for that child object appear
automatically in the mapping table.

If your Microsoft Excel file contains a header row with field names, select the corresponding checkbox File
Contains Header so that the system reads the first row as a header. If the checkbox is not selected, the system
treats the first row as data.

To import your business partner records from Microsoft Excel into SAP Business One, Web client, you must
define the Microsoft Excel fields based on certain rules. These fields must follow certain rules; otherwise, the
import will fail.

When importing data from a Microsoft Excel file, the checkbox Create Related Objects enables the system
to automatically create new objects when the uploaded file contains a value that is not yet defined in the
database. If such a value is detected during the import process, the system will create the corresponding new
object automatically. The Create Related Objects function supports automatic creation for the following fields:

• Group Code (OCRD.GroupCode)
• BP Currency (OCRD.Currency)
• Sales Employee / Buyer (OCRD.SlpCode)
• Shipping Type (OCRD.ShipType)
• Factoring Indicator (OCRD.Indicator)
• Business Partner Project (OCRD.ProjectCod)
• Industry (OCRD.IndustryC)
• Priority (OCRD.Priority)
• User-Defined Fields (UDFs) – Business Partner Master Data
• User-Defined Fields (UDFs) – Business Partner Contact Persons
• User-Defined Fields (UDFs) – Business Partner Addresses

1.6.2.1  Managing Activities

To open the Managing Activities list view, click the Activities tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for activities, see Working with Activities [page 402].

400

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Selecting Views

The Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of activity records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Activities displays all the open activities created by the user who is currently logged in.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Activities displays all the activities of the company.
• My Activities displays all the activities created by the user who is currently logged in.
• My Closed Activities displays all the closed activities created by the user who is currently logged in.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Assigned To When the values in this filter are included in the Assigned To users, recipient lists or multiple

recipients of activities, those records appear in the table area.

 Note

If the activity is assigned to an employee, you need to use the Assigned Employee filter.

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

1.6.2.2  Working with Activities

The detailed view in the Web client allows you to view and work with all relevant details for the record in one
place. The header area contains key information about the specific data record and business action buttons,
while the content area displays related fields structured with a series of tabs. When you open a data record in
the detailed view, it is displayed in view mode.

Viewing Key Record Information

Below the activity record number, the header displays key information about the business record.

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Activity
Type

The page appears differently based on the different activity types: Phone Call, Meeting, Task,
Email, Note, Campaign and Other.

For Email type activities, when you choose Send by Email from the Share menu, the system will
draft an email to all specified recipients using the defined subject and content with the default
email app of your operating system. The activity status will then update to Emailed, and further
edits to this activity will not be possible. This type of activity does not appear in the calendar of the
SAP Business One client.

Subject

Short description of the activity. For Email type activities, this is the email subject.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
