1.6.2.2.1

Creating Activities

Procedure

1. To create a new activity, click the Create Activity tile.

2. On the General tab, in the Type dropdown list, select the activity types: Phone Call, Meeting, Task, Email,

Note, Campaign, and Other.

For Email type activities, in the view mode of detailed view, when you choose Send by Email from the Share
menu, the system will draft an email to all specified recipients using the defined subject and content with
the default email app of your operating system. The activity status will then update to Emailed, and further
edits to this activity will not be possible. This type of activity does not appear in the calendar of the SAP
Business One client.

3. On the General tab, in the Subject field, describe the activity shortly. For Email type activities, define the

email subject.

4. On the General tab, in the Assigned To dropdown list, select the following that are handling the activity:

• User
• Employee
• Recipient List: this option appears when you have defined recipient lists. Only active recipient lists

appear for selection.
You can also create a new recipient list directly from the activity. From the recipient list selection dialog
box, choose Create. In the Recipients List dialog box that appears, add the recipients and choose Add.

• Multiple Recipients: select a combination of users, employees or recipient lists.

By default, the user who created the activity is displayed.

 Note

Employees that are linked to users are only displayed as users in the user list. When all employees are
linked to users, or there is no employee, you can assign the activity to a user only.

When an employee is linked to a user, the activities originally assigned to the employee are
automatically assigned to the user instead of the employee.

5. On the Scheduling tab, set a date, time and location for the activity:

• In the Time section, enter a date and time, and set a reminder if needed.
• In the Meeting Location field, you can choose the business partner address.
• In the Recurrence Information section, the settings are different based on different values of

Recurrence: None, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Annually.

6. On the Content tab, describe the activity, or provide any other event that took place during the activity. You
can enter long text and insert predefined text as needed. For Email type activities, define the email body.

7. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

8. To add the new activity to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New, Add

& Back. For more information, see Apps for Creating Records [page 89].

1.6.3  Managing Business Partner Catalog Numbers by BP

Click the Business Partner Catalog Numbers by BP tile to open the Business Partner Catalog Numbersby BP
page in view mode. The catalog numbers are grouped by business partners. Here you can filter, sort, expand,
and collapse the BP catalog number records.

To enter the edit mode, above the table area on the right, choose Edit. Here you can create, edit, and delete a
business partner catalog number:

• To create a catalog number, in the table, specify a business partner and item for which you want to create a

catalog number, and enter the catalog number.

• To set a default catalog number for a specific BP and specific item, select the Default radio button in that

row.

• To duplicate an item row, including the catalog number information, select the item row, choose Duplicate

Item above the table area on the right.

• To delete all catalog numbers related to a specific business partner, select the BP row and choose Delete

above the table area on the right.

 Note

The deletion is irreversible after you choose Save.

• To delete a catalog number related to a specific business partner and specific item, select the item row

under the business partner and choose Delete above the table area on the right.

 Note

The deletion is irreversible after you choose Save.

To save all the changes to the catalog numbers, choose Save.

1.6.4  Scanning Business Cards

With the Scan Business Card app, you can create a business partner or a contact person for a business partner
by selecting a photo or taking a picture of a business card with an IOS device, such as an iPad.

The app supports the following languages of business cards: Chinese simplified, Chinese traditional, Dutch,
English, French, German, Hebrew, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish.

1.7.3  Managing Drafts

You can create and process draft documents of sales documents, purchasing documents, payments
documents, and inventory documents.

To create a draft document, click the Create... tile of the relevant object, for example, Create A/R Invoice or
Create Purchase Quotation, or Create Outgoing Payment for Business Partner, enter all relevant details and then
choose one of the following options in the multi-choice button:

Save as Draft & New Adds the draft document and opens the document detailed view in Create mode for

creating another document in sequence.

Save as Draft & View Adds the draft document and has it displayed for further review.

In the list views of draft documents, such as the Manage Sales & Purchasing Drafts list view, the Manage
Incoming & Outgoing Payments Drafts list view, or the Manage Inventory Transactions Drafts list view, you can
perform the following tasks for single or multiple drafts:

Delete

Deletes the selected drafts from the database.

Close

Sets the status of the drafts as Closed.

Reopen Opens closed drafts and changes the status of open drafts to Closed, as in list view.

Add

Adds the drafts as official documents.

Add and Delete

Adds the drafts as official documents and deletes them from the database.

Preview, Print, Choose
Layout and Preview,
Choose Layout and Print

Preview or print one or more drafts in the default or a different Crystal Reports
layout.

 Note

The Print and Choose Layout and Print options are only available for sales and
purchasing drafts.

By default, the list view shows drafts created by the current user.

To view a certain draft, choose its row. The header displays the status Draft for all drafts, whether open or
closed. The following actions are available:

Delete

Choose this button to delete the draft.

Reopen / Close Changes the draft status from Closed to Open for closed drafts or from Open to Closed for

open drafts.

New Activity Creates an activity for the business partner that appears in the draft. The draft is automatically

added to the Linked Document section of the activity.

Related Activities

Opens a list view showing the activities created for the given draft.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

417

Preview, Print, Choose
Layout and Preview,
Choose Layout and Print

Preview or print the draft in the default or a different Crystal Reports layout.

 Note

The Print and Choose Layout and Print options are only available for sales
and purchasing drafts.

As with other documents, when you open a draft with draft status Open, it appears in View mode. You need to
choose Edit in order to switch to the Create mode.

After editing the draft, you can save it as an official document, or as a draft, the same as when creating a new
document.

 Note

• Sales documents are created in SAP Business One, Web client with a generation type of Not Relevant

that is only visible on the Electronic Documents tab in the SAP Business One client. To process
documents created in SAP Business One, Web client as electronic documents, you must manually
adjust the generation type in the SAP Business One client. For more information about working with
electronic documents, see the online help for SAP Business One.

• In the following scenario, you receive a confirmation message with the existing draft numbers and are

asked whether to continue with the process:

1. You use the Copy To or Copy From function to add one or more base sales or purchasing

documents to a target document.

2.

If approval isn’t required, you use the Save as Draft function to save the target document. If
approval is required, the system automatically creates a draft after you add the document, pending
approval.

3. You (or another user) use the Copy To or Copy From function to copy the same base documents to

another target document again.

4. You (or another user) try to add the target document, save the target document as a draft again, or

add the target document for approval again.

Before making your decision, you can open the Sales & Purchasing Drafts app in the Web client to view
details of the existing drafts using the provided draft numbers.

1.7.4  Managing Documents in Approval Process

When trying to add or update a document that triggers an approval process, you see that this document is
saved as a draft. After the authorizers approve the draft in the Manage Approval Decisions list view, you can
continue adding or updating the draft.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

418

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Context

This function supports sales orders, sales quotations, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, returns,
A/R credit memos, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve invoices, goods receipt POs, goods
returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods issues, outgoing payments, inventory transfers, and inventory
transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When creating or updating a document in Web client, you are notified by the system that an approval is

required.

2. You become the originator of the approval process and a draft is created.

3. The authorizers review the draft and either approve or reject the request in the Manage Approval Decisions

list view.

4. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer.

5. To view the approval status and proceed with the process, click the Docs in Approval Process tile; the
Manage Docs in Approval Process list view opens. (Alternatively, you can access the draft from the
notification as well.)

 Note

For the outgoing payments approval process, there is a separate list view: Manage Outgoing Payments
in Approval Process.

In the list view you can:

• Filter, sort, group, and access the relevant drafts
• Add approved drafts
• Cancel approval processes for selected drafts
• Restore approval processes for selected drafts

6. Depending on the approval status, you can either generate a document (choose  Edit Add & View ) or

update the draft (choose Edit) to trigger a new approval process.

Related Information

Approval Decisions [page 226]

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

419

1.7.5  Approval Decisions

When a user triggers an approval process, as the authorizer, you can see all the draft documents for approval in
the Approval Decisions list view and decide what to do with those requests.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales quotations, sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, return
requests, returns, A/R credit memos, purchase requests, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve
invoices, goods receipt POs, goods return requests, goods returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods
issues, goods receipts, inventory transfers, and inventory transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When a user that is creating or updating a document triggers an approval process, you as an authorizer are

notified by the system that your approval is required.

 Note

You can choose to also get those notifications by email. See Approval Process Settings [page 715]

2. You become the authorizer of the approval process for the draft that was created.

3. To review the requests for approval, click the Approval Decisions tile; the Manage Approval Decisions list

view opens. The requests for approval that match the selected view are displayed. The default view is My
Pending Requests for Approval.

4. You can perform the following actions:

• Choose another view or apply different filters and view settings to fine tune the displayed list.
• Select one or more requests for approval and apply the relevant action. You can choose to approve or

reject the request.

5. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer and can

proceed with the process. See Managing Documents in Approval Process [page 225]

top-left corner of the header area:

1.7.7.1

Endorsing Checks

Context

The check endorsement function enables you to forward an incoming check (for example, from a customer) to
a third party (a vendor) without having to deposit it first. Only checks that are not canceled or deposited can be
endorsed. Follow these steps to endorse a check:

Procedure

1. Choose Check Register on the home page.

2.

In the selection criteria, select No for Endorsed and Not Deposited for Deposit Status.

3. Choose the check you want to endorse. The detailed information of the check is displayed in a detailed

pane on the right side of the check register.

4. Choose Edit in the detailed pane.

5. Choose  Endorse in the top right corner.

 Note

If the check is not endorsable, you can set Endorsable to Yes in the General tab and update the check.

6. The Journal Entry window opens. The first line is auto populated, and the check fund account is credited.

Add another line to enter the debit details.

 Note

You can use  Ctrl  +   B  to auto populate the debit amount in the second line.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

423

7. Choose Add & View or Add & Back to add the journal entry.

Related Information

Check Register [page 422]

Canceling Checks [page 424]

1.7.7.2

Canceling Checks

Context

Follow these steps to cancel non-deposited and deposited checks that were received as incoming payment
documents.

Canceling deposited checks

1. Choose Check Register on the home page.

2.

In the selection criteria, choose Not Deposited for Deposit Status.

3. Choose the check you want to cancel and choose Edit in the detailed pane.
4. Select Cancel Check from the Cancel dropdown list.

Canceling Non-
Deposited Checks

 Note

1. Choose Check Register on the home page.

2.

In the selection criteria, choose Deposited for Deposit Status in the selection criteria.

3. Choose the check you want to cancel and choose Edit in the detailed pane.
4.

In the Cancel  options, select either Cancel Deposit or Cancel Deposit and Payment.

If the current system date does not match the original document date, the Cancellation Options dialog box
appears. Choose one of the following:

• Current System Date: Applies the current date as the transaction date of the cancellation.
• Original Document Date: Applies the same posting date, due date, and document date as the canceled

document.

Results

A reverse journal entry is created to cancel the journal entry created when the incoming payment was added.
The date assigned to this transaction is according to the selection you made in the Cancellation Options dialog
box.

424

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

For deposited check cancellation, a reverse deposit document of a negative amount is created. The date
assigned to this deposit is according to the selection you made in the Cancellation Options dialog box. It
contains only the check you have chosen to cancel.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

 Note

If you need to edit certain information that cannot be edited through Web client, please edit it from the SAP
Business One client.

Viewing Key Record Information

Below the item master data record number, the header displays the image of the item and in stock, committed,
ordered, and available quantities. For more information, see Header Area [page 54].

Performing Business Actions

You can perform the following actions using the toolbar on the right side of the header:

 Note

This section documents app-specific business actions. For generic options, see Header Area [page 83].

Delete

Deletes the item from the company database.

 Note

Only items with no transactions can be removed.

Duplicate Duplicate the item master data record.

You can choose not to duplicate bar codes while duplicating items by deselecting the Duplicate Bar

Codes While Duplicating Items checkbox in the  Administration

 System Initialization

Settings

 Inventory Item  tab of the SAP Business One client.

Displays activities created for this item.

Create
Activity

The Activity form appears, with the preferred vendor of the item populated in the Business
Partner field and the item code appearing on the Linked Document tab.

all warehouses.

Working with the Record Content

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide general information about the item: its number, description, type, group, and so
on.

Logistics Tab

The fields on this tab provide logistics information about the item.

Manage
Item By

Warranty
Template

The methods by which you receive and release items:

• None (default) – no special management for this item.
• Serial Numbers – the item is managed by serial numbers.
• Batches – the item is managed by batches. This type of management tracks items that have
unique numbers and characteristics but have been combined in a single group, for example,
pharmaceutical products.

This section is displayed only when your item is managed by serial numbers.

If you have predefined contract templates for the item in the Contract Templates page ( Main

Menu Administration Configuration Service Contract Templates ), you can select a
warranty contract template from the Warranty Template dropdown list here.

When you create an A/R invoice or a delivery for this item, Web client automatically creates a
contract for the customer with the template that you select for this item. You don’t need to define
all fields in the contract manually.

Bar
Codes

You can add new bar codes by entering bar codes and their descriptions for the selected UoM.
Multiple bar codes are allowed for each single UoM of an item. The application sets the first bar
code as the default bar code for the corresponding UoM. Updating or deleting a bar code does not
affect the previous transactions in which the bar code was used.

Purchasing Tab

The fields on this tab provide purchasing-related information, such as regular vendor details, purchasing unit,
unit of measurement, and measurement details.

Business One Service Layer.

Path

When you upload an attachment, it is saved to the default target path folder set by your system
administrators. Your access to the attachment folder is granted through Authorizations in the SAP
Business One client.

• When default subfolders are assigned per user in User Defaults in the SAP Business One

the Subfolder Path field is not editable.

in the Subfolder Path field, and all uploaded attachments for the document will be stored in
that location.

1.9.2.1

Creating Items

Context

You can create items to be used for sales, purchasing, manufacturing, and inventory. Item types include items,
labor, and travel.

Procedure

1. To create a new item, choose one of the following options:

• From the Manage Items list view, choose the Create button.
• From an existing item, choose the New button.
• Click the Create Item tile.
• Click the Create Item entry in the main menu.

2. On the General tab, enter all relevant data:
• Note that Item No. is a mandatory field.
• Choose  Upload to upload an item image; it will be displayed in the item’s header.

3. On the Logistics tab, set the serial or batch numbers management method for the item and add bar codes,

if used.

When the UoM group is Manual, there is no concept of inventory UoM, so the bar code displayed in the
table is the default bar code for the specific item.

In the case of items with a UoM group other than Manual, you can select the UoM and define the bar codes
for the UoMs.

4. On the Purchasing and Sales tabs, enter relevant measurements.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

437

In the case of items with a UoM group other than Manual, these tabs display a table form for defining the
UoM and Package Types.

You can add a new line, remove lines, and define a default UoM and package type.

You can create QR (Quick Response) codes for items in the Create QR Code From field on the Sales tab.
QR code information can be added manually, by DI input, or by using a formula in a formatted search. The
source for QR codes can also be user-defined fields that are called by API.

5. On the Tax tab, you can set tax information for the item.

6. On the Inventory tab, set weight, valuation method, and manage warehouses values.

7. On the Pricing tab, you can define a price for the item for the relevant units of measure, pricing units, and

price lists.

In the case of items with a UoM group other than Manual, you can set prices for other defined UoMs by
adding new rows to the grid.

8. On the Properties tab, select the checkboxes of the item properties you need to include in the master data

record.

9. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

10. On the User-Defined Fields tab, you can enter relevant values for the listed UDFs.

11. To add the new item to the company database, choose the relevant button: Add & View, Add & New, or Add

& Back.

1.9.2.2  Preparing a Microsoft Excel Import File for Items

You can now import items data directly from a Microsoft Excel file into your SAP Business One, Web client. The
data is copied from the file to the corresponding fields in the Web client. You can only upload a single sheet
Microsoft Excel file for the import process. This feature allows for both single and mass uploads, allowing your
Microsoft Excel file to contain either one record or multiple records, with each row representing a separate Item
object.

You can also export the data shown in the Preview section by choosing the  Export to Microsoft Excel icon.

Fields to Import

When you import data from Microsoft Excel, you can choose to upload the main Item record, known as the
parent object, or the related child objects that store supporting details. Item Master Data supports two child
objects:

438

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Item Prices (ITM1)
• Item Warehouses (OITW)

Item Prices (ITM1) records can only be updated. New ITM1 records cannot be created. When you select a
sub-object menu line in the field mapping, all related fields for that sub-object will automatically appear in the
mapping table list.

The Microsoft Excel file sheet must contain a single object type, which can either be the parent object (Items
- OITM), the Item Prices (ITM1) child object, or the Item Warehouses (OITW) child object.

If your file includes a header row containing field names, select the checkbox File Contains Header so the
system interprets the first row as a header. If you do not select this checkbox, the system treats the first row as
data.

for each field.

1.9.3  Managing Alternative Items

To open Alternative Items in view mode, click the Alternative Items tile on the home page. Alternatively, choose

Item Management Alternative Items  in the Main Menu. Alternative items are defined by item. Here you

can filter, sort, expand, and collapse the item records.

To enter the edit mode, above the table area on the right, choose Edit. Here you can create, edit, and remove an
alternative item:

Creating an Alternative Item

1.

In the edit mode, choose Expand to expand all items to see the hierarchy of the defined alternative items.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

449

2. Go to the end of the item list, specify the item code for which you want to create an alternative item.

3. Specify the code for an alternative item.

You can specify multiple alternative items for an item.

4. Enter remarks, if required, and specify the Match Factor value. The higher the value, the more suitable the

match.

5. Choose Reverse Link to create a reverse relationship between the alternative item and the original item.

6. Choose Save.

Updating an Alternative Item

1.

In the edit mode, choose Expand to expand all items to see the hierarchy of the defined alternative items.

2. Go to the existing original item.

3. Add new alternative item rows or specify the Match Factor or Remarks field of an alternative item.

4. Choose Save.

Removing an Alternative Item

1.

In the edit mode, choose Expand to expand all items to see the hierarchy of the defined alternative items.

2. To remove all alternative items from an original item, select the original item row and choose Remove.

3. To remove an alternative item related to a specific original item, select the alternative item row under the

original item and choose Remove.

4. Choose Save.

1.9.3.1

Selecting Alternative Items

You can select an alternative item for a missing item when creating or editing an item type sales and purchasing
documents.

1.

In a sales or purchasing document, on the Contents tab, select Item in the Item/Service Type field.

2. From the Details section, in the Product table, enter an item number.
3. Click the  Settings icon to open the Select Columns dialog and select the Alternative Items column.

4. From the Alternative Items column, choose the button to open the Select Alternative Items dialog.

Warehouse Select a warehouse to view the quantities of the alternative items in the warehouse.

To view alternative items in all warehouses, leave the Warehouse field empty.

Price After Discount

Displays the price of the alternative item.

450

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

In Stock Displays the quantity of the alternative items in the warehouse. The value is displayed for the

warehouse selected above. If the field is empty, the total quantity of the alternative items in all
warehouses is displayed.

Match
Factor

Displays the value to specify the matching degree in points. A higher value represents a higher
match.

 Example

Item 1001 has two alternative items: 1002 and 1003. The matching factor defined for item
1002 is 100 and for item 1003 is 80. If there is no item 1001 in the warehouse, item 1002
can replace it, as it has the highest matching factor.

1.10

Inventory Transactions

The apps in the Inventory Transactions group allow you to optimize your inventory management and perform
various inventory transactions, including item movements and inventory counting. You can also save inventory
transactions as drafts and manage documents for approval.

The Inventory Transactions group includes apps that allow you to work with the following inventory transaction
documents: goods issues, goods receipts, inventory counting, inventory posting, inventory opening balances,
available-to-promise reports, inventory transfer requests, and inventory transfers.

1.10.1.2.1  Creating Goods Issues

Context

You can create a goods issue to decrease the inventory in situation that is not the direct result of adding a sales
document.

For example, when you find that some items have been damaged in a warehouse, you can remove the reduced
quantities by adding a goods issue.

Procedure

1. To create a new goods issue, click the Create Goods Issue tile.

2. On the General tab, select the relevant price list for the items.

3. On the Contents tab, enter the relevant items and fill in the items’ details.

4. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

5. To add the new goods issue to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the goods issue, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar on the
right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions are posted
to journal entries, for example, by another user, during the journal entry preview, the final journal entry
might differ from the one previewed.

 Note

Adding and editing goods issues is not supported in the India localization.

Performing Business Actions

Duplicate

Copy to
Inventory
Posting

Duplicate items and their information (including warehouse, bin locations, and single
UoM codes) to a new open counting document and exclude counting-related details. It’s
applicable to closed inventory counting documents and the closed document lines of open
counting documents.

Copies the current inventory counting document to a posting document. For documents
with multiple counters, select the set of counting results that you want to post.

 Note

For a counting document with multiple counters, you can only copy one set of counting
results to the inventory posting document. For example, if you choose to post the team’s
counting results or an individual counter's counting results, only the selected set of
counting results is copied.

Depending on the counting type and selected counters, the following copy options are
available:

• Total Counted Quantity: The system copies the sum of all team counters' counted

quantities for each item.

• Items with No Counters' Differences: The system copies only items for which all

counting results are the same.

468

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• <Individual Counter's> Counted Quantity: The system copies the selected individual

counter's counted quantity for each item.

To copy the counting results from a specific row of an inventory counting document to
the inventory posting document, ensure the following:

• The Counted checkbox in the row is selected.
• The counted quantity in the row is different from the in-warehouse quantity

recorded in the system.

 Note

If you select to calculate in-warehouse quantities based on the posting dates of inventory
transactions, the system may remind you of some newly posted inventory transactions
that should be taken into account. You can choose whether to update the in-warehouse
quantities based on the new transactions. For more information, , see Calculation of
In-Warehouse Quantities on Count Date.

After you add an inventory posting document based on inventory counting documents, rows
that are copied to the inventory posting document are automatically closed and items in
these rows are "unfrozen".

However, some rows may remain open if there is no difference between the in-warehouse
quantity on count date and the counted quantity. You cannot create new inventory counting
documents for the items in the open rows. Similarly, items in the open rows remain "frozen",
and you cannot record any inventory transaction for them. To resolve these issues, you must
manually close the rows in your base inventory counting documents.

To close these rows automatically, select the When Copying Inventory Counting to Inventory
Posting Close Counted Rows with Zero Diff. checkbox in the Inventory Document Settings tab

under  Administration Configuration

Inventory .

For more information, see the description about the checkbox When Copying Inventory
Counting to Inventory Posting Close Counted Rows with Zero Diff. in the Inventory Counting
Tab in Inventory Document Settings [page 768].

Relationship
Map

Provides an interactive representation of both the counting document and the related
posting document in one view, along with any other linked transactions.

Refer to Relationship Map [page 90] for more details.

Working with the Record Content

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide general information about the inventory counting and the referenced documents.

You can modify the following fields in edit mode on this tab:

Counting
Type

In the Web client, you can choose the following counting scenarios:

• A single counter
• Multiple counters

• Individual counting, where individual counters conduct independent counting of an item

at a storage location

• Team counting, where a group of counters' counting results of an item at a storage

location add up to its total quantity

• A combination of individual counting and team counting

In edit mode, you can switch counting types in either of the following ways. However, if the
document is copied to inventory posting, this field is disabled.

• From Single Counter to Multiple Counters

The setting When Changing from Single to Multiple Counters, Set Selected Counter As in

the SAP Business One client is considered under  Administration

 System Initialization

 Per Document

Document Settings
• When the radio button Individual Counter is selected, the first individual counter will be
updated with the counter name and the counted quantities of the single counter.
• When the radio button Team Counter is selected, the first team counter will be updated

 Inventory Counting .

with the counter name and the counted quantities of the single counter.

• From Multiple Counters to Single Counter

A dialog box appears and asks you to select, from a dropdown list, which count you want to
keep. In this case, you can only save one inventory count. The following rules apply:
• When there are only individual counters, all individual counters are displayed in the
dropdown list in the order of selections in the individual counter table. If you choose
one of the individual counters’ count, the Counter Name and Counted Qty of the single
counter will be updated accordingly.

 Example

You employed two individual counters to count a product. Individual Counter 1 A
counted 200, while Individual Counter 2 B counted 300. If you switch to Single
Counter and choose to keep the counting results of the first individual counter A, the
Counter Name and Counted Qty will be updated to A and 200 respectively.

• When there are only team counters, the dropdown list displays two options: Team

Counted Qty and Clear All Counts. If you choose the Team Counted Qty, the team’s total
counted quantity will be kept, and the Counter Name will be updated to the name of the
user who is currently logged in.

• When there are both individual counters and team counters, the dropdown list displays

all individual counters, together with the Team Counted Qty.

In all scenarios, when you select Clear All Counts, the counted quantities will be cleared, the
Counted checkbox will be deselected, and the Counter Name will be updated to the name of the
user who is currently logged in.

The first options in each of these scenarios are the default selections.

You can edit the following fields in the table:

Item No.

In addition to displaying the items' numbers, this column also allows you to sort items in an either
ascending or descending order. It also enables you to filter certain items you want.

Freeze Enables you to block any inventory transactions (except inventory posting) of items that affect the

in-warehouse quantities in the selected warehouses or bin locations. You can check whether the items
are frozen in Item Master Data.

By default, the Freeze checkbox is unchecked. To freeze items, select the checkbox and add the
inventory counting document.

To unfreeze items, you can do one of the following:

• Deselect the checkboxes in the relevant rows and choose Update.
• Add counting results to inventory posting.

For a mass operation, you can click the Freeze column header to display the following two options:

• Select All option checks the Freeze checkboxes in selected or filtered rows.
• Clear option deselects the Freeze checkboxes in selected or filtered rows.

 Note

You need authorization to use the freeze function in inventory counting.

1.10.3.2.1  Creating Inventory Counting

Context

You create an inventory counting to match the actual inventory to the quantities that are saved in the database.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

475

Procedure

1. To create a new inventory counting transaction, click the Create Inventory Counting tile.

2. On the General tab, specify Counting Type.

• If you select Single Counter, select Inventory Counter.
• If you select Multiple Counters, select up to 5 individual counters and 10 team counters.

3. On the Counting tab, enter the relevant items and fill in the items’ details as you count.

When you work with multiple counters, the  Dropdown List in the upper left corner above the table enables
you to switch between two segments: Individual for individual counting and Team for team counting.

If you count by UoM, click the value help icon   in the UoM Counted Qty field. The Inventory Counting by
UoM dialog box pops up for you to specify the UoM details. For more information, see Counting Inventory
by Units of Measure [page 477].

If you count by batches or serial numbers, click the value help icon   in the Counted Qty field. The Serial/
Batch Number Counting dialog box pops up, which allows you to select batch or serial numbers and create
new ones as drafts, either manually or automatically. The value help icon is also available in the Team Total
Counted Qty field.

After specifying the required information, choose the OK button.

 Note

In multiple counters type, UoM Counted Qty and Counted Qty fields are displayed per counter and
shown as <User/Employee Name> - UoM Counted Qty and <User/Employee Name> - Counted Qty
respectively.

4. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

5. To add the new inventory counting to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add

& New, Add & Back.

1.10.3.2.2  Counting Inventory by Units of Measure

When adding an inventory counting document, you can count your inventory in single or multiple UoMs.

Prerequisites

The inventory you are counting is managed by UoM.

Procedure

1.

In create mode of inventory counting, specify the information on the General tab.

2. On the Counting tab, choose at least one item managed by UoM.

3.

In the UoM Counted Qty field, click the value help icon   to open the Inventory Counting by UoM dialog
box.

4. Specify a single or multiple UoMs by which you want to count your inventory. Bar codes are not currently

required.

5. Enter the UoM counted quantities. The Counted Qty column and the total counted quantities in the footer
are updated automatically. The Counted Qty field allows you to adjust rounding differences and its value is
reflected in the table on the Counting tab.

 Note

If you work with multiple counters, the UoM Counted Qty and Counted Qty fields are displayed per
counter.

When you work with both individual and team counters, you can use the dropdown list in the upper left
corner to switch between the Individual segment and the Team segment. Depending on which segment you
are in when you open the dialog box from the counting table, the relevant segment will be displayed upon
clicking.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. Choose OK to close the dialog box.

1.10.3.3  Importing Counting Results from Microsoft Excel

Prerequisites

Prepare a Microsoft Excel file with the data you want to import. Make sure the file meets the following
requirements:

• The file must not contain any blank rows.
• The file must be saved as TXT, xlsx, and csv files. SAP Business One, Web client supports the following TXT

formats for import:
• Tab-delimited
• MS-DOS
• Macintosh

• The number of characters in the columns of the Microsoft Excel table must not be greater than the length

of the corresponding fields in SAP Business One, Web client.

Context

You can import your counting results into an inventory counting document from a pre-filled Microsoft Excel file.

Procedure

1. Go to the Inventory Counting app.

2. To begin a new inventory counting record, select Create.

3. Enter the required information in the detail view of the inventory counting document. Define the counting

type and specify the counters.

The fields available to the import template differ depending on your counting type.

4. On the Counting tab, choose Import Items to import counting results via Microsoft Excel. Alternatively, you
can select an existing inventory counting record from the list view and then choose Import Items in its
detail view to import counting results. The Mapping Data Fields dialog box opens. Choose your preferred
import method. Select either of the following import methods:
• If you want to import all data in the spreadsheet and update existing records, select the Add New

Records and Update Existing Records radio button.

• If you want to import all data in the spreadsheet except for items (in the same storage locations)

that already exist in the inventory counting document, select the Add New Records Without Updating
Existing Records radio button. The system prevents you from adding the document if any duplicate
items exist.

478

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

When multi-branch is enabled, if the branch at the header level is not defined, you cannot select Import
Items.

5. Choose the Microsoft Excel file to import by choosing the   icon. If your prepared Microsoft Excel file

contains a header row, select the File Contains Header checkbox.

6. Once your file is selected, the columns from your file will be available for mapping. Map the system fields to

the columns in your file.

7. Choose OK. Once you choose OK, the system imports your counting results into the Inventory

Counting document (or page).

 Note

When counting by a single unit of measure (UoM), the counted quantity updates in the UoM Counted
Qty field. When counting by multiple UoMs, it updates in the Inventory Counting by UoM dialog box. In
both cases, the counted quantity also appears as a summary in the Counted Qty field.

8. Make any necessary adjustments to the counting results.

9. To save the counting results in SAP Business One, Web client, choose one of the following:

• Add & View
• Add & New
• Add & Back

To save the counting results to an existing inventory counting document, choose the Update button.

Results

If you feel satisfied with the counting results (for example, differences between counters are small or rare), you
can proceed to post the results to adjust your inventory records in the system.

1.10.3.3.3  Merge of Lines with the Same Item

If you enter inventory records manually in SAP Business One, Web client, the item in each row of the document
must be unique; in other words, an item in the same storage location (warehouse or bin location) cannot be
specified twice in the document.

However, if you import inventory records from Microsoft Excel, the file may contain duplicate items. When
importing the records, the system automatically merges the lines with the same item (in the same storage
location) into one row.

1.10.4.1  Managing Inventory Postings

To open the Manage Inventory Postings list view, choose the Inventory Postings tile on the home page. Here you
can filter, sort, group, and access the relevant inventory posting records.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For information on the detailed view of inventory postings, see Working with Inventory Postings [page 487].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of inventory posting records. The views
store filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• Inventory Posting by Documents displays all inventory posting documents grouped by document number.

This view is displayed by default.

• All Inventory Postings displays all the company's inventory posting documents.
• Inventory Postings by Items displays all inventory posting documents grouped by item number.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

1.10.4.2.1  Creating Inventory Postings

Context

An inventory posting document is used to reconcile the item quantities with the inventory counting results and
adjust the inventory records.

490

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Procedure

1. To create an inventory posting document, choose the Create Inventory Posting tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the Price Source.

3.

In the Default Values section, specify the Inventory Offset - Increase Account or Inventory Offset - Decrease
Account depending on whether the inventory quantity increases or decreases.

4. To create a posting document by copying existing inventory counting documents:

1. Choose Copy from Inventory Counting in the top right corner.

2. Select one or more inventory counting documents. The Contents tab fills automatically with the

selected data.

5. On the Contents tab, specify item details as needed. You can select items individually by choosing the

 Value Help icon, or choose the Select Items option to batch select items by filtering with item details,
warehouse, and user-defined fields.

 Note

If a UoM code is defined for the item, the UoM code displays when you select the item. You can change
it if needed.
• For a single UoM, you can change the code and enter the counted quantities directly into the

counting column. Alternatively, you can choose the  Value Help icon in the UoM Counted Qty field,
specify a UoM code, and enter your counted results in the Inventory Posting by UoM dialog box.
• For multiple UoMs, you can only change the codes by choosing the  Value Help icon in the UoM

Counted Qty field.

6. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

7. To add the new inventory posting document to the company database, choose one of the following: Add &

View, Add & New, Add & Back.

1.10.5.2.1  Creating Inventory Opening Balances

Context

You can set up inventory opening balances at these points:

• As initial settings: Before entering any inventory transactions.
• After transactions exist: If opening balances were not set up initially, you can enter them later, even when

inventory transactions are already recorded.

Procedure

1. To create a new inventory opening balance document, choose the Create Inventory Opening Balance tile on

the home page.

2. On the General tab, select the Price Source for the items.

• By Price List: Select the required price list in the Price List field.
• Last Evaluated Price: Displays the price generated in the last inventory valuation simulation run for
perpetual inventory and the inventory valuation report run for non-perpetual inventory systems.

• Item Cost: When you select Item Cost as the price source, all lines will be updated with the item cost as

the price unit.

3. On the Contents tab, add the items for which you want to enter opening balances.

To batch select items based on item details or warehouses, choose the Select Items button to open the
item selection criteria window.

 Note

To allow initial quantities with a price value of 0, select Allow Positive Inventory Opening Balances with

Zero Price in  Administration Configuration

Inventory

Inventory Document Settings .

4. Enter the inventory opening balances information:

• Input initial quantities in the Opening Balance field.
• Unit prices are pre-filled according to the selected price list. Lines with negative variance always use

the item costs.

6. To add the new inventory opening balance to the company database, choose one of the following: Add &

View, Add & New, Add & Back.

1.10.6  Managing Drafts

You can create and process draft documents of sales documents, purchasing documents, payments
documents, and inventory documents.

To create a draft document, click the Create... tile of the relevant object, for example, Create A/R Invoice or
Create Purchase Quotation, or Create Outgoing Payment for Business Partner, enter all relevant details and then
choose one of the following options in the multi-choice button:

Save as Draft & New Adds the draft document and opens the document detailed view in Create mode for

creating another document in sequence.

Save as Draft & View Adds the draft document and has it displayed for further review.

In the list views of draft documents, such as the Manage Sales & Purchasing Drafts list view, the Manage
Incoming & Outgoing Payments Drafts list view, or the Manage Inventory Transactions Drafts list view, you can
perform the following tasks for single or multiple drafts:

Delete

Deletes the selected drafts from the database.

Close

Sets the status of the drafts as Closed.

Reopen Opens closed drafts and changes the status of open drafts to Closed, as in list view.

Add

Adds the drafts as official documents.

Add and Delete

Adds the drafts as official documents and deletes them from the database.

Preview, Print, Choose
Layout and Preview,
Choose Layout and Print

Preview or print one or more drafts in the default or a different Crystal Reports
layout.

 Note

The Print and Choose Layout and Print options are only available for sales and
purchasing drafts.

By default, the list view shows drafts created by the current user.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

497

To view a certain draft, choose its row. The header displays the status Draft for all drafts, whether open or
closed. The following actions are available:

Delete

Choose this button to delete the draft.

Reopen / Close Changes the draft status from Closed to Open for closed drafts or from Open to Closed for

open drafts.

New Activity Creates an activity for the business partner that appears in the draft. The draft is automatically

added to the Linked Document section of the activity.

Related Activities

Opens a list view showing the activities created for the given draft.

Preview, Print, Choose
Layout and Preview,
Choose Layout and Print

Preview or print the draft in the default or a different Crystal Reports layout.

 Note

The Print and Choose Layout and Print options are only available for sales
and purchasing drafts.

As with other documents, when you open a draft with draft status Open, it appears in View mode. You need to
choose Edit in order to switch to the Create mode.

After editing the draft, you can save it as an official document, or as a draft, the same as when creating a new
document.

 Note

• Sales documents are created in SAP Business One, Web client with a generation type of Not Relevant

that is only visible on the Electronic Documents tab in the SAP Business One client. To process
documents created in SAP Business One, Web client as electronic documents, you must manually
adjust the generation type in the SAP Business One client. For more information about working with
electronic documents, see the online help for SAP Business One.

• In the following scenario, you receive a confirmation message with the existing draft numbers and are

asked whether to continue with the process:

1. You use the Copy To or Copy From function to add one or more base sales or purchasing

documents to a target document.

2.

If approval isn’t required, you use the Save as Draft function to save the target document. If
approval is required, the system automatically creates a draft after you add the document, pending
approval.

3. You (or another user) use the Copy To or Copy From function to copy the same base documents to

another target document again.

4. You (or another user) try to add the target document, save the target document as a draft again, or

add the target document for approval again.

Before making your decision, you can open the Sales & Purchasing Drafts app in the Web client to view
details of the existing drafts using the provided draft numbers.

PUBLIC

1.10.7  Managing Documents in Approval Process

When trying to add or update a document that triggers an approval process, you see that this document is
saved as a draft. After the authorizers approve the draft in the Manage Approval Decisions list view, you can
continue adding or updating the draft.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales orders, sales quotations, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, returns,
A/R credit memos, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve invoices, goods receipt POs, goods
returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods issues, outgoing payments, inventory transfers, and inventory
transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When creating or updating a document in Web client, you are notified by the system that an approval is

required.

2. You become the originator of the approval process and a draft is created.

3. The authorizers review the draft and either approve or reject the request in the Manage Approval Decisions

list view.

4. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer.

5. To view the approval status and proceed with the process, click the Docs in Approval Process tile; the
Manage Docs in Approval Process list view opens. (Alternatively, you can access the draft from the
notification as well.)

 Note

For the outgoing payments approval process, there is a separate list view: Manage Outgoing Payments
in Approval Process.

In the list view you can:

• Filter, sort, group, and access the relevant drafts
• Add approved drafts
• Cancel approval processes for selected drafts
• Restore approval processes for selected drafts

6. Depending on the approval status, you can either generate a document (choose  Edit Add & View ) or

update the draft (choose Edit) to trigger a new approval process.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

499

Related Information

Approval Decisions [page 226]

1.10.8  Approval Decisions

When a user triggers an approval process, as the authorizer, you can see all the draft documents for approval in
the Approval Decisions list view and decide what to do with those requests.

Prerequisites

The approval process is enabled in the SAP Business One client.

Context

This function supports sales quotations, sales orders, A/R reserve invoices, deliveries, A/R invoices, return
requests, returns, A/R credit memos, purchase requests, purchase quotations, purchase orders, A/P reserve
invoices, goods receipt POs, goods return requests, goods returns, A/P invoices, A/P credit memos, goods
issues, goods receipts, inventory transfers, and inventory transfer requests.

Procedure

1. When a user that is creating or updating a document triggers an approval process, you as an authorizer are

notified by the system that your approval is required.

 Note

You can choose to also get those notifications by email. See Approval Process Settings [page 715]

2. You become the authorizer of the approval process for the draft that was created.

3. To review the requests for approval, click the Approval Decisions tile; the Manage Approval Decisions list

view opens. The requests for approval that match the selected view are displayed. The default view is My
Pending Requests for Approval.

4. You can perform the following actions:

• Choose another view or apply different filters and view settings to fine tune the displayed list.
• Select one or more requests for approval and apply the relevant action. You can choose to approve or

reject the request.

5. The originator receives a notification that the document was approved/rejected by the authorizer and can

proceed with the process. See Managing Documents in Approval Process [page 225]

1.10.9.2.1  Creating Inventory Transfer Requests

Context

You can create an inventory transfer request to request goods movements between warehouses and bin
locations of the same warehouse. In inventory transfer requests, you can choose a warehouse both as the
issuing and receiving warehouse, and after adding the document, you can copy it to an inventory transfer and
specify different bin locations.

Procedure

1. To create a new inventory transfer request, choose the Create Inventory Transfer Request tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the required information, for example, business partner and price list.

3. On the Contents tab, enter the relevant items, the receiving and issuing warehouse, and other details. If you

work with items managed by batches or serial numbers, you need to select batch or serial numbers.

4. Optionally, on the Referenced Documents tab, specify the referenced-to and referenced-by documents.

5. Optionally, on the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

6. To add the new inventory transfer request to the company database, choose one of the following: Add &

View, Add & New, and Add & Back.

1.10.10.2.1  Creating Inventory Transfers

Context

You can create an inventory transfer to move your inventory between warehouses and bin locations at the same
warehouse. An inventory transfer can also be carried out as a consignment for a customer. The items are then
stored in the customer’s warehouse and are sold from there.

Once you add the inventory transfer, you can’t change the document, but you can only correct it by entering a
compensatory movement.

Procedure

1. To create an inventory transfer, choose the Create Inventory Transfer tile.

2. On the General tab, specify the needed information, for example, business partner and price list.

3. On the Contents tab, enter the relevant items, the receiving and issuing warehouse, and other details.

You can also choose the Copy From button in the top-right corner of the header to select from a list of all
the inventory transfer requests and copy information about items, warehouses, and serial/batch numbers
to the current inventory transfer.

4. Optionally, on the Referenced Documents tab, specify the referenced-to and referenced-by documents.

5. Optionally, on the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

6. To add the new inventory transfer request to the company database, choose one of the following: Add &

View, Add & New, or Add & Back.

 Note

Before you add the inventory transfer, you can use the Journal Entry Preview option in the toolbar
on the right side of the header to preview the corresponding journal entry posting. If transactions

1.10.11.1  Managing Recurring Transaction Templates

Recurring transaction templates can be used to streamline business processes that repeat regularly.

To open the Recurring Transaction Templates list view, choose the Recurring Transaction Templates app on the
home page from the Sales, Purchasing, or Inventory Transactions groups.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of delivery records. The views store filter
settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, My, Open) to determine which
records are displayed in the list view. Select one of the following predefined views available in the views menu in
the top-left corner of the header area:

• My Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays recurring transaction templates that have been

created by the current user and whose validity date is in the future.

• All Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all the recurring transaction templates that are available in

the system for localization, including those with validity dates in the past and in the future.

• Open Recurring Transaction Templates - Displays all recurring transaction templates available in the system

for the localization, with their validity date in the future.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

1.10.12  Managing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin

Locations

You can work with batches, serial numbers and bin locations in relevant marketing documents and inventory
documents.

In this case, both outgoing and incoming batches, serial numbers and bin locations are available.

There are two scenarios where you work on the outgoing side:

• Inventory issue documents, for example, deliveries.
• Inventory issue lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an incoming document. For example,

on a line of a goods receipt PO, the quantity is minus 100.

For more information, see Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 227].

Likewise, there are two scenarios where you work on the incoming side:

• Inventory receipt documents, for example, A/P invoices.
• Inventory receipt lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an outgoing document. For example,

on a line of an A/R invoice, the quantity is minus 50.

For more information, see Incoming Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 229].

1.10.12.1  Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin

Locations

You can select batches, serial numbers and bin locations in outgoing marketing and inventory documents that
are relevant to serial/batch numbers and bin location allocation.

On the Contents tab of the document detailed view, you can find the following three fields.

Serial/
Batch
Numbers

 Note

This field is only active when the items are managed by batches or serial numbers.

This field allows you to select batches and serial numbers.

You can type serial/batch numbers directly in the field. As you type, a list of serial/batch
numbers is displayed for you to choose from. For batch items, their available quantities are also
displayed.

Alternatively, choose the  Value Help icon to open a dialog box where you can select batches or
serial numbers, manually or automatically.

In the dialog box, you can:

• Manually allocate batches or serial numbers. If bin locations are enabled for the selected

warehouse on the line, you can manually allocate per bin location.

• Change allocation rules if bin locations are enabled.

1.10.12.2.1  Automatically Creating Batches and Serial

Numbers

When you need to create a large amount of batches or serial numbers, you can use the automatic creation
function. For inventory counting transactions, the newly created serial/batch numbers are stored in the system
as drafts.

Prerequisites

You are working with items managed by batches or serial numbers.

Context

To access the Automatic Creation button, you can do either of the following:

• On the Contents tab of the detailed view in relevant documents (except inventory counting transactions),

choose the  Value Help icon in the Serial/Batch Numbers field.

• On the Counting tab of the detailed view in inventory counting transactions, choose the  Value Help icon

in the Counted Qty field.

 Note

• For A/R returns and A/R credit memos, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Serial/Batch

Numbers field, and then in the center right of the opened dialog box, select the Create button.
If bin location-enabled warehouses are selected on the line, you can also choose the value help icons in
the Bin Location Allocation and Bin Locations fields.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

521

• For inventory counting transactions, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Counted Qty

field, and then in the center right of the dialog box, select the Create button.
When you work with team counters, the dialog box is also accessible through the value help icon in the
Team Total Counted Qty field.

Procedure

1. Click the Automatic Creation button. A dialog box opens up.

2. (Optional) In the Bin Location field, specify the bin location to store your batches or serial numbers.

3. For batch items, in the field No. of Batches, specify how many batches you want to create.

4.

5.

6.

7.

In the Batch or Serial Number field, choose the value help icon. The dialog box Automatic String Creation
opens up.

Input strings for batches or serial numbers.

In the Type column, choose String or Number.

If you choose the Number type, in the Operations column, you can define one of the following operations
for the numbers: No Operations, Increase, and Decrease. The operations are performed during the
automatic creation process. If you choose the String type, the column isn’t editable. The format is
displayed in the Final String field.

8. To save your actions, choose OK.

9. To start the automatic creation, choose Create.

Results

The newly created serial/batch numbers are displayed in the dialog box. You can review and update relevant
information. To save all data and close the dialog box, choose OK.

Factors

Indicates whether the factor is relevant to the calculation of Single Run Capacity, which is

Standard
Daily
Capacity

For every day in the table, enter up to four daily capacity factors in numbers that determine
the overall daily capacity of the resource. The total daily standard capacity is automatically
calculated in the Daily Capacity field by multiplying the factors. Instead of entering daily factors,
you can enter the daily capacity directly in the Daily Capacity field.

 Example

If the values for factors 1, 2, and 3 are given as 7, 8, and 1, and no value is given for the fourth
factor, the daily resource capacity for that day will be 7*8*1=56.

Single Run
Capacity

Displays the capacity a resource requires to complete one cycle of an
operation in production and is calculated by multiplying only the factors
marked as relevant for single run capacity.

1.11.2.1  Creating Resources

Context

You can create new resources such as machine and labor to be used for production and project management.

Procedure

1. To create a new resource, choose one of the following options:

• From the Manage Resources list view, choose the Create button.
• From an existing resource, choose the New button.
• Choose the Create Resource tile on the home page.

2. On the General tab, enter all the relevant data:

• Series: Select the series from the dropdown list. The default option is Manual.
• Resource Type: Choose from the three options: Machine, Labor, and Other.
• Resource Group: Choose from the two options: Resources and Define New. The Define New option

takes you to the Resource Group creation page.

• Issue Method: Choose from the two options: Backflush or Manual.
• Resource Standard Cost: The standard costs are fetched based on the resource group entered for the

resource.

3. On the Capacity tab, you can view resource capacity for a desired period range per warehouse.

4. The Planning Data tab helps you to specify the default capacity for the resource to be used when

generating the resource capacity. These values are defined on a daily basis.
• Daily Capacity Factors: There are four factors available and the daily capacity is calculated by

multiplying the specified factor values.

• You can choose whether a factor is Relevant to Single Run Capacity by selecting the checkboxes.

5.

In the Fixed Assets tab, select the assets tagged to the resource. This tab is only available for the Machine
resource type.

6.

If the resource type is Labor, fill in the details on the Employees tab.

7.

In the Properties tab, select the relevant properties for the resource.

8. To add the new resource master data to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View,

Add & New, Add & Back.

1.12  Production

The apps in the Production group give quick and easy access to the production process, from creating and
maintaining bills of materials and production orders, issuing materials for production, and receiving deliveries
from production.

A finished product may be the result of an entire production process, or a collection of items that are sold as a
unit but are not the output of a production or assembly process.

The Production group includes apps that allow you to work with the following production documents: bills of
materials, production orders, receipts from production, and issues for production.

1.12.1.2.1  Creating Bills of Materials

Procedure

1. Enter the Bill of Materials (BOM) page in one of the following ways:

• In the Manage Bills of Materials app, choose Create.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Production Create Bill of Materials .
• On the Home page, choose the Create Bill of Materials app in the Production group.

2.

In the Product Number field, specify a product number and choose the item that you want to define as a
parent.

You can enter the product number directly in the Product Number field. The Web client automatically
suggests the best matched item master records.

You can also search for and find the product number by choosing the  Value Help icon to open the Items
dialogue.

If the parent already has a BOM, its components are displayed. However, you can still create a new BOM for
that parent item.

3. Specify a BOM type.
• Production:

The Production BOM represents a finished product (parent) comprising different inventory
components (child components). During the production process, you turn the components into the
finished product. Select the Production BOM to include the product in the MRP run and to process
standard production orders.
Components in the Production BOM are physical items, for example, a screw, a wooden board, a
measured quantity of lubricant or paint, or virtual entities, such as one work hour.

• Sales and Assembly:

The Sales BOM and the Assembly BOM represent a finished product assembled at the sales stage, that
is, the finished product is composed of its component items only when the parent product is actually
sold. The component items are stored and tracked individually in the warehouse.
For both the Sales BOM and the Assembly BOM, you do not manage the parent product as an
inventory item, but rather as a sales item. The components can also be sales and inventory items in
their own right. When you create the delivery to dispatch the customer order, the components are
backflush issued from inventory.

 Note

The components for Sales BOMs and Assembly BOMs must be sales items.

• Use a Sales BOM where there is a fixed combination of components and the customer needs

confirmation of each item. The component items cannot be altered or removed from a sales order.
Other items cannot be inserted between the parent and component items in the sales order.
However, the quantities of the component items can be modified.

• Use the Assembly BOM when you would not expect the customer to check each component in the

order, such as a gasket set.

542

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Example

Sharon's Garden Ltd. sells garden tools and outdoor furniture. One of her bestsellers is the
Metal Table set. This set is composed of one metal and glass table, six metal chairs and one
umbrella.

If she chooses the Sales BOM, the table, six chairs and one umbrella, and the Metal Table
set all appear in the sales order. She can sell this set with only four chairs, but she cannot
introduce a footstool as part of this set in the sales order.

If she chooses the Assembly BOM, then only the Metal Table set (the parent product) is listed
in the sales order.

In both cases, each of the component items is tracked individually in the inventory. When you
create the delivery to dispatch the customer order, the components are automatically issued
from the warehouse.

• Template:

The Template BOM is a bundle of items, where the parent product is the first item on the list. It does
not act as a BOM once it is added to the sales document, but rather as a list of items brought together
at the same time. You can update the quantity of those items, swap items, or delete them in the BOM
or the sales order. The components appear below the parent as a list of items in a sales or purchase
document. Use the Template BOM when you require flexibility in selecting components for a product.

 Example

Computers can be sold as a standard unit, in which case the Production or Sales BOM is
appropriate. However, to customize a sales order, use the Template BOM to allow for DVD burners,
speakers, ergonomic keyboards, and so on.

4. Enter other data for the finished product and its components.

 Note

If the BOM contains more than one component with the same serial or batch items, combine the items
in a single component and increase the quantity appropriately to prevent possible errors in the batch or
serial quantities.

5. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the BOM.
• Add & New: add the BOM and open a new Bill of Materials page.
• Add & Back: add the BOM and go back to the Manage Bill of Materials page.

• Inventory Transfer Request: Select this option and a dialog box appears, in which you can

select the components that you want to transfer for the production order. For the component
quantities to be transferred, you can either choose to transfer the open quantities of
components from the production order, or determine the quantity to transfer by specifying

• Component Transfer: Select this option and a dialog box appears, in which you can select the
components that you want to transfer for the production order. For the component quantities
to be transferred, you can either choose to transfer the open quantities of components
from the production order, or determine the quantity to transfer by specifying the quantity
of parent items. Choose OK and the Inventory Transfer page appears with relevant data
populated.

• Report Completion: This option is available for production orders in the released status. When
you select the option, the Receipt from Production page appears with relevant data from the
production order populated. You can revise the quantities and warehouses as needed, and
then create a receipt from production.

 Note

For the Disassembly type orders, when you choose Report Completion, the Issue for
Production page appears because you receive the components of the disassembled
production order in the warehouse and issue the product from the warehouse.

This dropdown is not available for canceled or closed production orders.

General Tab

The fields on this tab provide information about the production order.

Type Displays the type of the production order:

• Standard: Used to produce a regular production item based on the bill of materials.
• Special: Used to produce or repair any inventory items and for custom requirements.
• Disassembly: Used to dismantle a manufactured/parent item and return its components to

inventory.

Status The default status when creating a production order is Planned.

You can change the status to Released when it is released to the shop floor for production. At this
stage, you can report transactions for the production order and the issue of the components. You can
add a new component or update the component items if there are no transactions for the selected
components.

When the production process is completed, you can change the status to Closed. You cannot add any
new transactions to a closed production order.

You can change the status to Canceled to remove the production order from the list before the
production process starts.

 Note

Once a receipt from production is added, the production order cannot be canceled. If you have
already issued some components, you can only cancel the production order after returning all of
the issued quantities of components.

Product Group Displays the item group to which the parent item belongs, which is defined in the Item Group

field in the parent item's detailed view.

Transaction No. When the production order is closed, this field displays the number of the journal entry

generated from the production order.
