1.12.2.2.1  Creating Production Orders

Context

You can create production orders to track the quantity and cost of materials and the product status in the
manufacturing process.

Procedure

1. To create a new production order, choose one of the following options:

• In the Manage Production Orders list view, choose Create.

550

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• In the detailed view of an existing production order, choose New.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Production Create Production Order

.

2. On the General tab, enter all the relevant data:

• In the Type field, select one of the following: Standard, Special, or Disassembly. The default option is

Standard.

• In the Product No. field, select the parent item for the production order. For Standard and Disassembly
types, choose from the list of bills of materials, and for the Special type, choose from the list of items.

• Enter the planned quantity of the product. The default value is 1.
• In the Priority field, specify the degree of importance of the production order. The default value is 100.

The lower the number, the higher the importance of the production order.

• When resource-type components exist, you can select how the automatic allocation of resources will

occur from the Routing Date Calculation field.

• You can select the Procure Items checkbox to enable the creation of procurement documents for all

item-type components included in the production order.

• In the Linked To field, choose from the drop-down list to specify if the production order is linked to a

sales order or production order. The Sales Order option is displayed by default. Enter the relevant sales
or production order number in the Linked Order field.

3. On the Components tab, enter all the relevant data in the table:

• In the Type column, choose from Item, Resource, Text, or Route Stage. The default option is Item. The

remaining fields are automatically adjusted based on the selection.

• You can choose Manual or Backflush as the issue method. Individual components of a parent item are

either issued manually or automatically.

4. To add the new production order to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

Results

The production order is created in Planned status.

To release the production order to the shop floor, choose Edit and change the status to Released on the
General tab. Then you can select Report Completion in the Functions dropdown list to report completion of the
production order.

To close a production order, choose Edit and change the status to Closed on the General tab.

1.12.3.2.1  Creating Receipts from Production

Context

This topic will walk you through how to report completion of products and components after a production order
is released.

For Standard and Special production orders, finished products are posted to the inventory.

For Disassembly production orders, the components are posted to the inventory.

Procedure

1. Enter the Receipts from Production page in one of the following ways:

• In the Manage Receipts from Production app, choose Create.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Production Create Receipt from Production .
• On the Home page, choose the Create Receipt from Production app in the Production group.

2.

In the Series / No. field, choose a series for the receipt from production. Next to the series, a sequential
number is already filled in automatically.

3.

In the Posting Date field, specify a transaction posting date. The current date is displayed by default.

556

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

4.

In the Journal Remark field, enter your remark for the journal entry that is created to record the completion
of products when the receipt from production is created.

After you create the receipt from production, the remark you enter is displayed in the Journal Remark field
with a prefix “Receipt from Production”. You can click the link associated with the Journal Remark field to
open the linked journal entry.

• For companies that do not use perpetual inventory management, the remark is displayed in the

Remarks field in the transaction history file.

• For companies that use perpetual inventory, the remark is displayed in the Remarks field in the General

Ledger and transaction history file.

5. Go to the Contents section.

• In the Production Order No. field, specify the production orders that you want to receive items from.
You can enter a production order number directly in the Production Order No. field. The Web client
automatically suggests the best match.
You can also search for and select a production order by choosing the  Value Help icon to open the
Production Orders dialogue.
To select multiple production orders in one time, choose the Production Order button on the right of
the page header.

• In the Quantity field, specify the quantity of the completed or rejected items. The open quantity is

displayed by default; however, you can update that value.

 Note

• You cannot update this field for by-products with the Backflush issue method. However,
if you update the quantity of the parent item, the quantity of the by-product is updated
proportionally.

• You can update this field manually for by-products with the Manual issue method. Updating

the parent item's quantity does not affect the received quantity of such by-products.

• In the Trans. Type field, choose one of the following transaction types for the production order:

• Complete: to report the completion of the product quantity.
• Reject: to report the rejection of the product quantity.

• Edit other information as needed.

6. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the BOM.
• Add & New: add the BOM and open a new Bill of Materials page.
• Add & Back: add the BOM and go back to the Manage Bill of Materials page.

Results

The specified numbers of products or disassembly components are added to inventory. You can see increased
stock numbers on the Inventory Data tab in the associated Item Master Data.

If the issue method for the components of the products is backflush, the corresponding number of
components is removed from stock automatically.

 Posting Instructions

Go back to the production order and change the status to closed.

If you want to return manually released items back to inventory as available stock, for example, when a
production order is canceled or when you have specific items in a production order that were not used in
production, you can choose the Return Components button on the right of the page header.

1.12.5  Managing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations

You can work with batches, serial numbers and bin locations in relevant marketing documents and inventory
documents.

In this case, both outgoing and incoming batches, serial numbers and bin locations are available.

There are two scenarios where you work on the outgoing side:

• Inventory issue documents, for example, deliveries.
• Inventory issue lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an incoming document. For example,

on a line of a goods receipt PO, the quantity is minus 100.

For more information, see Outgoing Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 227].

Likewise, there are two scenarios where you work on the incoming side:

• Inventory receipt documents, for example, A/P invoices.
• Inventory receipt lines, which means a negative quantity on the line of an outgoing document. For example,

on a line of an A/R invoice, the quantity is minus 50.

For more information, see Incoming Batches, Serial Numbers, and Bin Locations [page 229].

1.12.5.2.1  Automatically Creating Batches and Serial

Numbers

When you need to create a large amount of batches or serial numbers, you can use the automatic creation
function. For inventory counting transactions, the newly created serial/batch numbers are stored in the system
as drafts.

Prerequisites

You are working with items managed by batches or serial numbers.

Context

To access the Automatic Creation button, you can do either of the following:

• On the Contents tab of the detailed view in relevant documents (except inventory counting transactions),

choose the  Value Help icon in the Serial/Batch Numbers field.

• On the Counting tab of the detailed view in inventory counting transactions, choose the  Value Help icon

in the Counted Qty field.

 Note

• For A/R returns and A/R credit memos, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Serial/Batch

Numbers field, and then in the center right of the opened dialog box, select the Create button.
If bin location-enabled warehouses are selected on the line, you can also choose the value help icons in
the Bin Location Allocation and Bin Locations fields.

• For inventory counting transactions, you first need to choose the value help icon in the Counted Qty

field, and then in the center right of the dialog box, select the Create button.
When you work with team counters, the dialog box is also accessible through the value help icon in the
Team Total Counted Qty field.

Procedure

1. Click the Automatic Creation button. A dialog box opens up.

2. (Optional) In the Bin Location field, specify the bin location to store your batches or serial numbers.

3. For batch items, in the field No. of Batches, specify how many batches you want to create.

4.

5.

6.

In the Batch or Serial Number field, choose the value help icon. The dialog box Automatic String Creation
opens up.

Input strings for batches or serial numbers.

In the Type column, choose String or Number.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

569

7.

If you choose the Number type, in the Operations column, you can define one of the following operations
for the numbers: No Operations, Increase, and Decrease. The operations are performed during the
automatic creation process. If you choose the String type, the column isn’t editable. The format is
displayed in the Final String field.

8. To save your actions, choose OK.

9. To start the automatic creation, choose Create.

Results

The newly created serial/batch numbers are displayed in the dialog box. You can review and update relevant
information. To save all data and close the dialog box, choose OK.

1.12.6  Procurement Confirmation Wizard

on the home page. Alternatively, choose  Production Procurement Confirmation Wizard  or  Production

Procurement Confirmation Wizard  in the Main Menu.

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with this app:

• Create one or more procurement documents, such as purchase quotations, purchase orders, or

production orders, directly from one or multiple sales documents or production orders.

• Combine several base documents into a single target document for a customer.

1.12.6.1  Creating Purchase Orders from Sales Orders

Context

You can create a purchase order directly from a sales order following these steps:

Procedure

1. Create a sales order specifying customer and item information. In the Logistics tab, select the checkbox

Procure Non-Drop-Ship Items.

 Note

Alternatively, you can edit an existing sales order and select the Procure Non-Drop-Ship Items checkbox
in the Logistics tab.

2. After you add or update the sales order, the Procurement Confirmation Wizard opens.

3. The wizard displays the Base Document and Business Partners fields, pre-filled with customer details from

the selected sales order. You can add business partners if required.

4. To create purchase orders for all open sales orders with unfulfilled purchase quantities for selected

business partners, select the Include All Open Base Documents checkbox.

5. Choose Next. All open sales orders are listed for you to select.

6.

In the Base Document Lines step, choose Purchase Order as the Target Document. Make sure all items have
a vendor assigned to them. If an item has a preferred vendor, this vendor is already entered in the line. If
required, change the vendor code. The other details are automatically filled in.

7. To save the purchase order as a draft, select the Create Draft Document checkbox.

8. Choose Next.

9.

In the Consolidation step, specify whether to consolidate the purchase requirements from multiple sales
orders into one purchase order, and which consolidation options to apply.

 Note

If you choose No Consolidation, the documents are grouped by vendor, that is, one purchase order is
created per vendor.

10. Specify the system response to errors that may occur in the document generation process in the If an Error

Occurs dropdown list. You can select either Skip to Next Vendor (default option) or Stop Execution.

11. Choose Next. The Results Preview displays the details of all purchase orders that will be created. The

purchase orders are grouped by vendor and the consolidations options you selected.

12. To generate the documents, choose Execute Now.

13. The Summary Report displays all the documents that have been created and any errors that have

occurred.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

571

1.12.6.2  Creating Procurement Documents from Production

Orders

Context

You can create purchase orders, purchase quotations, or purchase requests from a production order.
Alternatively, you can procure components directly for a production order to ensure availability for the
production process. By creating procurement documents based on actual production requirements, you can
better maintain minimum inventory levels and support efficient production planning.

Procedure

1. Create a production order specifying the product information. On the General tab, select the Procure Items
checkbox. The Components tab is updated with the Allow Procurement Doc. column checked for the item
entries.

2. Add the production order, and the Procurement Confirmation Wizard opens.

3.

In the Base Document Type step, the product number and description fields are prefilled based on the
production order. You can select more products for which you want to generate procurement documents.

4. Select the checkbox Include All Open Base Documents to ensure all related open documents for the

selected products are displayed in the next step.

5. Choose Next and select the base documents from which you want to generate procurement documents.

6. Choose Next. In the Base Document Lines step, select one of the following options as the target document

type: Purchase Order, Purchase Quotation, or Purchase Request.

7.

If an item has a preferred vendor, this vendor is already entered in the line. If required, change the vendor
code. The other fields are automatically filled in.

8. To create the procurement document as a draft, select the Create Draft Document checkbox.

9. Choose Next. In the Consolidation step, specify whether to consolidate the purchase requirements from
multiple production orders into one purchasing document, and which consolidation options to apply.

 Note

If you choose No Consolidation, the documents are grouped by vendor, that is, one purchasing
document is created per vendor.

10. Specify the system response to errors that may occur in the document generation process in the If an Error

Occurs dropdown list. You can select either Skip to Next Vendor (default option) or Stop Execution.

11. Choose Next. The Results Preview displays the details of all purchasing documents that will be created. The

purchasing documents are grouped by vendor and the consolidations options you selected.

12. To generate the documents, choose Execute Now.

13. The Summary Report displays all the documents that have been created and any errors that have

occurred.

1.13.1.2.1  Creating G/L Accounts

Procedure

1. To create a new G/L account, in the Chart of Accounts app, select the G/L account for which you want to

create a same level or sublevel account, and choose an option in the Create dropdown list.

2. On the General tab, enter the relevant account information, such as the account code, account name, and

so on.

3. On the Properties and Details tabs, define the relevant properties and details.

4. On the Positions tab, the information is filled automatically according to your selected account and

creation option. Change the settings if needed.

5. To add the new G/L account to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back. For more information, see Apps for Creating Records [page 89].

1.13.2  Creating G/L Accounts with Account Code Generator

Prerequisites

• Ensure that account segmentation is allowed for your country/region or state.
• Ensure that the option Use Segmentation Accounts is selected under  Administration

 Configuration

Accounting Accounting Settings .

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

577

Context

Use the Account Code Generator app to have active accounts generated automatically from a combination of
different segments. These segments represent the specific business units or activities that you want to track.

Procedure

1. To create G/L accounts with the account code generator, click the Account Code Generator tile.

2. On the G/L Account Details tab, define the details for the accounts.

• In the Natural Account field, define the account code. The generated account code is the combination
of this natural account and the segment codes. The number of characters of this natural account is
limited to the value of the Size field in the Account Segmentation - Setup window in the SAP Business
One client for the first segment: Natural Account.

• In the Account Name field, define the account name. The generated account name is the combination

of this account name and the segment short names.

3. On the G/L Account Location tab, define the location of the accounts.

The Parent Article dropdown list displays titles from one level above the value you set in the Level dropdown
list of the G/L Account Details tab.

 Example

When you select 3 in the Level dropdown list, the Parent Article field displays titles from level 2 of the
selected drawer.

4. On the G/L Account Properties tab, define the relevant properties for the accounts.

The fields appear according to the selected drawer.

5. Choose the button for each segment to open Segment Codes, where you can select the required codes

from each segment to be included in the accounts.

 Note

You must use all the segments when you create new G/L accounts.

6. Choose OK to open the Account Code List, where you can view the accounts to be generated in the chart

of accounts, according to the parameters you set. You can change the name, currency, and parent article, if
required.

In the Add column, select the accounts that you would like to create.

7. To add the new G/L accounts to the company database, choose Add.

Procedure

583

2. On the General tab, enter the relevant transaction information, such as reference number, dates, and so on.

With the Template Type and Template fields, you can create the manual journal entry according to either of
the following templates:

• A journal entry template: selecting a journal entry template will fill the lines with defined percentages.
After you enter a value in a line, the other lines with be filled with values calculated according to the
percentages.

• A recurring journal entry: selecting a recurring journal entry instance will fill both the General and

Contents tabs.

3. On the Contents tab, enter the relevant accounting details.

Lines without amounts will be saved in the database if both of the following criteria are met:

• Yes is selected in the message asking whether you want to continue when lines without amounts exist

in the journal entry.

• Allow Zero Amount Line is selected for Journal Entry on the Per Document tab of the Document

Settings window in the SAP Business One client.

4. On the Attachments tab, add new attachments by choosing Upload.

5. To add the new journal entry to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back. For more information, see Apps for Creating Records [page 89].

Importing a Single Journal Entry from Microsoft Excel Files [page 584]

1.13.3.2.1.1  Importing a Single Journal Entry from Microsoft

Excel Files

Context

You can import data from Microsoft Excel files to a single journal entry in SAP Business One, Web client. The
data is copied from a Microsoft Excel file to the corresponding fields in Web client. This import feature can be
used by the consultants during the implementation process or by the end-users from time to time.

You must first configure the definitions for the import, according to the following rules:

• Microsoft Excel files must be saved as XLSX, CSV, or TXT files.
• Files must not contain any blank rows.

584

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• The number of characters in the cells of the Microsoft Excel file must not be greater than the length of the

corresponding fields in SAP Business One, Web client.

Procedure

From SAP Business One, Web client, choose the Create Journal Entry tile, and choose the Import from Excel
button. The Mapping Data Fields window appears.

1.

Import Journal Entry Header.

1.

In the Mapping Data Fields window, from the Select Object field, select Journal Entry Header and
choose the browse button in the File to Import field. Select your Microsoft Excel file that includes the
header information of the journal entry, which are the fields on the General tab of the Journal Entry
window. Choose the File Contains Header checkbox if your Microsoft Excel file has a header row.

2. Map the columns in the Microsoft Excel file with the header fields in the journal entry object. Choose
the dropdown lists and select the fields of the journal entry header. Additionally, you can use the Use
Predefined Template option to automatically map fields. Once you download the template, enter your
data in the required format, upload the file, and select this option to map the file columns to your
system fields automatically. If you select the Hide Mapped Fields checkbox, the dropdown list will not
show the already mapped fields. You can display the UI Field names and/or the Database Field names
according to your preferences.

3. You can continue to import journal entry lines or choose the OK button to import the journal entry

header file.

2.

Import Journal Entry Lines.

1.

In the Mapping Data Fields window, from the Select Object field, select Journal Entry Lines and choose
the browse button in the File to Import field. Select your Microsoft Excel file that includes the lines
information of the journal entry, which are the fields on the Contents tab of the Journal Entry window.
Choose the File Contains Header checkbox if your Microsoft Excel file has a header row.

2. Map the columns in the Microsoft Excel file with the lines fields in the journal entry object. Choose
the dropdown lists and select the fields of the journal entry lines. Additionally, you can use the Use
Predefined Template option to automatically map fields. Once you download the template, enter your
data in the required format, upload the file, and select this option to map the file columns to your
system fields automatically. If you select the Hide Mapped Fields checkbox, the dropdown list will not
show the already mapped fields. You can display the UI Field names and/or the Database Field names
according to your preferences.

3.

If you want to import more journal entry lines from other Microsoft Excel files, repeat the above steps
to import multiple Microsoft Excel files.

3. Choose OK to import the Microsoft Excel files.

 Note

In the United Kingdom, France and Greece localizations, you also have the option to import withholding tax
data. To import withholding tax data:

1. Select Withholding Tax from the Select Object field in the Mapping Data Fields window, and choose the

browse button in the File to Import field. Select your Microsoft Excel file that includes the withholding
tax information of the journal entry. Choose the File Contains Header checkbox if your Microsoft Excel
file has a header row.

2. Map the columns in the Microsoft Excel file with the withholding tax fields in the journal entry object.
Use the dropdown lists to select the fields for the journal entry withholding tax data: Wtax Code,

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

585

Taxable Amount, and Wtax Amount. If you select the Hide Mapped Fields checkbox, the dropdown list
will not show the already mapped fields. You can display the UI Field names and/or the Database Field
names according to your preferences.

3.

If you want to import more withholding tax data from other Microsoft Excel files, repeat the above steps
to import multiple Microsoft Excel files.

4. Choose OK to import the Microsoft Excel files.

Results

Once the import process is complete, all the imported information from the Microsoft Excel file is displayed in
the new journal entry window. Make sure that all values are valid.

To add the new journal entry to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,
Add & Back.

App

Use the Journal Vouchers app to work with a temporary storage facility for journal entries that cannot yet be
posted to the company database. Once you have checked and approved the journal voucher content, you save

Tasks

• Search and filter journal vouchers
• View and manage different views of journal voucher lists
• View, edit, and delete journal vouchers
• Create journal vouchers by adding new transactions with entries.
• Create transactions with entries to a selected voucher.
• Post journal vouchers.

1.13.6  Working with Exchange Rates and Indexes

Exchange Rates

You can use the exchange rate table to set up exchange rates for foreign currencies.

To open the exchange rate table, click the Exchange Rates tile on the home page. Alternatively, from the Main

Menu, choose  Accounting
and the current month. You can filter, view, and edit the records.

 Exchange Rates . Exchange rates are defaulted to display by the current year

You can also update the exchange rates in other apps through the Enter Exchange Rate dialog box, and the
exchange rates are saved to the Exchange Rates app according to the document posting date.

 Example

On 06/10/2025, you create a sales order for the foreign customer C10000, whose currency is EUR. After
specifying the customer code, the Enter Exchange Rates dialog box appears, asking you to enter the
exchange rate on the sales order posting date, which by default is taken from the current date 06/10/2025.
You enter an exchange rate of 6 and choose Update.

Later, you change the posting date to 07/20/2025, and the Enter Exchange Rate dialog box pops up again
and you enter an exchange rate of 7 and choose Update.

As a result, 6 is saved to the date 06/10/2025 and 7 is saved to the date 07/20/2025.

The following scenarios display the Enter Exchange Rate dialog box, allowing you to enter the exchange rate:

• Scenario 1: You are creating a new document in Web client and the system currency (SC) is different from

the local currency (LC).

• Scenario 2: You are creating or editing a new document in Web client and the exchange rate is missing for

the business partner currency; you select the business partner.

• Scenario 3: The rate for the business partner currency is missing for the selected posting.

Similarly, you change the posting date and the new posting date does not have an exchange rate.

• Scenario 4: You edit the currency in a document item (for example, the unit price currency of a sales order

line), and the related exchange rate is missing.

Within the Exchange Rates app, above the table area, the header contains 2 dropdown lists, one filtering the
year and the other filtering the month. And the table reflects your choice dynamically.

In the table area, each column represents a specific currency, each row represents a specific day in the
specified month, and each cell represents the corresponding exchange rate.

You have the following options to manage exchange rates.

 Note

information.

the predefined template to prepare your Microsoft Excel file.

Service Call
<Number>

A combination of "Service Call" and a defined, automatically-generated sequential number
that identifies the service call.

The service call number information is taken from the Number field in the Service Call
Details section on the General tab.

Type Sales type indicates that the service is provided to your customer.

Purchasing type indicates that the service is provided by your vendor.

The type information is taken from the option that you select for the Type dropdown list in the Business
Partner Details section on the General tab when you create a service call.

Customer or
Vendor

If the Type is Sales, this field displays the business partner code and name of the customer.

If the Type is Purchasing, this field displays the business partner code and name of the vendor.

You can choose the business partner code to open the Business Partner quick view in a
popover to view some basic information about the business partner. In the popover, you can
choose View More to view the Business Partner Master Data in a new tab or in the current tab of
your Web browser.

The code information is taken from the business partner that you choose for the Customer
or Vendor field in the Business Partner Details section on the General tab when you create a
service call.

Item Displays the item number and item description if the service is provided for an item.

You can choose the item number to open the Item quick view in a popover to view some basic
information about the item. In the popover, you can choose View More to view the Item Master Data in a
new tab or in the current tab of your Web browser.

The item information is taken from the item that you choose for the Item No. field in the Item Details
section on the General tab when you create a service call.

Status Status of the service call.

There are three default statuses:

• Open: The initial status of a service call after it is created. It awaits service engineers to work on it.
• Pending: The issue is acknowledged but the call has not yet been resolved or closed. This could be
due to needing approval, needing further information, waiting for parts, or any other reason that
might delay the completion of the service call.

• Closed: The service call is resolved. You cannot set the status of a service call to Closed if you

have not provided a solution.

The status information is taken from the option that you select for the Status dropdown list in the
Service Call Details section on the General tab when you create a service call.

You can select one of the default statuses for the service call or define a new status. The call status
influences the relevant service reports.

1.14.1.2.1  Creating Service Calls

Context

You can create a service call for a customer if the service is provided to your customer, or for a vendor if the
service is received from your vendor.

This topic will walk you through an example of how to create a service call for a customer.

Procedure

1. Enter the Service Call page in one of the following ways:

• In the Manage Service Calls app, choose Create.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Service Create Service Call
.
• On the Home page, choose the Create Service Call app in the Service group.

2. Select Sales from the Type dropdown list.

3. Specify a customer.

You can enter the customer code directly in the Customer field. The Web client automatically suggests the
best match.

You can also search for and find a customer by choosing the  Value Help icon to open the Business
Partners dialogue.

Once a customer is selected, all other relevant information will be filled in automatically.

4. Enter a short description in the Subject field.

5. Specify an item and serial number.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

609

You can enter the serial number for an item directly in the Serial Number field. Web client automatically
suggests the best match.

You can also search for and find an item that is managed by serial numbers by choosing the  Value Help
icon to open the Customer Equipment Card dialogue.

The Contract No. field displays the number of the service contract linked to the selected serial number
of the selected customer. If there are at least two valid contracts for the selected customer, a warning
message appears until you select a valid contract manually.

6. Specify an assignee who handles the service call.

When a service call is created, the user who created the service call is selected as the default User in the
Assignment section.

You can select a different user, for example, if you need to forward the service call for advanced handling.
The new assignee receives an alert regarding the forwarded service call via the internal messaging system.

When you create a new service call, you can also select a queue. When you update a service call, you need
to allocate it to a specific assignee.

7. Go to the Solutions & Resolution tab, enter a solution ID in the ID field and select the target solution from
the auto-complete list, or choose the  Value Help icon to enter the Service Call Solutions dialog to select
an existing solution that solves the service call problems.

After you specify a solution, you can choose the arrow icon ( ) next to the solution ID to open the Service
Call Solution quick view in a popover to view some basic information about the solution. In the popover, you
can choose View More to view the detailed view of the solution in a new Web browser tab, or choose the
 Open Menu icon to open the detailed view in the current Web browser tab.

8. Go to the Scheduling tab, schedule a technician visit for the service call.

To schedule more than one technician visit for the same service call, or one visit for more than one

technician, select the Enable Scheduling Multiple Tickets option from the  Document Settings Per

Document

 tab in the SAP Business One client.

Note that the activation is irreversible due to a database structure change that occurs during the
activation.

Once you enable this option, the Technician field will be moved from the General tab to the Scheduling tab.
You can select a technician for a specific visit. The technician will receive a notifications in the Notification
Center.

You can use the Handled By field to specify who handles this service call. The person will receive a
notifications in the Notification Center as well.

9. Go to the Attachments tab, and upload files or emails as attachments.

10. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the service call.
• Add & New: add the service call and open a new Service Call page.
• Add & Back: add the service call and go back to the Manage Service Calls page.

Card Type

When you edit an existing equipment card, you can change the equipment card type in the
following ways:

• You can change the type from either Sales or Purchasing to Sales & Purchasing.
• To change the type from Sales & Purchasing to Sales, first remove all Vendor type of

business partners from the equipment card.

• To change the type from Sales & Purchasing to Purchasing, first remove all Customer type

of business partners from the equipment card.

Status • Active

The item was shipped.

• Returned

The item was returned to the warehouse.

• Terminated

The item is not in use and is therefore not eligible for service. An equipment card defined as
Terminated cannot be added to a service contract or service call.

• Loaned

The item is loaned to the business partner. You might use this status if you need to repair an item
for the business partner, and you loan the business partner a similar item until the original item is
fixed. Specify the serial number of a loaned item in the Previous Serial Number field.

• In Repair Lab

The item was returned for repair. If the business partner received a temporary replacement, this
is displayed in the New Serial Number field. The item cannot be shipped to another business
partner.

1.14.2.2.1  Creating Equipment Cards

Prerequisites

In the SAP Business One client, select the following options:

• Go to  Administration

 System Initialization

 Document Settings

 Per Document

 tab. Choose

Equipment Card from the Document dropdown list. Select the checkboxes, Add Multiple Business
Partners to an Equipment Card and Automatically Add Business Partners from New Documents to Existing
Equipment Cards.
• Go to  Administration

Inventory  tab. Select the Serial

 System Initialization

 General Settings

Number option for the Unique Serial Numbers By field.

Context

We will walk you through an example of how to create an equipment card to track a serial-numbered item, that
you purchased from a vendor and then sold to a customer, throughout its end-to-end service period.

First, we create an equipment card with the vendor information. Then we show you how a customer is
automatically added to the existing equipment card.

Procedure

1.

In the SAP Business One client, create an A/P invoice for a purchased item that is managed by serial
numbers.

616

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

2. To create a new equipment card, choose one of the following options:

• From the Manage Equipment Cards list view, choose Create in the table toolbar.
• From an existing equipment card, choose New in the header of the record.
• From the home page, choose the Create Equipment Card app in the Service group.

3. On the Equipment Card page, open the Equipment Type dropdown list and select Sales & Purchasing.

4.

In the Item Code field, enter the item code for the purchased item directly in this field, or choose the
 Value Help icon to enter the Items dialog and select the item.

5. Enter the Serial Number of the purchased item.

6.

In the Business Partner Details section, choose the  Add icon.

In the Business Partner Code field, enter the code of the vendor from whom you purchased the item, or
choose the  Value Help icon to enter the Business Partners dialog and select the vendor.

(Optional) You can add multiple business partners to the same equipment card. The first selected business
partner automatically becomes the default business partner. The default business partner will become the
default business partner when you choose Create Service Call in the toolbar of the equipment card detailed
view to create a service call.

You can change the default business partner if you want to.

If the default business partner is inactive, you cannot save the equipment card successfully. If the default
business partner is active but one or more non-default business partners are inactive, you receive a
confirmation message for each inactive business partner, prompting you to decide whether to continue
with the process.

7. Choose Add & View to save the equipment card and view its details.

8. Choose the Navigate to Home icon to go to the home page.

9. On the home page, choose the Create Delivery app in the Sales group.

10. In the Customer field on the Delivery page, enter the business partner code of the customer to whom you

want to sell and deliver the purchased item, or choose the  Value Help icon to enter the Business Partners
dialog and select the customer.

11. In the Item No. column on the Contents tab, enter the item number for the item to be delivered, or choose

the  Value Help icon to enter the Items dialog and select the item.

12. If the Batch/Serial Numbers column is hidden, choose the  Settings icon to open the Select Columns

dialogue to select and display the column.

In the Batch/Serial Numbers column, enter the serial number for the item, or choose the  Value Help icon
to enter the Select Serial Numbers dialog and select the serial number.

13. Choose Add & Back to add the delivery and go back to the Home page.

14. On the Home page, choose the Equipment Cards app in the Service group to enter the Manage Equipment

Cards page.

15. On the Manage Equipment Cards page, select and open the equipment card that you created previously.

16. In the Business Partner Details section of your equipment card detailed view, the customer is added

automatically.

You can see both your vendor and your customer information.

Prerequisites

• Your item is managed by serial numbers.
• Certain contract templates have been predefined for the item on the Contract Templates page ( Main

Context

If your item is managed by serial numbers, when you create an A/R invoice or a delivery that includes this item
for your customer, the Web client automatically creates a service contract with the contract template that you
select for this item. You don’t need to manually fill in all information in the contract.

This topic will walk you through an example of how a service contract is created automatically for your
customer when you create an A/R invoice for your item.

Procedure

1. Choose  Main Menu. Under the main menu, choose

Item Management

Items  to enter the Manage

Items list view.

2.

In the Manage Items list view, find your item that is managed by serial numbers and choose the row to open
the Item Master Data detailed view.

3. On the Item Master Data page of your item, go to the Logistics tab, find the Service Attributes section and

the Warranty Template dropdown list, and select a warranty contract template for the item.

4. Choose  Main Menu. Under the main menu, choose  Sales Create A/R Invoice  to open a blank A/R

Invoice page.

5. On the A/R Invoice page, specify general information for your customer.

Go to the Contents tab, specify the item number and serial numbers for your item. Fill in other necessary
information and create an A/R invoice.

After you create the A/R invoice successfully, a service contract is created automatically with the template
that you select.

6. Choose  Main Menu. Under the main menu, choose  Service Service Contracts  to enter the Manage

Service Contracts list view.

7.

In the Manage Service Contracts list view, find the service contract that is just created automatically for
your customer and item, and choose the row to open the Service Contract detailed view to check more
details.

1.15.1.2.1  Creating New Time Sheets

Context

You can create a time sheet to record the amount of a worker's time spent on the job.

Procedure

1. To create a new time sheet, choose one of the following options:

• From the Manage Time Sheets list view, choose Create in the table toolbar.
• From an existing time sheet, choose New in the header of the record.
• From the home page, click the Create Time Sheet tile in the Human Resources group.

2. On the General tab, select the type of the person recording time sheet hours from employee, user and

external, and specify the start and end date of your time sheet.

Once a person is selected, all other relevant information will be filled in automatically.

Specify the owner of the time sheet. Only the owner and super users can access the time sheet.

 Note

The system will retrieve an employee’s absence information from the date range you defined in the
general area and fill it automatically in the Time Recording table. You cannot modify the absence
information in the Time Sheet window. You maintain the absence information of an employee from the
SAP Business One client, using the Absence button on the Administration tab of the Employee Master
Data window.

3. On the Contents tab, enter the relevant details.

• Billable Time will be calculated automatically based on the entered start time, end time, break and

nonbillable time, for which you will be expected to pay.

• Total Billable Time, Total Effective Time and Time Recording Completed percentage will be calculated

automatically and displayed on the header area.

4. To add the new time sheet to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add & New,

Add & Back.

1.16  Analytics

SAP Business One, Web client provides both built-in and customizable analytics capabilities and content.

Apps

If you are working with SAP Business One, you can find the following apps in the Analytics group:

• User-Defined Queries
• Export and Import Views
• General Overview
• Linked List Views

If you are working with SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA, there are additional SAP HANA-specific
Overview and Chart tiles available.

Choosing an Overview tile opens a view displaying analytical cards (reports) that you have added as part of
your analytics activities. You can edit the Overview view and the displaying cards and configure a different set of
filters so as to produce a variant set of data. Every Overview view or view thereof can be added as a tile to your
home page to serve as a potential entry point for further analytics.

General Authorizations

User access to the User-Defined Queries, Export and Import Views, and Linked List Views apps is granted in the
General Authorizations window in the SAP Business One client.

User access to business documents and objects that are set up in the SAP Business One client is automatically
applied to the accessibility of data in the General Overview app in the Web client. Additionally, when you select
User-Defined Tables or User-Defined Objects as data sources for your cards in the General Overview app, your
access to these tables or objects is determined by two factors: the Apply Authorization setting applied during

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

635

their creation in the Web client, and their specific authorization configurations in the SAP Business One client.
For more information, see Creating User-Defined Tables [page 816] and Creating a User-Defined Object [page
808].

If you are working with SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA, with SAP Business One analytics enabled,
user access to predefined semantic layers that are set up in the SAP Business One client is automatically
applied to the accessibility of the following analytical data in the Web client:

• Data in the General Overview app that use those semantic layers as data sources.
• Data in the SAP HANA-specific Overview and Chart views and views thereof.

Here’s a list of the predefined semantic layers that are available for the Web client:

• Profitability Analysis
• Sales Analysis by Document
• Customer Open Balances And Credit Limit Comparison
• Purchase Analysis
• Purchase Analysis by Document
• Vendor Balance Analysis Query
• Inventory Status
• Inventory Transaction Documents
• Financial Analysis
• Sales Quotation Header
• Sales Quotation Details

For more information, see the following guides:

• How to Define Authorizations in SAP Business One 10.0
• User Guide - SAP Business One analytics 1.2 powered by SAP HANA
• How to Work with Semantic Layers in SAP Business One 9.2, version for SAP HANA

Data Ownership Authorizations

Data ownership authorizations that are set up for business documents and objects by document owners,
business partner owners, and branches in the SAP Business One client are automatically applied to the
accessibility of data in the General Overview app in the Web client.

However, as the data ownership authorizations function is not available for semantic layers, if you are working
with SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA, you cannot apply data ownership authorizations to control
accessibility of segmented data for the SAP HANA-specific Overview and Chart views or views thereof in the
Web client. If your cards in the General Overview app use SAP HANA semantic layers as data sources, or use
user-defined queries as data sources in either an SAP HANA or Microsoft SQL environment, you cannot apply
data ownership authorizations either.

For more information, see the following help documents:

• Data Ownership
• User Guide - SAP Business One analytics 1.2 powered by SAP HANA
• How to Work with Semantic Layers in SAP Business One 9.2, version for SAP HANA

1.16.1  Designing Overview Page

You can do the following on an Overview page:

• Perform an in-depth analysis of a single data area.
• Use global page filtering to change filters at runtime (either manually or by selecting from pre-saved views)

that apply to all cards displayed in the Overview page simultaneously.

• Save the changed filters as views and link to home page tiles to enable those views to be opened directly

from the home page.

You can also flexibly create and configure variant page views that include different dashboards on an Overview
page. You can edit the cards and adapt filters to display the required data in those cards.

On an Overview page, choose Edit to perform the following operations. This button becomes the Finish Edit
button to enable you to return to the Overview page upon completion of editing.

Adding a Card

1.16.1.1  Adapting Filters

Being in filtering mode lets you create and adapt filters for the types of data to be displayed in the analytic
cards.

On the right side of the filter bar, choose the Adapt Filters button.

In the displayed Adapt Filters form, you can:

• Enter the condition you require for any new filter and select its checkbox to display it in the filter bar.
Choosing the icon on the right side of each filter opens a new form that lets you refine the condition.

• Remove the conditions for any filter you no longer want to use and deselect its checkbox so that it does not

appear in the filter bar.

• After you have completed adapting the filters, choose Go to return to the Overview page.
• Choose Cancel to close the form without saving any changes.

Once you have completed your editing, choose the Finish Edit button to exit Edit mode:

• All card changes currently active are saved when saving a view or when saving as a tile.
• Choose the card header opens the corresponding Chart view with the same filters and chart type, measure,

dimension, or sort selections as the current card.

1.16.2  User-Defined Queries

App

In the Analytics group, you can find the User-Defined Queries (UDQs) app.

Tasks

With this app, you can create your own queries to flexibly serve your own specific analytical requirements.

With this app, you can carry out the following tasks:

• Create, edit, delete, and copy UDQs.
• Update existing UDQs created in the SAP Business One client that do not include parameters or

expressions which change field labels.

• Present UDQs without parameters in standard list views and utilize all standard list view functions.

UDQs created in this app can be further utilized across SAP Business One, Web client:

• You can create links from list views, or from the header or table section within detailed views of linkable

objects, to list views that are created from UDQs. For more information, see Linked List Views [page 661].
• You can use UDQs as source data to create cards in the General Overview app. For more information, see

General Overview [page 658].

 Note

Unlike the SAP Business One client, you can only create and manage SELECT statements in the Web client;
CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE or other statements are not supported.

The accessibility of SELECT queries across different client platforms is affected by the presence of
parameters:

• If a SELECT query doesn't contain parameters or expressions which change field labels, it is accessible

and interchangeable between the SAP Business One client and the Web client.

• If a SELECT query contains parameters or expressions which change field labels, it is accessible and

usable only in the client where it is created.

• A parameterized SELECT query created in the Web client can currently only be previewed on the

creation page. It cannot be opened in a list view or used elsewhere in the Web client.

General Authorizations

To enable access to this app, make sure that Full Authorization is selected for User-Defined Queries App in Web
Client in the General Authorizations window in the SAP Business One client.

1.16.2.1  Managing User-Defined Queries

To open the Manage User-Defined Queries view, choose the User-Defined Queries tile in the Analytics group

on the home page. Alternatively, choose  Analytics User-Defined Queries  in the Main Menu. Here you can
view and manage user-defined queries (UDQs) to which you have access.

Searching for Records

Enter keywords in the search bar in the header to search for a specific query record.

Performing Business Actions

Use the options in the table toolbar to perform the following actions:

Create

Choose this button to create a new UDQ.

Active Select a single or multiple UDQs and choose this button to activate them all.

When a UDQ is active, it is available for use. For example, it is listed as an option in the Data Source
dropdown list when you create cards in the General Overview app and available as a linkable list view
option in the Linked List Views app.

Inactive Select a single or multiple UDQs and choose this button to deactivate them all.

When a UDQ is inactive, you can view it within the User-Defined Queries app but cannot use it
anywhere.

Expand By default, UDQs are collapsed under each category. Choose this button to unfold all UDQs.

Collapse

Choose this button to fold all UDQs under all categories.

A User-Defined Query (UDQ) detailed view is divided into two parts: header and body. The header area

and settings, and results preview structured with a series of tabs.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

Performing Business Actions

You can perform the following actions using the toolbar on the right side of the header:

Edit

Modifies the current UDQ.

Duplicate

Duplicates the current UDQ.

After you choose this button, a copy of the current UDQ appears in Create mode.

When you duplicate a UDQ, the following attributes are copied with it:

• The SQL statement itself.
• The associated category.
• All metadata.
• All variant views saved from its associated list view.

Remove Removes the current UDQ.

Open in List View Presents the current UDQ in a standard list view and utilize all standard list view functions.

If you remove a column from a UDQ, the following objects are removed as well:

• Card views and chart views that use the UDQ as a data source.
• Linked list views that directly use or display the column.
• User-defined list views and home page tiles that are created from the UDQ.

Name

The field name returned from the SAP Business One database.

This field is non-editable.

Description Explanatory text for a field.

By default, this column displays field descriptions returned from the SAP Business One
database. You can edit the text if necessary.

The descriptions in this column determine the actual field names displayed on the Preview tab
below and are referenced by other UI elements within the Web client. For example, column
headers in table view of a list view, filter fields in the filter bar, and dimension or measure names
in chart view.

Type The type of a non-numeric field is Dimension and is non-editable.

The type of a numeric field can be either Measure or Dimension. The default type is Measure.

Dimensional fields contain qualitative values, such as names or dates. Measured fields contain
quantitative values that can be counted, calculated, or otherwise mathematically manipulated.

When you change a field type from Dimension to Measure, the values in the Aggregation and Decimal
Places columns revert to the defaults.

When you open the query in a list view, the type of a field determines whether the field falls in the
measures or dimensions group in chart view and card view.

Aggregation The default way that values of a field are summarized. When you open the query in a list view,

the aggregated result is displayed in the last row in table view.

The aggregation method is set to None for all non-numeric fields and is non-editable.

Numeric fields can be aggregated by the following methods:

• None

Field values are not aggregated.

• Sum

A sum of field values are calculated.

• Average

An average of field values are calculated.

• Count

The total number of field values are calculated.
When the aggregation method for a field is Count, a suffix "Count" is added to the value in
the Description column.

• Min

The minimum value of all field values is displayed.

• Max

Link
To

You can use this Link To dropdown list to build links based on alphanumeric fields between different
database tables. These alphanumeric fields are intended specifically for identification purposes, such
as customer codes or document numbers.

In SAP Business One, many business objects are represented by more than one database table. For
example, the sales order document uses different tables for the header and document rows. The table
ORDR stores the header data and the table RDR1 stores the document rows.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

649

By selecting a database table from the Link To dropdown list for an alphanumeric field, you build a
link based on the field from a source business object to a target business object which is associated
with a target database table. When you open the query in a list view, the field values are displayed as
linked texts. You can choose the linked field values to quickly access the associated business object
with identical field values.

For example, if you link a BP Code field that contains business partner code A00001 from a dataset
of sales order tables to the OCRD - Business Partners table, when you open the query in a list view,
you can choose the linked business partner code A00001 in the BP Code column to open the Business
Partner quick view, through which you can open the associated business partner master data of
A00001 in a detailed view.

Match
Unique ID
With

If an alphanumeric field contains overlapped values sourced from multiple database tables, you
can use this Match Unique ID With dropdown list, together with the Link To dropdown list, to set
combined conditions to uniquely identify a data record.

For example, your query retrieves results that contain two fields, Document Type and Document
No., from a dataset of sales quotations and sales orders. As sales quotations and sales orders can
have identical document numbers, one Document No. field value can be paired with two different
Document Type values.

In the Link To dropdown list for the Document No. field, select Document Type. As a result, the
associated Match Unique ID With dropdown list is enabled. Leave the field Match Unique ID With
blank to use Document No. as the default option, or choose Document No. from the dropdown
list.

By doing this, unique links from source document numbers to different types of business
objects with identical document numbers are built by matching source document numbers with
document type values, unique IDs of business objects of the same types, and eventually target
document numbers.

When you open the query in list view, you can choose a linked document number in the Document
No. column to open the corresponding sales quotation or sales order quick view with an identical
document number. Through the quick view, you can open the associated sales quotation or sales
order in a detailed view.

Original

The original SAP Business One database table from which a field is retrieved.

A predetermined value assigned to a parameter. This can help prevent errors and ensure that

Preview Tab

Use this tab to preview the first 1,000 results returned from the database.

In the Test Value column, the values are prefilled with default values where available.

3. Enter a specific value in the Test Value column for each parameter to verify the behavior of a query and

ensure that it produces the expected results when executed.
To revert your changes to the defaults, choose Reset.

4. Choose Run to test the query and check the test results on the Preview tab.

1.16.2.1.2  Creating User-Defined Queries Without Parameters

Context

When you create a user-defined query (UDQ) that doesn't include parameters, it is static and executes the
same operation every time without input variations. Such queries are straightforward and typically used for
fixed datasets or repeated operations that don't require input variability.

Procedure

1. Enter the User-Defined Query page in either of the following ways:

• In the Manage User-Defined Queries app, choose Create.
• From the Home page, choose  Main Menu Analytics User-Defined Queries Create .

2. Go to the General tab. Enter a descriptive name for your query in the Name field.

3. From the Category dropdown list, select a group to classify your query.

You can change the selected category after you save the query. If you change the category and save the
query again, please refresh the web page before you leave to avoid errors.

You can only change the category of a query in the Web client. You cannot change the category in the SAP
Business One client, though the categories available in the dropdown list are created and managed in the
SAP Business One client.

4. Enter a SELECT statement in the SQL Statement input box.

 Example

To view information on the total and open amounts, associated customers, posting and due dates, and
sales employees responsible for non-canceled sales orders, enter the following statement:

SELECT
    T0."DocEntry" AS "Document_Internal_Key",
    T0."DocNum" AS "Document_Number",
    T0."CardCode",
    T0."CardName",
    T0."DocDate",
    T0."DocDueDate",
    T1."InsTotal" AS "Total_Amount",
    T1."InsTotal" - T1."PaidToDate" AS "Open_Amount",
    CASE
        WHEN T0."SlpCode" = '-1' THEN T5."USER_CODE"
        ELSE T3."USER_CODE"
    END AS "Sales_Employee"
FROM
    ORDR T0
INNER JOIN
    RDR6 T1 ON T0."DocEntry" = T1."DocEntry"
LEFT JOIN
    OHEM T2 ON T0."SlpCode" = T2."salesPrson"
LEFT JOIN

652

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

    OUSR T3 ON T2."userId" = T3."USERID"
LEFT JOIN
    OHEM T4 ON T0."OwnerCode" = T4."empID"
LEFT JOIN
    OUSR T5 ON T4."userId" = T5."USERID"
WHERE
    T0."CANCELED" = 'N'

5. Choose Validate in the lower right corner of the input box to verify the statement.

Check the verification result in the Validation Result field. You can only save queries that pass the
validation.

6. Switch the Active button to Yes or No.

• Yes:

A UDQ is activated and available for use. For example, it is listed as an option in the Data Source
dropdown list when you create cards in the General Overview app and available as a linkable list view in
the Linked List Views app.

• No:

A UDQ is deactivated. You can view it within the User-Defined Queries app but cannot use it anywhere.

7. When the Active switch is on, the option Display as Tile on Home Page is available.

If you switch on this option, when the UDQ is created, the query will be displayed as a shortcut tile in the
Analytics group on the Home page. When you open the tile, the query is presented in a list view.

If a tile with the same name already exists on the Home page, the existing tile will be replaced.

If you switch off Display as Tile on Home Page for a query which already has an associated tile, the tile will
be deleted.

8. Go to the Columns tab. This tab shows all fields detected from your SQL statement and their properties.

Edit the properties in the columns as necessary.

9. Go to the Preview tab. Choose Preview Top 1000 Rows to view the first 1000 query results returned from

the database.

10. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the current query. You can then choose Open in List View in the header

toolbar to present the current UDQ in a standard list view and utilize all standard list view functions.

• Add & New: add the current query and open a new User-Defined Query page.
• Add & Back: add the current query and go back to the Manage User-Defined Queries page.

1.16.2.1.3  Creating User-Defined Queries with Parameters

Context

When you create a user-defined query (UDQ) that includes parameters, it allows for dynamic input. This
makes the queries flexible and reusable, as they can accept variable inputs each time they are executed. Such
queries are often used to filter results based on user-provided values or to execute the same query logic across
different datasets.

Procedure

1. Enter the User-Defined Query page in either of the following ways:

• In the Manage User-Defined Queries app, choose Create.
• From the Home page, choose  Main Menu Analytics User-Defined Queries Create .

2. Go to the General tab. Enter a descriptive name for your query in the Name field.

3. From the Category dropdown list, select a group to classify your query.

You can change the selected category after you save the query. If you change the category and save the
query again, please refresh the web page before you leave to avoid errors.

You can only change the category of a query in the Web client. You cannot change the category in the SAP
Business One client, though the categories available in the dropdown list are created and managed in the
SAP Business One client.

4. Enter a SELECT statement in the SQL Statement input box.

Use a colon (:) to denote a placeholder for a parameter, for example, :P. Parameter names can contain
only letters, numbers, underscores. Refrain from the use of the "@" symbol to avoid confusion with
User-Defined Tables.

 Example

Use the following example to retrieve sales order numbers for a specific customer where the document
total is at least a specific amount. In the example statement below, :MyCardCode is a parameter
placeholder for customer code, and :MyDocTotal for the document total. They are intended to be
replaced with default values before query execution and/or with test values for results preview.

Select "DocNum" from ORDR
Where "CardCode" = :MyCardCode
And "DocTotal" >= :MyDocTotal

5. Choose Validate in the lower right corner of the input box to verify the statement.

Check the verification result in the Validation Result field. You can only save queries that pass the
validation.

654

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

6.

Ignore the Active switch. It's currently non-functional.

7. Go to the Parameters tab. Review all parameters detected from your SQL statement and their properties.

8. Edit the text in the Description column as needed.

9. (Optional) In the Default Value column, enter a predetermined value for each parameter.

Make sure the values that you enter meet the parameter constraints.

To revert the Description column texts to the defaults, and clear all values in the Default Value column,
choose Reset.

 Example

In order to retrieve sales order numbers for customer BA01 with a document total of at least 1,000
dollars, you can enter default customer code BA01 for the parameter MyCardCode and default
document total 1000 for the parameter MyDocTotal.

10. Go to the Preview tab. Choose Preview Top 1000 Rows in the table toolbar.

11. The Preview dialog box appears, listing all parameters and their properties.

In the Test Value column, the values are prefilled with default values where available.

12. (Optional) Enter a specific value in the Test Value column for each parameter to verify the behavior of a

query and ensure that it produces the expected results when executed.

Make sure the values that you enter meet the parameter constraints.

To revert your changes to the default values, choose Reset.

 Note

If a parameter is defined with a Not Null constraint and does not have a default value assigned,
you need to provide a test value and preview the results before you can successfully add your SQL
statement.

13. Choose Run to test the query and check the first 1,000 results returned from the database that match your

conditions.

14. Choose one of the following options:

• Add & View: add and view the current query.
• Add & New: add the current query and open a new User-Defined Query page.
• Add & Back: add the current query and go back to the Manage User-Defined Queries page.

 Note

In the Web client, a parameterized query can currently only be previewed on this creation page. It
cannot be opened in a list view or used elsewhere.

1.16.3  Export and Import Views

Apps

In the Analytics group, you can find the Export and Import Views app.

Tasks

With this app, you can export and import the following data from one company to another:

• Views in built-in list views, user-defined list views, User-Defined Tables (UDTs) list views, User-Defined

Objects (UDOs) list views, and the General Overview app.

• Links to views in built-in list views, user-defined list views, UDTs list views, UDOs list views, and the General

Overview app.

 Note

The export and import of User-Defined Values (UDVs) are not performed within this app but rather in the
User-Defined Values app. For more information, see Managing User-Defined Values [page 830].

1.16.4  General Overview

App

In the Analytics group, you can find the General Overview app.

Tasks

With this app, you can view and adapt two sets of predefined analytical variant views. You can also create your
own view that contains cards from any of the existing analytical cubes.

The functions available on this page are similar to the individual overview pages. However, unlike those
individual pages, General Overview does not contain filter fields in the header. Since each card comes from
a different analytical cube, it contains its own independent set of queries (local filters). A global filter for all the
cubes would not be meaningful.

1.16.4.1  Predefined Views of General Overview

The General Overview page features two sets of predefined analytical variant views: the Standard view and the
Last 4 Completed Calendar Quarters view. You can use them as templates and adapt them according to your
specific analytical needs.

The Standard view is displayed by default. It consists of card templates with analytical data and insights that
can be tailored to your business.

After you choose Standard, the My Views popover appears, where you can switch to the Last 4 Completed
Calendar Quarters view.

The Last 4 Completed Calendar Quarters view consists of card templates grouped by calendar quarter. Each
group of analytical data is divided into 4 quarters and is presented with 4 separate cards. The number in the
card title indicates the quarter: -1 (minus one) means the last quarter, -2 means the second to the last quarter,
-3 means the third to the last quarter, and -4 means the fourth to the last quarter.

1.16.5  Linked List Views

App

In the Analytics group, you can find the Linked List Views app.

Tasks

With this app, you can create links from nearly any list views, or from the header or table section within
detailed views of applicable business records, to other list views or General Overview views that open in new
Web browser tabs. The linkable list views include those for system objects, user-defined objects (UDOs), user-
defined tables (UDTs), and user-defined queries (UDQs). This feature is designed to streamline micro business
processes, giving individual end users the ability to easily and quickly create personalized, context-relevant
information.

In the Linked List Views app, in the Linkable Objects menu in the left pane, you can see a collapsible list of all
the available target business documents and objects. When you choose each linkable object, you can find the
following submenus where applicable:

• List View:

• Use this option for linking from one list view to another list view or a General Overview view, and even

daisy-chaining list views.

• The linked list view or General Overview is additionally filtered by the selected field values from the

table area of the source list view.

• This option is applicable to almost all list views, such as the Business Partners list view.

 Example

purchasing data for them from the past year in the linked General Overview.

• Detailed View Header:

General Overview view.

header of the source detailed view.

• This option is applicable to almost all list views, except for list views created from UDQs.

that business partner. Choosing the link in the detailed view opens the Sales Orders list view in Open
Sales Orders view, which is additionally filtered by the business partner code from the current business
partner record.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client

671

1.18  Reports

SAP Business One, Web client provides both built-in and customizable reports, enabling you to generate
dynamic reports that tailor to your business needs.

Apps

In the Reports group, you can find the following tiles:

• Sales Analysis
• Profit and Loss Statement

The Sales Analysis report is available for all localizations. The Profit and Loss Statement is currently available
for the following localizations:

• Germany
• The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
• The United States of America and Puerto Rico

The reports in the Web client, while sharing the same names and source data as those in the SAP Business One
client, extend beyond simple period reporting through our enhancements.

Each Web client report page is divided into a header area and a table area, similar to a standard list view. In
particular, the table area consists of two parts: a hierarchical report table in the upper area and a Breakdown
table in the lower area.

The new hierarchical table enables business owners and analysts to group, aggregate, and summarize data
across multiple levels of rows and columns. This helps identify combined and segmented business and
operational indicators, thereby offering advanced insights. The Breakdown table serves as a complementary
tool. It offers a detailed examination of an amount or number aggregated in the hierarchical table. It enables
you to directly access the underlying source documents and transactions, facilitating deeper analysis and
informed decision-making.

In addition, the Web client versions of these SAP Business One reports offer two more enhancements:

• More flexible filtering conditions
• A greater range of visible fields

These Web client reports are completely independent and not linked or synchronized with those in the desktop
client. If you create new report views in the Web client, they do not automatically appear or get replicated in the
desktop client. Changes made in the Web client will not be synchronized with the desktop client, and vice versa.

General Authorizations

User access to the above reports is granted under the  Reports Web Client Reports  category in the
General Authorizations window in the SAP Business One client.

672

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

User access to business documents and objects that are set up in the SAP Business One client is automatically
applied to the accessibility of data in the Web client reports. Additionally, when your Web client reports include
User-Defined Tables or User-Defined Objects, your access to these tables or objects is determined by two
factors: the Apply Authorization setting applied during their creation in the Web client, and their specific
authorization configurations in the SAP Business One client.

For more information, see the guide How to Define Authorizations in SAP Business One 10.0 and the online help
topics Creating User-Defined Tables [page 816] and Creating a User-Defined Object [page 808].

Data Ownership Authorizations

Data ownership authorizations that are set up for business documents and objects by document owners,
business partner owners, and branches in the SAP Business One client are automatically applied to the
accessibility of data in the upper hierarchical table of each Web client report. However, you cannot apply data
ownership authorizations to control accessibility of detailed data in the lower Breakdown table of each Web
client report.

For more information, see the online help for Data Ownership.
