1.18.1  Working with Sales Analysis Report Views

To open the Sales Analysis report views, choose the Sales Analysis tile on the home page. Alternatively, choose

Reports Sales Analysis  from the Main Menu.

Sales Analysis report views offer advanced insights into sales metrics across multiple dimensions, extending
beyond simple period reporting. This helps identify combined and segmented sales performance indicators.
For example, you can analyze the best-selling products among the most-profitable clients over a rolling cycle of
years, quarters, and months.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

673

Selecting Views

A Sales Analysis report view page is divided into a header area and a table area, similar to a standard list view.
In particular, the table area consists of two parts: a hierarchical report table in the upper area and a Breakdown
table in the lower area.

The Web client offers multiple views for sales analysis reports. These views store distinct settings and
parameters for the filter bar in the header area, the hierarchical report table, and the Breakdown table. You
can select one of the predefined example report views from the views menu in the top-left corner of the header
area:

• Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item:

This view shows the analysis of gross profit and net sales by both customer and their associated items
over a rolling cycle of years and quarters. The figures in the hierarchical report are summarized from sale
invoice data starting from the first posting date to the present. This view enables businesses to evaluate
customer and item profitability and sales trends over time, aiding in strategic planning and optimizing sales
strategies.
This view is displayed by default.

• 5-Year Document Comparison:

This view shows a comparative analysis of net sales across different types of sales documents (delivery
and return documents, sales invoices, and sales orders) for individual items over the past five years. The
figures in the hierarchical report are summarized from sale invoice data starting from the first posting date.
With this view, businesses can evaluate the effectiveness of their sales strategies and identify which items
are performing well. It also helps in understanding the dynamics between different sales documents and
their impact on net sales.

• Invoice-Based Gross Profit by Customer:

This view shows the analysis of gross profit and document total amounts by customer over a rolling cycle
of years and quarters. The figures in the hierarchical report are summarized from sale invoice data starting
from the first posting date to the present. This view helps assess customer profitability and overall sales
performance, supporting strategic decision-making and enhancing customer relationship strategies.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

Use the filter bar to set conditions for the report view display and for filtering raw sales data from the
SAP Business One database. This filtered dataset is the basis for advanced analysis in the Sales Analysis
hierarchical report below and serves as the source data for the Breakdown table at the bottom.

674

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

The Web client offers various filter fields for applying conditions at the report, document, customer, and item
levels, including but not limited to the following:

Report
Granularity
Level

Choose the level of detail presented in the report view:

• Header Data Only:

This option analyzes data outside the Contents table area of sales documents. Line data
within the Contents table is excluded. It is the default for the built-in example report view
Invoice-Based Gross Profit by Customer.

• Both Header and Line Data:

This option analyzes all data inside and outside the Contents table area of sales
documents. It is the default for the built-in example report views: Quarterly Invoiced Sales
by Customer and Item and 5-Year Document Comparison.

This is a required filter field. It also determines selectable fields for the filter bar, the
hierarchical table, and the Breakdown table.

Document
Type

Choose one or more document types on which you want to build the report view:

• Invoices:

Invoice-type sales documents, such as A/R invoices.

• Orders:

Sales orders.
• Delivery Notes:

Delivery and return documents.

If no options are selected, the Web client treats it as if all three options are selected.

 Example

In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, the default is
Invoices.

In the example report view 5-Year Document Comparison, all three document types are
selected by default.

 Note

• A/R credit memos based on A/R down payment invoices are excluded.
• Canceled sales orders are excluded.
• Returns decrease sales amounts as part of delivery notes.
• As the report displays open quantities only, sales orders and delivery notes are
displayed with zero quantities and zero amounts in the following scenarios:
• The sales orders are closed or fully copied to either deliveries or A/R invoices.
• The delivery notes are closed or fully copied to either A/R invoices or returns.
Sales orders or delivery notes that were partially copied into target documents are listed
with remaining open quantities for deliveries or invoices.

For more information about how to use filters, see Filter Bar [page 54] and Working with Date Offset Filtering
[page 56].

1.18.1.1  Creating Sales Analysis Report Views

Prerequisites

2. Set custom filter conditions in the filter bar of the header area.

Procedure

1. Create a sales analysis hierarchical report in the report view.

1.

In the Sales Analysis table toolbar, choose  Select Columns to open the Select Columns dialog box.
Fields listed in this dialog box are sorted alphabetically by default. They are categorized into the
following:
• Measure fields

Measure fields contain quantitative values. They are numerical values that can be summed,
counted, or otherwise mathematically manipulated across records in the filtered dataset.

676

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Examples of measure fields include Gross Profit and Document Total. They provide insights into
overall sales performance over time or other categories.

• Dimension fields

Dimension fields contain qualitative values. They provide context to measures and aid in data
analysis by categorizing information. They are used to slice and dice data, offering views from
different perspectives. Dimension fields typically include descriptive data such as names, dates, or
geographical locations. They provide the "who," "what," "where," and "when" context for measures.
Examples include Customer Code and Posting Date.

2. Select desired dimension fields and at least one measure field to define your analytical purpose.

You can select only one date-type dimension field and up to five dimension fields in total. The fields
available for selection depends on your choice for the Report Granularity Level filter field.

3. Choose OK to confirm your selection and exit.

2. Adjust settings for the report table and the Breakdown table as needed.

3. Save the current view as a custom view.

Results

A sales analysis report view is created based on your settings.

The Sales Analysis report is presented in a hierarchical table. The selected dimension and measure fields are
automatically applied to group and aggregate data based on the filtered dataset by multiple levels of both rows
and columns.

Next to the table title, you can see linked text that summarizes the count of dimension fields used for both
row and column grouping. If you select a date field, it is by default visualized by sequential calendar years
and quarters in a two-level tree structure on the right side of the table header area. If you reopen the Select
Columns dialog box, the selected fields are resorted by their appearing order in the report.

 Example

• In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, in the Sales Analysis

hierarchical report, Customer Code and Item Code (Lines) are used as dimension fields, Posting Date as
a date field, and Gross Profit (Lines) and Net Sales Amount (Lines) as measure fields.

• In the example report view 5-Year Document Comparison, in the Sales Analysis hierarchical report, Item
Code (Lines) and Document Type are used as dimension fields, Posting Date as a date field, and Net
Sales Amount (Lines) as a measure field. Document Type is visualized as three specific types organized
in separate columns for each year: Delivery, Invoice, and Order. The document categories covered by
each type match those defined for the Document Type filter field in the filter bar.

• In the example report view Invoice-Based Gross Profit by Customer, in the Sales Analysis hierarchical
report, Customer Code is used as a dimension field, Posting Date as a date field, and Gross Profit Total
and Document Total as measure fields.

For information about how to view and adjust the Sales Analysis hierarchical report, as well as how to view and
adjust data breakdown, see the online help topics in the Related Information section.

1.18.1.2  Viewing Sales Analysis Report

The Sales Analysis report is presented in a hierarchical table that organizes rows and columns in a tree-like
format. This table helps you summarize, analyze, explore, and present summary sales data. Its structure
effectively manages data that naturally fits into nested categories or levels, providing clear insights and
reporting flexibility.

To maximize the report display, choose  Enter Full Screen in the table toolbar.

Row Structure

By default, non-date dimension fields serve as row-grouping categories. They appear in column headers on the
left side of the table.

The row hierarchy consists of multiple levels, where each level represents a different grouping category. The
first column category has the highest level. You can choose  Expand/Collapse next to each field value at an
upper level to view associated values in separate lower-level rows.

The last row in the hierarchy displays totals for the subtotals in each measure column.

 Example

In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, rows in the first column are
grouped by customer code, while those in the second column are grouped by item code. By expanding each
value in the Customer Code column, you can see all items sold to each different customer listed in the Item
Code (Lines) column. This allows for a detailed examination of sales per customer and item.

Column Structure

The column hierarchy features multiple levels organized on the right side of the table.

When you select a date field from the Select Columns dialog box, it is by default placed at the top level
of the hierarchy, visualized as a two-layer structure that represents a rolling cycle of years and quarters in
ascending order. The first layer shows sequential calendar years, while the second layer breaks each year into
four quarterly columns.

678

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

By default, measure fields function as column-grouping categories and are the smallest components in the
column hierarchy. They are organized in separate columns and appear as branches under each upper-level
column.

In addition, a Total column is placed between the last non-date dimension column and the date columns. This
column provides totals at different row levels over the specified date period or other dimensions, calculated for
the selected measures.

 Example

In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, the column hierarchy is
structured into three distinct levels:

• Top Level:

Displays each calendar year in separate columns.

• Second Level:

Each year is further divided into four calendar quarters.

• Third Level:

Each quarter contains branches for two separate measure fields: Gross Profit Total (Lines) and Net
Sales Amount (Lines).

This structure allows for an organized and detailed examination of these financial metrics within each
quarterly time frame.

Additionally, following the Item Code (Lines) column, there is a Total column with the measure fields
branched out, enhancing the ease of comprehensive analysis.

Parent-Child Relationships

The data in the hierarchical report is connected through parent-child relationships, where higher-level data is
summarized or aggregated from lower-level data.

This relationship allows for drill-down and roll-up operations, which are useful for detailed and summary views
of data.

Data Aggregation

The hierarchical report enables data aggregation at different levels.

 Example

In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, data aggregation is visible
across multiple hierarchical levels:

• Year and Quarter Level:

Aggregated amounts for Gross Profit (Lines) and Net Sales Amount (Lines) are shown for each quarter
within each year.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

679

• Customer Level:

These measures are also aggregated for each customer, providing insights into sales performance per
customer.
• Item Level:

Aggregation applies to each item associated with each customer, allowing for detailed analysis of
product performance.

• Total Level:

Overall aggregated figures are available, offering a summary of gross profit and net sales amounts.

The aggregated values for gross profit and net sales are computed based on all filtered individual sales
invoice records, providing a clear picture of financial performance across different dimensions.

Direct Access to Master Data

In the hierarchical table, dimension fields with values linked to master data offer a convenient way to access
detailed information directly. By choosing the golden arrow ( ) next to such values, you can seamlessly view
related master data.

 Example

In the example report view Quarterly Invoiced Sales by Customer and Item, choosing   beside a Customer
Code value opens the Business Partner quick view. This provides a concise overview of the chosen
customer. To explore further, choose View More in the quick view to open the detailed view of the
corresponding business partner master data either in a new browser tab or within the current tab.

1.18.1.3  Adjusting Sales Analysis Report

After creating your initial Sales Analysis report in the hierarchical table, you can dynamically restructure, sort,
and filter data to better suit your analysis needs.

Next to the table title, you can see linked text that summarizes the count of dimension fields used for both row
and column grouping. Choose this linked text to open a popover menu for report adjustments.

Changing Row Structure

In the Group Rows By section of the popover menu, row categories are listed from left to right by their
appearing order and hierarchical levels in the table.

To change the hierarchical level of a row category, simply drag and drop the corresponding field label to your
preferred position.

The change in field order is also synchronized with the Select Columns dialog box when accessed from the
table toolbar.

Changing Column Structure

Similar to rows, in the Group Columns By section, column categories are listed by appearing order and
hierarchy.

To change the hierarchical level of a column category, drag and drop the corresponding field label as needed.

The change in field order is also synchronized with the Select Columns dialog box when accessed from the
table toolbar.

 Note

You cannot drag and drop field labels between the Group Rows By and Group Columns By sections.

Adjusting Column Settings

Choose a field label in the Group Rows By or Group Columns By section to open a new Column Settings popover
menu.

Alternatively, you can open the Column Settings popover menu by directly choosing a column header in the
hierarchical table. This menu is only available for dimension fields.

The menu consists of the following sections:

Sort By

To sort data in the chosen column field in ascending or descending order, choose  Ascending or
 Descending on the right of the field name.

As a result, you are navigated back to the parent popover menu. In the parent menu, a new Sort By section
appears, where your sort preference is listed as a label.

In the hierarchical table, the sorted state is indicated by 1 Sorted at the end of the linked text near the
table title. The respective sort icon appears in the column header (except for date columns). The data in the
corresponding column is reordered accordingly, together with the associated values in the measure columns.

To clear your sort preference, choose  Remove within the sort label in the Sort By section of the parent
popover menu.

Adjusting Date Dimension

When you choose the On or Off row for a date field, a Group Columns By or Group Rows By popover submenu

• Year

• Month

Your selection is visualized in the hierarchy of the final report:

• To build a report focused on a specific time frame (yearly, quarterly, monthly, or daily), select a single

option.

• To build a report that spans a combined time frame, such as years and months, select multiple options.

 Note

Some option combinations are invalid. For example, selecting Year and Day without Month is not
supported. The Web client cannot structure the data properly because it needs the Month level to link
days to their correct years.

Removing Grouping Categories

Filter By

1.18.1.4  Viewing and Adjusting Data Breakdown

The Breakdown table at the bottom of the Sales Analysis report view page serves as a complementary tool to
the hierarchical table above. It offers a detailed examination of aggregated amounts or numbers, enabling you
to drill down to the underlying source sales documents and associated journal entry transactions directly. This
facilitates deeper analysis and helps in making informed decisions.

Dynamic Data Breakdown

By default, the Breakdown table shows all underlying sales data records that meet the filter conditions set in
the filter bar. The table content dynamically updates according to both the Report Granularity Level and your
selection in the hierarchical table:

• If the Report Granularity Level is Header Data Only:

• When you choose an amount or number cell in a measure column, the Breakdown table lists all
individual sales documents or transactions that contribute to that specific amount or number.
• When you choose a value cell in a dimension column, such as a specific customer or item, the

Breakdown table lists all individual sales documents or transactions that affect the row totals for the
selected measures in the Total column.

• If the Report Granularity Level is Both Header and Line Data:

• When you choose an amount or number cell in a measure column, the Breakdown table individually

lists all item records of each sales document or transaction that contribute to that specific amount or
number.

• When you choose a value cell in a dimension column, such as a specific customer or item, the

Breakdown table individually lists all item records of each sales document or transaction that affect the
row totals for the selected measures in the Total column.

• If you choose an empty cell in any column, no data breakdown is shown.

The last row in the table displays subtotals for all amounts or numbers of each measure column selected from
the hierarchical table.

Information about the row and column of the chosen cell is presented in an information strip located between
the hierarchical and Breakdown tables.

In the Document No. or Transaction Number column of the Breakdown table, choose   next to a number.
The sales invoice or Journal Entry quick view opens, showing an overview of the chosen document or

3. Choose View More in the quick view to open the detailed view of the corresponding invoice or journal entry.

If the Breakdown table includes dimension fields with values linked to master data (for example, the Customer
Code field), you can also access the master data by choosing the golden arrow ( ) next to a field value.

Flexible Table Settings

You can customize how and what breakdown data is displayed in the table.

• View Data in Full Screen:

In the table toolbar, choose  Enter Full Screen to maximize the data display.

• Select Visible Columns:

In the table toolbar, choose  Select Columns to open the Select Columns dialog box. Select fields that you
want to see in the table.
The fields available for selection depends on your choice for the Report Granularity Level filter field.

• Sort and Filter Data:

To sort column headers, adjust their order in the Select Columns dialog box.
To sort and filter data in a column, choose the column header to open the Column Settings popover menu.
The sort and filter options here are similar to those in the popover menu of the hierarchical table.

 Note

In the following scenarios, all quantitative data will be cleared from the report:

• If you change Report Granularity Level from Header Data Only to Both Header and Line Data in the filter
bar after creating a report view, all selected measure fields will be removed from the current view. This
happens because their calculation mechanisms do not apply to the new granularity level.

• If you change from Both Header and Line Data to Header Data Only, all measure fields of your selection
and line fields originating from the Contents table of sales documents will be removed from the current
view.

To prevent data loss, save your current view beforehand. This involves data and settings in the filter bar,
the hierarchical table, and the Breakdown table. After switching the report granularity, you can add new
measure and dimension fields in the new view to create a report.

1.18.2  Working with Profit and Loss Statement Report Views

To open the Profit and Loss Statement report views, choose the Profit and Loss Statement tile on the home

page. Alternatively, choose  Reports Profit and Loss Statement

 from the Main Menu.

The Profit and Loss Statement is a financial report that provides an overview of a company's financial
performance that spans a specific or combined time frame (such as years and months), by summarizing
the balances of revenues, costs, and expenses recorded in general ledger (G/L) accounts. It begins with
total revenues generated from business operations, deducts the cost of goods sold (COGS) to determine
gross profit, and further subtracts operational and non-operational expenses to reveal the net income. This
statement serves as a crucial tool for assessing profitability and guiding managerial decisions.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

Selecting Views

A Profit and Loss Statement report view page is divided into a header area and a table area, similar to a
standard list view. In particular, the table area consists of two parts: a hierarchical report table in the upper area
and a Breakdown table in the lower area.

The Web client offers multiple views for profit and loss statement reports. These views store distinct settings
and parameters for the filter bar in the header area, the hierarchical report table, and the Breakdown table. You
can select one of the predefined example report views from the views menu in the top-left corner of the header
area:

• 5-Year Quarterly Analysis:

This view shows the profit and loss statement for each quarter within the calendar years spanning the past
five years to the present. This view allows for detailed analysis of how each quarter performed within each
year, providing insights into seasonal trends or quarterly fluctuations.
This view is displayed by default.

• 5-Year Fiscal Review:

This view shows the profit and loss statement for fiscal years spanning the past five years to the
present. This view provides a broader, year-by-year perspective that is ideal for evaluating overall financial
performance.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

1.18.2.1  Creating Profit and Loss Statement Report Views

Prerequisites

1. Open a predefined example report view.

2. Set custom filter conditions in the filter bar of the header area.

688

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Procedure

1. Create a Profit and Loss Statement hierarchical report in the report view.

1.

In the Profit and Loss Statement table toolbar, choose  Select Columns to open the Select Columns
dialog box.
Fields listed in this dialog box are sorted alphabetically by default. They are categorized into the
following:
• Measure fields

Measure fields contain quantitative values. They are numerical values aggregated across records
in the filtered dataset. They offer insights into overall financial performance over time.
You can choose the following measure fields:
• Balance (available in local currency (LC), system currency (SC), and foreign currency (FC)):
The difference between the total debits and total credits recorded in an account within the
general ledger.

• Life-to-Date (available in local currency (LC) and system currency (SC)):

The cumulative total amount of an account from the inception of the company up to today or a
specific end date.
The Life-to-Date balance provides a comprehensive overview of a company's long-term
financial performance. It is useful for understanding the growth and profitability of the
company over its entire lifespan, offering insights into its sustained performance and financial
health.

• Year-to-Date (available in local currency (LC) and system currency (SC)):

This figure represents a cumulative total for an account, calculated within each individual fiscal
year. The calculation always starts from the first day of a fiscal year. If you break a calendar or
fiscal year down into periods such as quarters or months, the figure shown for each period is
the cumulative total from the start of the fiscal year up to the end of that period. This figure
doesn't accumulate across multiple historical years; it resets annually. For a running total that
accumulates over all specified years or periods, see the Total column in the final report.
The Year-to-Date balance helps stakeholders understand how the company is performing in
the current year relative to past performance or future projections. It can be used to make
informed decisions about budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning for the remainder of
the year.

• Dimension fields

Dimension fields contain qualitative values. They provide context to measures and aid in profit and
loss analysis by categorizing information.
You can choose the following dimension fields:
• Account Name:

This is a required field. It contains multiple levels of accounts and metrics defined in the
selected Chart of Accounts template.

• Posting Period:

Choose this field to organize the report table by fiscal year, period code, or both.

• Date:

Choose this field to organize the report table over a specific time frame (yearly, quarterly,
monthly, or daily), or a combined time frame (such as years and months).

 Note

• You can choose up to one date field. You cannot choose both Posting Period and Date.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

689

• If you choose a date field, make sure that a valid date range is already specified in the

Date Period field in the filter bar.

• If you choose Posting Period along with Year-to-Date, Life-to-Date, or both, make sure

that the following conditions are met in the filter bar for accurate analysis:
• The date type Posting Date is selected for the Date field.
• A valid date range is specified in the Date Period field.
This is because when you organize a report by Posting Period, it groups and
summarizes transaction data based on posting date. Filtering the raw report data by
a different date type, such as Due Date, will lead to inaccurate results because these
dates are often different and mixing them creates a mismatch.

2. Select desired measure and dimension fields to define your analytical purpose.

You can move measure fields up and down to determine their appearing order in the report table.

3. Choose OK to confirm your selection and exit.

2. Adjust the date dimension and the Breakdown table settings as needed.

3. Save the current view as a custom view.

Results

A profit and loss statement report view is created based on your settings.

The Profit and Loss Statement report is presented in a hierarchical table. The selected dimension and measure
fields appear as column headers in the report table.

Next to the table title, you can see linked text that summarizes the count of dimension fields used for both row
and column grouping. If you select a date field, it is by default visualized by sequential fiscal or calendar years in
separate columns. In the report, the balances at different account levels are aggregated or calculated from the
filtered dataset of journal entries recorded in these accounts.

 Example

• In the example report view 5-Year Quarterly Analysis, in the Profit and Loss Statement hierarchical

report, Account Name is used as a dimension field, Date as a date field, and Balance as a measure field.
The balances at different account levels are aggregated or calculated from journal entries recorded in
the related accounts, with posting dates falling within this five-year span.

• In the example report view 5-Year Fiscal Review, in the Profit and Loss Statement hierarchical report,
Account Name is used as a dimension field, Posting Period as a date field, and Balance and Balance
(SC) as measure fields.

To remove a field from your report, open the Select Columns dialog box and deselect the field.

1.18.2.2  Viewing and Adjusting Profit and Loss Statement

Report

The Profit and Loss Statement report is presented in a hierarchical table that organizes rows and columns in
a tree-like format. This table helps you summarize, analyze, explore, and present your company's financial
performance. It effectively reflects balance data across nested levels of general ledger (G/L) accounts for
revenues, costs, and expenses, providing clear insights into your company’s profitability.

To maximize the report display, choose  Enter Full Screen in the table toolbar.

Row Structure

By default, the Account Name field appears in the first column of the table.

The row hierarchy consists of multiple levels. It conforms to the G/L accounts levels defined in the Chart of
Accounts template of your choice. The levels visible in the table depends on your choice for the Level filter field
in the filter bar. You can choose  Expand/Collapse next to an account name at an upper level to view its child
accounts in separate lower-level rows.

If you use the default Chart of Accounts template, in addition to the hierarchical G/L accounts for revenues,
costs, and expenses, you can see the following financial metrics at the root level in the Account Name column:

• Gross Profit:

Gross Profit is a financial metric that represents the difference between a company's revenue and the cost
of goods sold (COGS) over a specific period.
The formula to calculate Gross Profit is: Gross Profit = Revenue − Cost of Goods Sold (COGS).

• Operating Profit:

Operating Profit is a measure of a company's profitability from its core business activities, excluding any
income or expenses not directly related to its core operations. It represents the profit a company makes
from its normal business operations before accounting for interest and taxes.
The formula to calculate Operating Profit is: Operating Profit = Gross Profit − Operating Expenses

• Profit After Financing Expenses:

Profit After Financing Expenses, also known as Earnings Before Tax (EBT), is a financial metric that
represents a company's profit after accounting for all operating and financing expenses but before income
taxes are deducted.
The formula to calculate Profit After Financing Expenses is: Profit After Financing Expenses =
Operating Profit − Interest Expenses

• Profit Period:

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

691

Profit Period refers to Net Profit for a specific period. It reflects how much profit a company has made over
that period, such as a quarter or fiscal year. Net Profit is the final measure of a company's profitability after
all expenses, including operating expenses, interest, taxes, and any other costs, have been deducted from
total revenue.
The formula for Net Profit is: Net Profit = Total Revenue − Total Expenses

If you use a custom Chart of Accounts template, the financial metrics may vary according to your settings
in the Group Data section during the template creation in the Financial Report Templates window in the SAP
Business One client.

The last row in the table shows total balances for subtotals in each measure column.

Column Structure

The column hierarchy features multiple levels organized on the right side of the table.

If you select the Date or Posting Period field from the Select Columns dialog box, it is by default placed at the
top level of the hierarchy, visualized as sequential calendar or fiscal years in separate columns.

By default, measure fields are the smallest components in the column hierarchy. They are organized in
separate columns and appear as branches under each upper-level column.

In addition, a Total column is placed between the Account Name column and the date columns. This column
provides totals at different row levels for each account over the specified date period, calculated for the
selected measures.

 Example

In the example report view 5-Year Quarterly Analysis, the column hierarchy is structured into three distinct
levels:

• Top Level:

Displays each calendar year in separate columns.

• Second Level:

Each year is further divided into four calendar quarters.

• Third Level:

Each quarter has a Balance column.

Additionally, following the Account Name column, there is a Total column. This enhances the ease of
comprehensive analysis.

Adjusting Date Dimension

To further adjust the date dimension for a more segmented analysis, proceed as follows:

1. Choose the linked text beside the table title to open a popover menu.

2. Go to the Group Columns By section. Choose the date field label to open the Column Settings popover

menu.

3. Go to the Group By section. Choose the row Group Columns By: <Field Name> to open the Group

Columns By popover menu.

4. The time intervals available for selection vary according to your date field:

• If the selected date field is Posting Period, you can choose whether to organize the report by Fiscal Year

or Period Code, or both. Fiscal Year is selected by default.

• If the selected date field is Date, you can choose the following time intervals, where Year is selected by

default:
• Year
• Quarter
• Month
• Day
Your selection is visualized in the column hierarchy of the final report:
• To present a report focused on a specific time frame (yearly, quarterly, monthly, or daily), select a

single option.

• To present a report that spans a combined time frame, such as years and months, select multiple

options.

 Note

Some option combinations are invalid. For example, selecting Year and Day without Month is
not supported. The Web client cannot structure the data properly because it needs the Month
level to link days to their correct years.

To remove the date field, go back to the popover menu opened by choosing the linked text, and choose
 Remove within the field label.

Parent-Child Relationships

The data in the hierarchical report is connected through parent-child relationships, where higher-level data is
aggregated or calculated from lower-level data.

This relationship allows for drill-down and roll-up operations, which are useful for detailed and summary views
of data.

Data Aggregation

The hierarchical report enables data aggregation at different levels.

 Example

In the example report view5-Year Quarterly Analysis, data aggregation is visible across multiple hierarchical
levels:

• Year and Quarter Level:

Aggregated account balances are shown for each quarter within each year.

• Account Level:

Balances are also aggregated for each level of G/L accounts.

different G/L accounts and financial metrics.

1.18.2.3  Viewing and Adjusting Data Breakdown

The Breakdown table at the bottom of the Profit and Loss Statement report view page serves as a
complementary tool to the hierarchical table above. It offers a detailed examination of amounts aggregated
or calculated for G/L accounts, enabling you to drill down to the underlying source journal entries directly. This
facilitates a more granular analysis, promoting transparency, offering deeper insights, and supporting effective
decision-making.

Dynamic Data Breakdown

By default, the Breakdown table shows all individual entries from journal entry documents that meet the
filter conditions set in the filter bar. The table content dynamically updates according to your selection in the
hierarchical table:

• If you choose an amount cell in a measure column for a G/L account, the Breakdown table individually lists
all entries from each journal entry document recorded in that G/L account, contributing to that specific
amount.

• If you choose a G/L account in the Account Name column, the Breakdown table individually lists all entries
from each journal entry document recorded in that G/L account, affecting the row totals for the selected
measures in the Total column.

• If you choose an empty cell in any column, no data breakdown is shown.
• If you choose an amount related to the following metrics or measure fields, no data breakdown is shown.
Because these metrics and measure fields contain calculated results and are not the direct G/L accounts
where journal entries are recorded.
• Metrics in the default Chart of Accounts template:

• Gross Profit
• Operating Profit
• Profit After Financing Expenses
• Profit Period
• Measure Fields:
• Life-to-Date

694

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Life-to-Date (SC)
• Year-to-Date
• Year-to-Date (SC)

• If you use a custom Chart of Accounts template, this limit extends to subtotals defined in the Group
Data section during the template creation in the Financial Report Templates window in the SAP
Business One client.

The last row in the table displays subtotals for all amounts of each measure column selected from the
hierarchical table.

Information about the row and column of the chosen cell is presented in an information strip located between
the hierarchical and Breakdown tables.

2.

number.

3. The Journal Entry quick view opens, showing an overview of the chosen transaction.

4. Choose View More in the quick view to open the detailed view of the corresponding journal entry.

In addition, you can access other accounting information closely related to a journal entry through the following

Choosing the golden arrow next to a field value opens a G/L Account quick view, through which you can

access details of the control account where the journal entry is recorded.

• Corresponding Account:

Choosing the golden arrow next to a field value opens a G/L Account quick view, through which you can
access details of the offset account for the journal entry posting.

To narrow down the data in a column, proceed as follows:

by linked text, 1 Filtered, at the end of the table title. The respective filter icon appears in the column
header. The column data is refreshed based on your applied condition. Choosing the linked text opens
a popover menu, where your filter condition is listed as a label in the Filter By section.
To clear your filter condition, choose  Remove within the filter label.

1.19.1.2  Working with Definitions

Definition pages allow you to define and maintain simple and detailed object data used for configuration
throughout the Web client. The definition pages can consist of a simple definition page (that has an Edit button)
and a detailed definition page (that has a Create button).

Prerequisites

You have the full authorization set in the SAP Business One client for the object for which you want to define
new values.

Working with Simple Definitions

When you choose to maintain simple definitions, you can edit existing entries or add new entries for the object
in the form of a list.

Context

You want to edit existing entries or add new entries for an object with a definition page. For example, you want
to change the effective discount for a particular customer/vendor group in Customer Groups or Vendor Groups.

1.

In the Administration group, click the Configuration tile. Alternatively, choose  Administration

Configuration  in the Main Menu.

2.

In the left pane of the Configuration page, select the relevant category or app group.
You can also enter the name of the object in the search field. In this case, Web client navigates you directly
to the definition screen for the object.

3. The objects related to the selected category or app group are displayed. Click the link for the object that

4.

5.

you want to modify.

In the definition page for the object, choose the Edit button.

In the editable table, you can do the following:
• To add a new entry, specify the values for each field in the last row.
• To update existing values in the table, modify any of the editable fields.
• To delete an entry, select the checkbox for the relevant entry and choose the Delete button.
You can also use the filter bars in the header of the screen to apply filter fields to the entries in the table.
For more information on how to work with list views, see Working with List Views [page 53]

6. Choose the Save button.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

699

Working with Detailed Definitions

The definition pages provide a list of the existing entries. When you choose to maintain detailed definitions, you
can edit existing entries or add new entries for the object in different views. In the definition list view, you can
search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records currently displayed in the table area, and
perform various actions with the records. From the definition list view, you can select a record to edit or update,
or create a new record. You can navigate to the detailed view of a specific definition by clicking  Details on the
row of the relevant definition or by clicking anywhere on the row. In the definition detailed view, you can add or
update relevant details displayed in the content area and structured in a series of tabs.

Context

You want to edit existing entries or add new entries for an object with a definition page. For example, you want
to add a new item group.

1.

In the Administration group, click the Configuration tile. Alternatively, choose  Administration

Configuration  in the Main Menu.

2.

In the left pane of the Configuration screen, select the relevant category or app group.
You can also enter the name of the object in the search field. In this case, Web client navigates you directly
to the definition screen for the object.

3. The objects related to the selected category or app group are displayed. Click the link for the object that

you want to modify.

4.

In the object definition list view, you can search for specific definitions, use filters, add columns to the table
area and remove definitions. For more information on how to work with list views, see Working with List
Views [page 53].

5. From the definition list view, you can navigate to the detailed view by doing one of the following:

• To create a new definition, choose the Create button.
• To update an existing definition, click  Details on the row of the relevant definition (or anywhere on the

definition's row), and then choose the Edit button.

6.

In the definition detailed view, you can perform various actions, such as Duplicate and Delete. In addition,
you can add or update relevant details in the different fields. For more information on how to work with
detailed views, see Working with Detailed Views [page 83].

7. Choose the Update button.

1.19.1.4  Approval Process

In some companies, approval from managers or senior members is required for certain documents, for
example, for purchase orders over $20,000 or for those issued by junior employees. With SAP Business One,
you can set up approval processes for various documents, under various conditions, and for different types of
employees.

In the course of an approval process, messages are automatically sent to the approval process originator (the
user who attempts to generate or update a document) and the authorizers to give timely updates on the
status of the approval request. The authorizers approve or reject the request after reviewing the document.
The approval process originator proceeds with the document generation or update according to the approval
process result.

In the Approval Process menu, you can configure settings and manage preexisting data for business documents
and objects used in the approval process.

To access the Approval Process menu, from the home page, choose  Main Menu Administration

Configuration Approval Process .

This menu consists of the following submenus:

Settings:

• Approval Process Settings

Definitions:

• Approval Stages
• Approval Templates
• Templates
• Substitute Authorizers

714

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

1.19.1.4.1  Approval Process Settings

On the Approval Process Settings page, you can enable the approval process function for the creation of sales,
purchasing, and inventory documents.

To access this page, from the home page, choose  Main Menu Administration Configuration Approval

Process Approval Process Settings .

To configure settings for a specific document type, follow these steps:

1. Choose the corresponding tab.

2. Choose Edit.

3. Make changes according to your business needs. Choose Update to save your changes.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

You can make the following settings:

• Enable Approval Process

Select the checkbox to enable the approval process in your company.
If the logged in user is an originator in any of the approval process templates then the user cannot change
this setting.

• Enable Approval Process in Data Interface (DI)

Enables the approval process in the DI

• Allow Update of Document Generated/Updated by Approval Process

Enables the update of the document that has been generated or updated by the approval process.

• Allow Originator to Update Document Draft in Pending/Approved Status

Enables the originator to update a document draft that is awaiting approval or has been approved by the
authorizer.

• Allow Authorizer to Update Document Draft in Pending Status

Enables the authorizer to update a document draft that was created by the originator and is awaiting
approval.

• Send Approval Process Notification via Email

Enables the originators and authorizers to receive the notifications via email, in addition to the notifications
in the system. To use this function, the Enable Mailer Service checkbox on the Services tab of the General
Settings window in the SAP Business One client must be selected, and the mailer service must be running.
For more information about starting the mailer service, see the SBO Mailer section in the Administrator’s
Guide provided with SAP Business One or SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA. You can then select to
use either of the following options to send the emails:
• SAP Business One Mailer: this is the default option. To use this option, senders and receivers must
have an email address defined on the General tab of the Users – Setup window in the SAP Business
One client, and the mailer service must be configured. For more information about configuring the
mailer service, see the SBO Mailer section in the Administrator’s Guide provided with SAP Business
One or SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA.

• SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration: To use this option, senders and receivers must have

an email address defined on the General tab of the Users – Setup window in the SAP Business One
client, Microsoft 365 integration must be set up, and the Microsoft 365 account of the user Workflow

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

715

must be bound to SAP Business One Microsoft 365 integration. For more information about setting up
Microsoft 365 integration, see How to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration.

In the email body, there is a link to the draft or generated document. It is an external access URL if you have
mapped external addresses to internal addresses for component Web Client for SAP Business One in the
SLD control center. This enables you to access the documents from outside the local network. The draft
document link will direct you to the draft document, even if the approval process ends or is canceled. For
marketing documents, you can approve or reject the draft directly from the draft document link. For other
documents, go to the Approval Decisions list view and decide what to do with those requests. To check the
results of sending the emails, go to the Sent Messages tab of the Messages/Alerts Overview window in the
SAP Business One client, and select the corresponding message.

 Note

When the prerequisites for using this function are not met, only the email notification is not sent; the
approval process continues without any impact.

The competitor names that you specify here appear as options in the dropdown list of the Name column in the

name from the dropdown list, the associated threat level and details that you define here are automatically
filled in the Threat Level and Remarks columns respectively in the Competitors tab of the opportunity page.

Industries

In the Name column, specify the industries where the customers or the leads of your sales opportunities are
from, or where the vendors of your purchasing opportunities are from, using a maximum of 40 characters. The
specified names appear as options in the Industry dropdown list in the Business Partner Details section in the
General tab of an opportunity page when you create or edit an opportunity.

Information Sources

In the Name column, specify the catalyst for initial customer or vendor interest using a maximum of 30
characters. Possible sources include online advertisements, newspaper articles, exhibitions, and personal
contacts. The specified sources appear as options in the Information Source dropdown list in the Opportunity
Details section in the General tab of an opportunity page when you create or edit an opportunity.

In the Sort column, specify a positive integer to determine the sort order of the information source options
in the dropdown list. The smaller the sort number, the higher the option appears in the dropdown list. For
example, if you specify the number 1 for information source Online Advertisements and the number 2 for
Newspaper Articles, Online Advertisements appears as the first option in the dropdown list, followed
by Newspaper Articles.

Interest Ranges

In the Description column, specify the scope of customer or vendor interests using a maximum of 30
characters, such as real estate or health care. The specified values appear as options in the dropdown list
of the Description column in the Interest Range section in the Potential tab of an opportunity page when you
create or edit an opportunity.

In the Sort column, specify a positive integer to determine the sort order of the interest range options in the
dropdown list. The smaller the sort number, the higher the option appears in the dropdown list. For example, if
you specify the number 1 for interest range Real Estate and the number 2 for Health Care, Real Estate
appears as the first option in the dropdown list, followed by Health Care.

Levels of Interest

In the Description column, specify the degree of customer or vendor interests using a maximum of 30
characters, such as Very Interested. The specified values appear as options in the Level of Interest
dropdown list in the Potential tab of an opportunity page when you create or edit an opportunity.

On the Sales and Purchasing Settings page, you can configure the general settings for sales and purchasing
documents.

To access this page, from the home page, choose  Main Menu Administration Configuration Sales and

Purchasing Sales and Purchasing Settings .

To configure settings for a specific document type, follow these steps:

1. Choose the corresponding tab with the desired document type name.

2. Choose Edit.

3. Make changes according to your business needs. Choose Update to save your changes.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

Sales and Purchasing Tab

Preferences Section

Rounding
Method

It is common to round amounts and prices in payments and marketing documents. In the Web
client you can select a rounding method to be used when rounding is required:

• By Currency

Select this option if you want to work with rounding account per currency. You have to define
the following parameters:

Administration

In
required rounding method for each currency, and define the display of the decimals and
whether the payments generated with this currency should be rounded.

 Currencies , determine the

 define a rounding account. The differences

between the original amount and the rounded amount are displayed in the Rounding field
of the marketing document and posted to this account. This is why the total of the credit and
the debit in the transaction created by the document is different from the document total.
The rounding of the amount appears in the Total field and is performed according to the
definitions made for the currency in all the documents. You can edit the amount that
appears in this field (before the document is added) by selecting the Rounding checkbox.

• By Document

definitions for each currency. For each type of sales document, you can determine whether it
should be rounded.

Display Remark
When Rounding

Select to determine whether a remark will be displayed in the Remarks field of the sales
document when an amount has been rounded. If you select the checkbox, a remark in a
foreign-currency invoice for a customer is displayed stating that the discount amount is
different from the discount percentage due to rounding.

Block Documents with Earlier
Posting Date

Select to disable the creation of a document with a posting date that is
earlier than today.

Allow
Future
Posting
Date

Select this checkbox to enable the posting of documents to a date that is later than the current
system date.

If you enable this function but also block the same documents with earlier posting dates
(controlled by the Block Documents with Earlier Posting Date checkbox), you may produce some
unwanted effects on your bookkeeping. For example, on 5 April, 2014, you add an A/R invoice
with the posting date of 6 April, 2014. As you block adding A/R invoices with earlier posting
dates, you cannot add any A/R invoice with a posting date that is earlier than 6 April, 2014.

Allow One Series
for Multiple
Document Types

Certain country/region regulations permit document numbering series that contain more
than one document type. All of these documents are part of the same numbering series.

Select this option if these regulations are relevant for the company. This setting
determines the settings that are displayed in certain Document Numbering views, and
cannot be changed after it has been selected.

Separate Net and
Gross Price Mode

Select the checkbox to enable the separation of price modes for sales and purchasing
transactions. Once this option is enabled, the prices that are entered and calculated in
the same transaction must be in the same mode.

 Note

You cannot deselect this checkbox after adding sales or purchasing documents to the
application.

Manage Freight

Select to add a Freight field in all sales and purchasing documents. This field lets
you calculate additional costs connected to a document, such as delivery charges and
deposit tax.

Copy Opening and
Closing Remarks to Target
Documents

When choosing Copy To in marketing documents, opening and closing remarks
are copied to the target document if this option is selected. Opening and closing
remarks are free-text fields with 256,000 characters.

Copy Document References
from Original Documents to
Duplicates

This checkbox ensures that if you duplicate any document with existing
document references, the document references are automatically copied
from the original document to its duplicate.

Copy Price List from
Base Document to Target
Document

Select this checkbox to enable copying the price list from base documents to the
target document.

If the base documents use different price lists, the target document uses the price
list defined on the Payment Terms tab of the business partner's record.

Inventory and Logistics Section

When Release or
Receipt of
Inventory is
Outside Range

You can define the system response when the inventory level of an item falls below the
minimum quantity as the result of a sales document/goods issue, or exceeds the maximum
quantity as the results of a goods receipt.

Select one of the following options:

Warning Only: A warning message appears. You can choose whether to continue (and
fall below the minimum level or exceed the maximum level), or to make the required
adjustments first, such as issue/receive only a partial quantity, search for alternative items,
and so on.

No Warning: Prevents any notification from SAP Business One.

Block Document Creation: An error message appears. You are prevented from completing
the document and falling below the minimum level or exceeding the maximum level defined
for the item.

Block
Negative
Inventory

Select to block documents that would cause the level of inventory to fall below zero. Deselect
the checkbox to allow negative inventory.

You have the following options to define negative inventory:

• By Warehouse: The item is blocked if its inventory goes below 0 in any warehouse to which it

has been assigned.

• By Item Group: The item is blocked if its inventory goes below 0 in the item group to which it

has been assigned.

• By Item Level: The item is blocked if its inventory goes below 0 by item level.

Manage
Inventory By
Warehouse

Document
Remarks
Include

If you select the checkbox, the system checks the warehouse inventory level in the warehouse
that was selected for the item when the sales document was entered. If a transaction causes
the inventory level in that warehouse to fall below the defined minimum inventory quantity, a
warning message appears even if the total available inventory of the item is greater than the
minimum warehouse quantity. The warning or block message depends on the selected option
in the When Release or Receipt of Inventory is Outside Range setting.

If you do not select this checkbox, the application checks the company inventory level values
and checks the total available inventory in all warehouses where this item is stored. This is
relevant when receipt quantity and inventory level is higher than the maximum quantity and is
similar to When Release or Receipt of Inventory is Outside Range.

You have the following options:

• Base Document Number

When you copy a base marketing document to a target document, the base document
number is copied as well and is included in the Remarks field.

• Manual Remarks Only

Print Preferences Section

Send Email Directly to
Recipient When Email
Document Is Selected
in Print Preferences in
SAP Business One

For marketing documents, except blanket agreements, down payments and landed
costs, if you select this checkbox, when a document is added manually in add
mode, added as an official document in the approval process, or added as an official
document from the draft, an email with the document as your selected attachment
type is submitted to Microsoft 365 for sending to the document email address. Once
you select this checkbox, you can further select Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, or
PDF as the attachment type.

To check the sending result, log in to your Microsoft 365 account or the Microsoft
365 account of the user Workflow, according to your settings. The email is sent
out using the Microsoft 365 account of the logged-in user by default. However, with
the checkbox Use Microsoft 365 Account of User "Workflow" to Send Emails Directly
on the Account Management page of SAP Business One Microsoft 365 integration,
administrators can choose to use the Microsoft 365 account of the user Workflow to
directly send out the email.

After the email is sent, you can check the corresponding email log in the E-mails
Sent window for the document in the SAP Business One client.

To use this feature, Microsoft 365 integration must be set up. For more information,
see How to Work with SAP Business One Microsoft 365 Integration.

checkbox in the When Adding Document section through  Administration

Define how commissions are calculated. A commission can be awarded based on the sales

Display Sales
BOM

Select this checkbox to determine the level at which sales price is displayed in a sales
document. You have the following options:

Gross Profit Calculation Section

Calculate Gross
Profit

Determines whether to activate gross profit calculation in sales documents of both item
and service types.

Base Price Origin The Base Price Origin field only appears when the Calculate Gross Profit checkbox is

selected.

From the dropdown list, select an origin for the base price to be used for calculating gross
profit in sales documents of the item type:

• <Price List>: Use item prices in the selected price list as base prices.
• Last Purchase Price: Use the item price the last time an item was purchased as the
base price. If the purchasing price of an item changes over time, the gross profit
calculation considers it.

• Last Evaluated Price: Use the price calculated the last time the Inventory Valuation

Simulation Report was generated as the base price.

 Note

In companies that do not manage a perpetual inventory system, the base price
takes the price calculated the last time the Inventory Valuation Report was
generated.

• Item Cost: Use item cost calculated on the

Item Master Data

Inventory Data

tab as the base price. The item cost may vary from time to time, depending on the
valuation method defined for an item.

Default Gross
Profit % for
Service
Documents

Calculate Gross
Profit % By

• Production Std Cost: Use Production Std Cost (the estimated cost of producing a

good or service, under usual conditions) that is entered on the

Item Master Data

Production Data  tab as the base price.

Enter the gross profit percentage rate to be used by default for calculating the gross profit
in sales documents of the service type.

This field only appears when the Calculate Gross Price checkbox is selected.

Choose one of the following methods to calculate gross profit percentage:

• Dividing Gross Profit by Sales Price
• Dividing Gross Profit by Base Price

 Example

You have an item with a base price of $30 and a sales price of $40.

If you choose Dividing Gross Profit by Sales Price, the gross profit percentage is:

gross profit/sales price x 100 = (40-30)/40 x 100 = 25%

If you choose Dividing Gross Profit by Base Price, the gross profit percentage is:

gross profit/base price x 100 = (40-30)/30 x 100 = 33%

The field Calculate Gross Profit % By only appears when the Calculate Gross Price checkbox
is selected.

Enter the default number of days, weeks, or months after the posting date that a
newly created sales quotation remains valid.

Include
Tax

This checkbox determines whether to calculate and display tax amount in sales quotation
documents.

Nonetheless, if you deselect this checkbox, when you create a sales order from a sales quotation,
Web client still calculates and displays the tax amount in the sales order according to the rules
defined for the customer and items.

Copy Closed
Quotation to
Target Documents

Confirm Sales
Quotation
Automatically

By default, after you copy an open sales quotation to a sales order and deliver the
goods, the sales quotation is closed automatically and cannot be copied and reused any
longer. If you select this checkbox, you can use the Copy To function to copy a closed
sales quotation to a subsequent target document, such as a sales order, delivery, or A\R
invoice.

This checkbox determines whether the Confirmed checkbox on the Logistics tab in a
sales quotation document is selected by default when you create a sales quotation.

If it is selected, the sales quotation is automatically confirmed without manual actions
and can be copied to certain target documents in subsequent processes.

To create a new territory, choose Edit on the Territories page. You have the option to create a territory as a child

 Sub

Level

.

 Same Level

.

• Move Up and Move Down arrow buttons - Use these arrows to move territories up or down within a

node.
• Up Arrow – moves the territory to a higher level
• Down Arrow – moves the territory to a lower level

• Move Left and Move Right arrow buttons - Use these arrows to move the position of a territory on

its original level, or to change the level of a territory without affecting the level of the parent or child
territories
• Left Arrow - moves the territory to the uppermost position, or keeps the territory on the original

level

• Right Arrow - moves the territory to the lowest position, or keeps the territory on the original level

• To deactivate a territory, select the territory and choose Inactive.

not linked to another function, for example, a sales opportunity.

Use this page to define credit card payments. To set up credit card payments, you enter the appointed times
when a credit card company credits your account for credit card vouchers generated by the creation of

The appointed time of the credit varies from one credit card company to another, and depends on the time at
which the credit card vouchers are deposited.

Code, Name

Payment
After

Voucher
Date of
Receipt

Select the option Payment After to specify the fixed period in the form of days and months that
must pass from the date of voucher creation.

To define this period, enter the required values in the Days and Months fields.

Determines that the credit card company credits you on a fixed date, based on the creation date
of the voucher.

Define the dates in the table as follows:

Select the option Voucher Date of Receipt to specify the fixed dates based on the voucher
creation date.

Define the ranges of dates through a month in the From and To fields. The total days in these
ranges must be 31 and a maximum of four ranges can be defined. For every defined range, enter
the day in the month, and after how many months the credit card company credits you.

Perpetual Inventory Section

Use Perpetual
Inventory

Select this checkbox to activate the management of perpetual inventory accounting system.
If selected, each transaction of inventory items is also reflected in the inventory related G/L
accounts.

 Note

After the first inventory transaction is posted, this option is disabled and its status cannot
be changed again.

Valuation
Method for
Item Groups

Specify the default valuation method for newly added item groups. This field is only available if
the Use Perpetual Inventory checkbox is selected.

The available valuation methods are:

• Moving Average: Calculates the inventory value by item cost.

This field is updated dynamically by every inventory receipt posting.

• Standard: Calculates the inventory value by a fixed price.

An item's standard price should be set before you start working in your company.

• FIFO: Calculates inventory value by the FIFO (first in first out) method.

• Each inventory receipt transaction creates a "layer" of quantities linked to costs.
• Each inventory release transaction uses quantities and their corresponding costs from

the first open layers.

 Note

You can change the selected valuation method at any time; however, the change applies
only to item groups added after the change, not retroactively.

Cost per
Warehouse

Allow Stock
Release Without
Item Cost

Select this checkbox to calculate inventory pricing for each individual warehouse.

Deselect this checkbox to calculate inventory pricing for all warehouses combined.

This field is only available if you have selected the Use Perpetual Inventory checkbox.

Select this checkbox to permit items to be included in documents such as deliveries or
A/R invoices, even when the items cost has not been determined.

Select this checkbox when the inventory valuation is performed according to moving
average or FIFO. If you valuate by the Standard option, a cost has already been defined.

If you deselect this checkbox, you can only add items whose activity periods cover the

documents and inventory opening balance documents).

Inventory Posting Tab

Allow Inbound Inventory Posting with Zero Price

Choose this option to allow adding inventory posting documents that increase stock quantities even when
the item price is zero. Use this option when inbound quantities must be recorded immediately, and pricing
information will be maintained later through valuation or purchasing documents.

Highlight Rows with Difference Greater Than

When the counted quantity differs from the in‑warehouse quantity by more than the defined amount, the
system automatically highlights the row in the Inventory Posting document. It helps users identify items with
significant variances that require review or approval.

Calculate In-Warehouse Qty on Count Date Based On

Determines the basis on which the system calculates each item's in-warehouse quantity on the count date.
You cannot change this setting if there is any open inventory counting document. In addition, the settings for
inventory counting documents and inventory posting documents must be the same.

For more information, see Calculation of In-Warehouse Quantities on Count Date.

The available options are:

• Transactions Creation Dates: Uses the document creation date to determine the quantity available in the
warehouse at the time of the inventory count. Select this method if you want the system to reflect the
document entry timeline rather than its official posting to inventory.

• Transactions Posting Dates: Uses the posting date of each transaction to calculate in‑warehouse quantities.

The posting date represents the financial and stock movement date.

Include Inactive Items in Document

Some items are inactive on the count date or posting date. If you still want to include these inactive items in
the document, you need to select this checkbox. For example, you stock up some products for future sales;
these products are temporarily set as inactive in the system but are actually in storage. In this case, you may
not want to exclude them from inventory counting.

If you deselect this checkbox, you can only add items whose activity periods cover the count dates (for
inventory counting documents) or the posting dates (for inventory posting documents and inventory opening
balance documents).

 Example

Item I001 is active from 2014.05.01 to 2014.05.31, and inactive from 2014.06.01.

Create an inventory counting document and set the count date to 2014.05.25. Add item I001 to the document
and then add the document. Then do the following:

772

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Change the count date in the inventory counting document to 2014.06.02.
• Result: You cannot update the inventory counting document.
• Copy the inventory counting document to an inventory posting document and set the posting date to

2014.06.02.

• Result: You cannot add the inventory posting document.
• Change the activity period of item I001 and set it to be active from 2014.05.01 to 2014.05.15.
• Result: You cannot update the inventory counting document unless you manually delete or close relevant

item rows.

Selection and deselection of the checkbox is synchronized for inventory counting documents and inventory
posting documents. In other words, when you select or deselect the checkbox for inventory counting
documents, the checkbox for inventory posting documents is selected or deselected accordingly (and vice
versa). This synchronization is irrelevant for inventory opening balance documents.

Enable On Release Only for Serial and Batch Numbers Management in Inventory Posting

You are not obligated to assign or create serial or batch numbers for an item managed by serial numbers or
batches if the following requirements are met:

• The checkbox is selected.
• The item is managed on release only, which is determined by the management method defined in the item

master data.

• On the count date, the counted quantity is higher than the in-warehouse quantity. This means that you
need to "receive" some more units of the item (identified by serial numbers or batch numbers) into the
system rather than releasing some units.

Inventory Opening Balance Tab

Allow Positive Inventory Opening Balances with Zero Price

Select this option to allow posting positive inventory opening balances for items without specifying a price. This
is useful if the item cost is determined externally or is unavailable at the time of entering opening balances.

Include Inactive Items in Document

Select this option to allow processing of inactive items in inventory opening balance documents. This lets you
manage inventory opening balances for both active and inactive items, supporting comprehensive inventory
initialization and reconciliation.

Item Groups

Use this page to classify your inventory items into groups. For example, you can create groups that correspond
to your business areas and assign the items to a business area using the group.

Item groups can also describe the nature of an item. If you enter a large number of items in Web client, it makes
sense to define groups in more general terms. If you handle just a few items in your company, the description of
the item group can be more detailed.

You can use the item groups to format your reports and evaluations, and to select several items so that they
can be processed together. For example, you could select all the raw materials for a physical inventory.

Item Properties

Use this page to classify your inventory items by properties, which you define according to your business
requirements. You assign the relevant properties when you process a master record for an item.

You can use the item properties to format your reports and evaluations, and to select several items so that they
can be processed together. For example, you could select all the raw materials for a physical inventory.

 Note

The properties are not mandatory; an item can have none, one, or up to 64 properties.

You can use the properties to:

• Format reports and evaluations
• Sort data

Units of Measure

To manage inventory items by different UoMs (units of measure) applicable to your business, you need to
define the individual UoMs in this page. These are the units in which the items will be purchased, sold, and
stocked. You can later group associated ones together as a set of UoMs with a definition of its conversion rules.

Unit of Measure Groups

A UoM (Unit of Measure) group is a set of UoMs that you want to use for a certain type of product. Each UoM
group has a base UoM. All the other UoMs belonging to this group are related to this base UoM by conversion
rules.

776

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

You can assign a UoM group to an item. When you use different UoMs for the item in sales, purchasing,
inventory, and production transactions, SAP Business One automatically processes the differences in UoMs
according to their conversion rules.

The conversion formula is as follows:

Alt. Qty x Alt. UDF Factor x Alt. Weight Factor = Base Qty x Base UDF Factor x Base Weight Factor

Therefore, the conversion value for any document line where an alternative quantity (Alt. Qty) has been
specified into Inventory Quantity equals:

(Base Qty x Base UDF Factor x Base Weight Factor) / (Alt. Qty x Alt. UDF Factor x Alt. Weight Factor).

The conversion value is multiplied by the document line quantity to determine the posted inventory quantity, if
the type of document line causes an inventory posting.

Base UDF Factor and Base Weight Factor selection options and field value calculations are respectively identical
to Alt. UDF Factor and Alt. Weight Factor fields.

Alt. UDF Factor, Alt. Weight Factor, Base UDF Factor, and Base Weight Factor are ignored in the calculation
formula if they are empty.

 Note

When you create a UoM group, pay attention to the following:

• A UoM group can only be added if a base UoM has been defined for it.
• If a UoM group has been assigned to an item, you are unable to remove it.

Resource Groups

Use this page to define and manage resource groups, which are used to classify and organize your resources
for streamlined processing and reporting.

Whenever you create a resource, it belongs to a group. The default resource group is Resources. You can create
more groups to classify your resources. Upon creation, a resource obtains setting defaults from its group. You
can change these settings at the resource level in the Resource Master Data page.

You can create new resource groups, and assign a resource type, such as Machine, Labor, or Other, to each
group. You can also define up to 10 cost components for each resource and specify their standard costs based
on your business needs.

classifications or characteristics that can be assigned to resources in your system.

descriptive name for each resource property.
