Reference Field Links

SAP Business One, Web client gives you considerable flexibility when differentiating and analyzing the effect of
business transactions in your financial reports, based on values in reference fields and in user-defined fields
(UDFs).

To enable you to record specific source document information with the journal entries in the accounting
system, SAP provides a number of reference fields in the journal entry to which values can be copied from the
source document. A source document in this context can be any document in the Web client that gives rise to
journal entries and therefore affects the financial accounts.

SAP Business One, Web client comes with predefined values for the reference fields – which differ depending
on the source document – but you can overwrite the predefined values, either when setting up your system or
when manually creating a journal entry. For example, your company may need to store varying or additional
information as part of journal entries, either for its day-to-day work or in order to fulfill localization-specific,
industry-specific, or legal requirements.

 Recommendation

You can change the reference field and UDF links at any time. However, we recommend that you set up
these links in advance of the financial year and only change the links at the end of the financial year and
prior to the start of the next financial year.

Make sure you discuss and validate these changes with your company accountant and partners in relation
to how these changes will impact financial processes.

The Reference Field Links list view displays the business documents for which you can configure the reference
links, and the status of the links. Any changes to the reference field links and/or user-defined field links of a
document are indicated by the status Customized, while documents with all default source fields are shown
with the status Original.

In the detailed view of each document, you can view the predefined values for each reference field and also
for any user-defined fields. Choose Edit to change the links, or restore the field values to the default ones.
Whenever a journal entry is created, the reference fields and any user-defined fields in the journal entry are
filled according to the values you have defined for the respective document.

Target Fields

The Field Name column displays the name of the following reference fields, or user-defined fields, in the journal
entry.

• Reference 1 - Header
• Reference 2 - Header
• Reference 3 - Header
• Remarks - Header

788

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Reference 1 - BP Row
• Reference 1 - Row
• Reference 2 - BP Row
• Reference 2 - Row
• Reference 3 - BP Row
• Reference 3 - Row
• Row Details - BP Row
• Row Details - Row

“Header” refers to the header of the journal entry. “BP row” refers to the journal entry row with the business
partner control account. “Row” refers to the journal entry row with the standard G/L account.

Source Fields

The Field Value column displays the names of the fields that are available for copying from the business
document. Fields that are automatically copied to other fields in journal entries, such as the due date, posting
date, or document date, are not available for copying to reference fields. However, with that exception, you may
copy from the same source field to multiple target fields.

 Note

You can copy from standard fields or from user-defined fields on header level only, not on row level.

Special Considerations

Before you define reference field links and user-defined field links for journal entries, we recommend that you
consider the features and special cases described below.

• Incoming and Outgoing Payments

• Ref. 2

The Ref. 2 field in the journal entry is not copied directly from the Reference 2 field in the payment
document. Instead, it is copied from a field that is not visible on the user interface, the Ref. 2 field in the
payments table on the database.
The standard behavior is that SAP Business One, Web client copies the field value from the payment
document to the field in the database, and then from the field in the database to the field in the journal
entry. However, if you use a partner add-on that modifies the value of the Ref. 2 field in the payments
table, this logic does not apply.

• Ref. 3

The value that is copied to the Ref. 3 field for rows depends on the payment means. However, if you
select a value other than Default for Reference 3 - BP Row or Reference 3 - Row, this is the value that is
then copied to these rows for all payment means.
If you select Default for Reference 3 - BP Row or Reference 3 - Row, the value that is copied depends on
the payment means, as shown in the following table:

• Remarks

The Remarks field in journal entry rows is not copied from the Doc. Remarks field from payments for

• Landed Costs

The source field Reference 1 corresponds to the Reference field in the landed costs document.
The source field Reference 2 is not otherwise visible on the user interface. The only way to edit the value in
this field is through the SAP Business One Software Development Kit (SDK).

• Inventory Transfers

The source field Reference 2 is not otherwise visible on the user interface. The only way to edit the value in
this field is through the SAP Business One Software Development Kit (SDK).

• That the source and target field lengths match
• That the source and target field values match
• That any truncation due to the target field being shorter than the source field is acceptable, or else

change the definition of the target field

1.19.1.12.3  Importing Currencies from Microsoft Excel

Context

The Import from Microsoft Excel feature on the Currencies definition page is designed to streamline the process
of updating and managing currency data within the SAP Business One, Web client system. This feature allows
you to efficiently import currency information from a Microsoft Excel file. By utilizing this feature, you can add
new currency records, update existing ones, or perform both actions simultaneously.

Procedure

1. To open the Currencies definition page, go to  Administration Configuration

 Accounting

Currencies .

2.

In the list view, choose Edit to enter the edit mode. This is necessary to enable the import function.

3. To initiate the import process, within the Currencies page, choose the Import button.

4. Upon choosing the button, the settings area of the import page will be displayed. Define the required

import settings, including the Import Method and Error Handling Options. If your file contains a header row,
select File Contains Header.

5. To upload your prepared Microsoft Excel file, choose Browse on the right of the File to Import field. Once

uploaded, the columns of your file will be visible in the Preview section.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

791

6. Choose Map Fields to open the Mapping Data Fields dialog box. Define the required information in this
dialog box, and map your spreadsheet file columns to the system fields. You cannot proceed with the
import without mapping the fields.

 Note

All Currency fields are available for a one-time selection during the field mapping process. Once
chosen, they are removed from the fields list.

 Note

Code and International Code are mandatory fields.

7. Once the mapping is complete, choose OK. You can view the mapped columns of your spreadsheet in the

Preview section along with their progress status.

8.

If you are satisfied with the records, choose Import. If there are errors, review the data in the records and
attempt the import again.

You can also export the data shown in the Preview section by choosing the  Export to Microsoft Excel icon.

For more information on importing data from Microsoft Excel, see Importing from Microsoft Excel [page 881] .

1.19.1.13  Service

In the Service menu, you can specify and maintain preexisting data for business documents and objects that
are available in the Service group apps.

To access the Service menu, from the home page, choose  Main Menu Administration Configuration

Service .

This menu consists of the following definition submenus:

• Service Call Origins
• Service Call Problem Types
• Service Call Problem Subtypes
• Service Call Statuses
• Service Call Types
• Solution Statuses
• Queues
• Contract Templates

1.19.1.13.1  Service Settings

On the Service Settings page, you can configure settings for service calls and equipment cards that are
available in the Service group apps.

Use the service definition pages to specify and maintain preexisting data for business documents and objects
that are available in the Service group apps.

To access these pages, from the home page, choose  Main Menu Administration Configuration

Service , and choose the submenu for the data that you would like to define.

For information on how to work with simple definition pages that have an Edit button, see the section Working
with Simple Definitions in Working with Definitions [page 699].

For information on how to work with detailed definition pages that have a Create button and additional drill-
down detailed views, see the section Working with Detailed Definitions in Working with Definitions [page 699].

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information.

Service Call Origins

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Origin dropdown list in the
Classification section in the General tab of a service call page when you create or edit a service call. The Origin
dropdown list is used to show how assistance and support requests are received from customers or sent to
vendors.

There are three default service call origins:

• Email: Service requests are received or sent by emails.
• Telephone No.: Service requests are received or sent by phone calls.
• Web: Service requests are received or sent online from webpages.

You can define custom origins but you cannot delete the default origins. If you want to hide an origin from the
dropdown list, or deactivate an origin, deselect the Active checkbox.

 Note

You cannot add a service call with such hidden options or update such hidden options of an existing service
call through the Data Interface.

Service Call Problem Types

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Problem Type dropdown list
in the Classification section in the General tab of a service call page when you create or edit a service call. The
Problem Type dropdown list is used to classify types of reported problems.

If you want to hide a type from the dropdown list or deactivate a type, deselect the Active checkbox.

804

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

You cannot add a service call with such hidden options or update such hidden options of an existing service
call through the Data Interface.

Service Call Problem Subtypes

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Problem Subtype dropdown
list in the Classification section in the General tab of a service call page when you create or edit a service call.
The Problem Subtype dropdown list is used to classify subordinate types of reported problems.

If you want to hide a subtype from the dropdown list or deactivate a subtype, deselect the Active checkbox.

 Note

You cannot add a service call with such hidden options or update such hidden options of an existing service
call through the Data Interface.

Service Call Statuses

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Status dropdown list in the
Service Call Details section in the General tab of a service call page when you create or edit a service call.

There are three default service call statuses:

• Open: The initial status of a service call after it is created. It awaits service engineers to work on it.
• Pending: The issue is acknowledged but the call has not yet been resolved or closed. This could be due to
needing approval, needing further information, waiting for parts, or any other reason that might delay the
completion of the service call.

• Closed: The service call is resolved. You cannot set the status of a service call to Closed if you have not

provided a solution.

You can define custom statuses but you cannot delete the default statuses. If you want to hide a status from
the dropdown list or deactivate a status, deselect the Active checkbox.

 Note

You cannot create a service call with such hidden options or update such hidden options of an existing
service call through the Data Interface.

Service Call Types

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Call Type dropdown list in the
Classification section in the General tab of a service call page when you create or edit a service call. The Call

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

805

Type dropdown list is used to classify your service calls. For example, you can use First Level, Technician,
or Field Repair.

If you want to hide a type from the dropdown list or deactivate a type, deselect the Active checkbox.

 Note

You cannot add a service call with such hidden options or update such hidden options of an existing service
call through the Data Interface.

Solution Statuses

Specify values in the Name column. The specified values appear as options in the Status dropdown list on the
General tab of a solution page when you create or edit a solution.

There are three default solution statuses:

• Internal: A solution is in the internal processing stage inside a department or organization.
• Publish: A solution has been made publicly available and is accessible to all users within a company.
• Review: A solution is going through a review process to ensure quality and correctness before it is

published.

You can define custom statuses but you cannot delete the default statuses. If you want to hide a status from
the dropdown list or deactivate a status, deselect the Active checkbox.

Queues

Use this page to define a team of employees responsible for managing service calls. You can also enter the
queue’s manager, and include a list of members. You can deactivate a queue, even a queue with service calls, so
that you can no longer send service calls to the queue.

Specify a code for the queue in the Queue Code field. The code (ID) is displayed in the pages related to this
queue.

Contract Templates

You define service contracts between your company and its customers. The contracts include items managed
by serial numbers that the company supports, daily service hours, and even an obligatory resolution time for
solving customer problems.

Use this page to create different types of contract templates. You specify general information, service contract
coverage, remarks, and attachments.

1.19.2  Customization

In SAP Business One, Web client, customization and extensibility are key features that empower you to tailor
the system to meet your specific business needs.

This document provides an overview of the customization options available: the User-Defined Objects (UDOs),
User-Defined Tables (UDTs), User-Defined Fields (UDFs), and User-Defined Values (UDVs). By leveraging these
tools, you can ensure that your SAP Business One, Web client environment is aligned with your unique
operational requirements, thereby optimizing efficiency and productivity.

You can find the following customization apps in the Administration group:

• User-Defined Objects:

Use the User-Defined Objects function to add new business logic or new objects to SAP Business One, Web
client.

• User-Defined Tables:

SAP Business One, Web client supports adding user-defined tables for storing additional sets of
information.

• User-Defined Fields:

SAP Business One, Web client supports adding user-defined fields that might be essential for the day-to-
day activities of your business. User-defined fields enable you to add fields to existing tables to keep track
of additional information.

 Note

The UDO and UDT created in SAP Business One appear in the User-Defined Objects and User-Defined
Tables apps in the Administration group in the Web client.

The UDF for headers of documents and master data can be displayed as columns in the table area
of the respective list views, and can be used as filters. In the detailed view, the UDF appear on the
User-Defined Fields tab. The UDF at row level appear in the grids of the respective detailed view.

• User-Defined Values:

Use the User-Defined Values app to manage UDVs for customizable fields in various business objects.

In this section, we will illustrate how to utilize these customization tools.

1.19.2.1  User-Defined Objects

User-defined objects (UDOs) enable you to create your own business objects for managing custom data and
creating custom functionality. Just as SAP Business One Web Client provides objects for basic, out-of-the-box
functionality, you can create custom objects for your custom functionality.

The UDO infrastructure makes it easy to create objects and to provide them with basic services (such as Add,
Delete, Update) without any programming.

You can create the following types of objects:

• Master data, for example,  Business Partner
• Documents, for example, the A/R Invoice

1.19.2.1.1  Creating a User-Defined Object

Prerequisites

You must create a user-defined table (UDT) for your user-defined object (UDO) before creating the UDO. See
Creating User-Defined Tables [page 816] for more information.

Procedure

1. Go to  Administration User-Defined Objects .

2. To start the UDO creation process, choose Create.

In the General step, enter the details of your user-defined object.

• Unique ID: Refers to the key to identify your user-defined object, the key you add must be unique.
• Object Name: The name or description you want to give your user-defined object.
• Type: Specify the Type of object you want to create, such as Master or Document.
• Select Table: Based on your selection in the Type field, available tables will be listed. You can then

choose one to be the master table for your object.

• Apply Authorization: This checkbox lets admins to provide authorization for data entry for their
specific objects. Once you select this checkbox, your UDO will be visible under the User-Defined
Objects category in the General Authorizations window in the SAP Business One client. To know more
about the Apply Authorization checkbox for user-defined objects, see User-Defined Tables and Objects
Authorizations

• Show in UI: If you select the Show in UI checkbox, your user-defined object appears on the Home page

as a tile under User-Defined Objects section.

4.

In the Setting Services step, select the built-in services to be available for your object.

If you select Find, the Modify Fields for Find step opens. Select the fields to display from the list and set the
order of the fields.

1.19.2.1.2  Available Services

SAP Business One, Web clientprovides built-in services that you can add to your object. Select from the
following services during registration:

Services

Add

Update

Find

Delete

Cancel

Close

Log

Description

The Add service enables the user to add a new record to
the user-defined table (and also a child user-defined table, if
one exists).

The Update service enables the user to update an existing
record in the user-defined table (and also a child user-
defined table, if one exists).

The Find service enables the Choose From List dialog box in
Find mode.

The Delete service enables the user to delete a record from

a user table (and a child user table, if one exists).

 Note

This service is for master data type objects only.

The Cancel service enables the user to cancel records

related to your object, as follows:

For document type objects, a canceled record cannot be

used in the application.

For master data type objects, a canceled record can be

restored but cannot be modified.

Canceled records of both object types can be displayed in

the application.

The Close service enables the user to close a document

without creating a posting.

A closed document cannot be modified and cannot be used

as a reference. Closing quotations, orders, and deliveries

does not create a posting in accounting.

 Note

This service is for document type objects only.

The Log service creates a table in the database that

maintains a history or log of all actions on the object's

records. The log table name starts with "A" followed by the

object's user table name.

SAP Business One, Web Client

Description

Manage Series

Year Transfer

If you unregister a UDO that includes the log service, the

history log table is deleted from the database.

If you update the UDO and remove the log service, the

will be done.

The Manage Series service adds the object to the document

numbering in the Administration module and manages the

The default setting for the UDO is the Primary series, First

The Year Transfer service enables the user to copy your

1.19.2.3  User-Defined Fields

User-Defined Fields setup is now available in SAP Business One, Web client.

You can now view, create, update or remove user-defined fields. This includes UDFs on system objects, user-
defined objects and user tables.

User-defined fields enable you to add fields to existing tables to keep track of additional information. For
example, you can add a field called CarNumber to the Employee Master Data table to keep track of the license
plate number for each employee.

1.19.2.3.1  Creating User-Defined Fields

When creating user-defined fields, you must specify a field name and the type of data to be contained in the
field. You can also specify the valid values for the field.

Procedure

1. To create a user-defined field, go to  Administration User-Defined Fields . The User-Defined

Management window opens.
The window displays a hierarchy of categories (form types) to which you can add user-defined fields. Some
categories affect a single form (such as  Business Partners under  Master Data), while others affect multiple
forms (such as Title and Rows under  Marketing Documents).
To view all the available form types, click  Expand.

2. Select the category to which you want to add a field and choose the  Create button.

The  Create User-Defined Field window opens.

3. Specify the name and type of field by entering the following fields in the  Create User-Defined Field  form:

Field Name

Title

The field name.

The  Title value cannot contain spaces or special charac-
ters.

A field is added to the database with the prefix  U_  fol-
lowed by the field name specified here. The full name, with

the prefix, is displayed in the query generator when you

view a table’s list of fields.

1.19.2.3.2  Linking a User-Defined Table to a User-Defined

Field

Instead of defining valid values for a field within the field definition, you can specify that the valid values are
contained in a user-defined table.

This can be helpful if you have several fields in different tables with the same valid values, or when you want to
update the valid values dynamically.

Prerequisite

• You are adding a user-defined field, as described in Creating User-Defined Fields [page 822], and you have

opened the Create User-Defined Field window to define the new field.
The field type is  Alphanumeric and its structure is  Regular.
The  Default Value, and  Mandatory Field checkboxes are not selected.

Procedure

1.

In the  Create User-Defined Field window, select the Link to Entity checkbox. A new field is displayed to the
right.
Click on value help icon in the field to open the Link to Entity dialog box and select User-Defined Tables.

2. Select the user table that contains the valid values for the current field and click OK.

3. Fill out the rest of the form and choose the  Create button.

Object (UDO)

You can link a user-defined field to a user-defined object. This can be helpful if you have UDOs related to a
standard system form (non-user form).

1.19.2.3.4  Creating Table Keys

You can set a user-defined field (or multiple fields) as a key in the database table to make the field (or set of
fields) unique and prevent duplicates.

Procedure

1. Go to  Administration User-Defined Fields . The User-Defined Fields Management window opens.

2. Select the table for which you would like to define a key and choose the Keys button.

The Manage Keys window appears.

3. To create a new key for the table, choose the Add button. The system creates a key with the name IX_0.
In the Key Name field, you can change this default name. You can create as many keys as you need by
choosing Add. You can also browse between the different keys by selecting them from the dropdown list.
In the Valid Values table, select the user-defined fields you want to include in the selected key.

4.

 Note

You can define more than one user-defined field in a single key.

5. Select the Unique checkbox.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

827

If the key is made up of one field, values entered for that field must be unique. If the key is made up of more
than one field, the set of values for these fields must be unique.

6. Click the OK button.

1.19.2.3.5  Updating User-Defined Fields

To update a user-defined field, do the following:

1. Go to  Administration User-Defined Fields . The User-Defined Fields Management window opens.

2. Select a field by clicking on it.

3. Choose the Edit button.
4. The Edit User-Defined Field window opens. You can update the field settings, except for Title, Type,

and Structure.

5. Once you finish editing, click on the Update button.

1.19.2.3.6  Removing User-Defined Fields

 Caution

This action is irreversible and deletes all values saved in this field in all its related objects. A query with a
removed user-defined field displays an error when you run it.

 Recommendation

Before you remove a user-defined field, back up the database.

To remove a user-defined field, do the following:

1. Go to  Administration User-Defined Fields . The User-Defined Fields Management window opens.

2. Select a field by clicking on it.

3. Choose the Delete button and click OK.

1.19.2.4  User-Defined Values

App

In the Administration group, you can find the User-Defined Values (UDVs) app.

828

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with this app:

• Centrally view, create, edit, and delete UDVs setups for customizable fields in the detailed views of various

business objects.
For more information, see Supported Business Objects and Customizable Fields [page 879].

• Copy UDVs setups from one source business object to one or more targets within the same business

module or group.

• Export and import UDVs setups between different companies in the same SAP Business One localization.
• Apply filters to the list of UDVs setups to simplify your search and organizational tasks.

Here are the available methods for UDVs customization:

• Filtered List:

Enables you to tailor the visible values for a field with a dropdown list of extensive predefined options,
ensuring you do not accidentally choose irrelevant values.

 Example

If you have a user-defined field Colors for all product colors, but are only selling Blue this week, you can
narrow down your selection to just Blue.

• Formula:

Enables you to automatically populate field values with the results of a formula that you define. This feature
is available for input fields, including date, time, and checkboxes.
A formula can include fixed text you enter, mathematical and logical expressions, and variables of
reference fields from the document where you set up UDVs, or from other business documents or objects
in the SAP Business One database.
This method aims to save time, reduce effort, and minimize errors by automatically entering information
that you would otherwise have to type or calculate manually.

 Example

You can set the Remarks field in a sales order to automatically display a customer's balance whenever
you change the customer code.

General Authorizations and Data Ownership

To manage user access to the UDVs feature in SAP Business One, Web client, look for the entries, User-Defined
Values - Setup and User-Defined Values App in Web Client, in the Customization Tool Authorizations topic in the
guide How to Define Authorizations in SAP Business One 10.0.

The data ownership settings associated with the UDVs feature in the Web client are determined by the settings
configured in the SAP Business One client. For more information, see Data Ownership.

 Note

For optimal performance, we recommend applying UDVs settings to five fields or fewer for each document
type.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

829

The UDVs you define in the Web client are completely independent and not linked or synchronized with
those in the SAP Business One client. This means if you define new UDVs in the Web client, they do not
automatically appear or get replicated in the desktop client. Changes made in the Web client will not be
synchronized with the desktop client, and vice versa.

1.19.2.4.1  Managing User-Defined Values

To open the Manage User-Defined Values list view, choose the User-Defined Values (UDVs) tile on the home
page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records.

Selecting Views

The list views store filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category to determine which records
are displayed. The Manage User-Defined Values list view provides you with a Standard view of the dataset
of all UDVs setup records across all supported business objects. You can also change the parameters of the
predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to set filters to apply on the records to be displayed in the table area. For more
information, see Filter Bar [page 54].

Using the Header Tools

The  Share menu in the top-right corner of the header allows you to perform a number of actions, such as
sharing a list view by email (Send by Email) or saving selected views as tiles on the home page (Save as Tile).
For more information, see Header Tools [page 65].

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Working with the Record Content

The User-Defined Values tree table contains a hierarchical set of UDVs setup data structured in rows and
columns, grouped into nodes. The number following the table header represents the total sum of UDVs setups.
The columns within the table provide detailed information about each UDVs setup record from different
aspects.

Business
Object

This is the first column, known as the tree column. It has three hierarchical levels:

• Root Level:

Displays business objects, which are digital models of real-world entities or components
within the SAP Business One and SAP Business One, Web client system, such as sales orders,
business partners, and A/R invoices. These models help you articulate and manage various
aspects of your business.
All root-level parent nodes are collapsed by default. Choose the  Expand/Collapse icon next
to a parent node to reveal its second-level child nodes.

• Second Level:
• Body Area:

Groups line items of all UDVs setups for fields outside the table section within the
detailed view of each business object.

• Table Section:

Groups line items of all UDVs setups for fields inside the table section within the detailed
view of each business object.

All second-level nodes are collapsed by default. Choose the  Expand/Collapse icon next to a
second-level child node to reveal its third-level child nodes.

• Third Level:

Displays the line items of UDVs setup names, as entered during the setup processes.

 Note

Selecting the checkbox next to a root- or second-level node does not automatically select
its child nodes. However, selecting the checkbox next to Business Object in the column
header automatically selects all visible nodes. To select all third-level nodes of all business
objects or a filtered range, use the  Expand All icon to display all nodes first, and then
select the checkbox in the column header.

Field This column shows the name of each field within a business object where a UDVs setup is applied.

Customization
Method

This column shows the method selected to define the UDVs for each field during the
setup process. The available methods are Filtered List and Formula.

Content If the Customization Method is Filtered List, this column shows the values of the filtered list options

selected during each UDVs setup.

If the Customization Method is Formula, this column shows the formula content entered during each
UDVs setup.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

831

Triggers This column shows the fields selected during each UDVs setup that trigger the formula application,

resulting in the automatic refreshing of field values.

Description This column shows a detailed explanation for each UDVs setup, as entered during the setup

process.

Edit For more information, see Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833].

Create For more information, see Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833].

Delete Select one or more third-level line items of UDVs setups and then choose this button to delete your

selection.

The root- and second- level nodes are predefined and cannot be deleted.

Import

Copy

For more information, see Importing User-Defined Values [page 873].

For more information, see Copying User-Defined Values [page 876].

 Collapse All Choose the  Collapse All icon to only display the root-level parent nodes, hiding all their

second- and third-level child nodes.

1.19.2.4.2  Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined

Values

This topic explains how to create and edit User-Defined Values (UDVs) and how to identify fields that already
contain UDVs.

Creating and Editing UDVs

You can create and edit UDVs, either within the centralized User-Defined Values app, or through the detailed
views of individual business objects without using the User-Defined Values app.

Procedure 1: Configuring within the User-Defined Values App

1. Open the User-Defined Values app in one of the following ways:

• On the Home page, choose the User-Defined Values tile in the Administration group.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Administration User-Defined Values .

2. Follow the procedures below to create or edit a UDVs setup:

• To create a new UDVs setup for a field, proceed as follows:

1. Go to the Business Object tree column in the User-Defined Values table, select a single root-level

business object node, such as Sales Order, and then choose Create.
• If existing records of the selected business object are present in your system, you will enter the

detailed view of the latest record to customize field values.

• If no such business object exists, you will enter a blank detailed-view page of the selected

business object to customize field values.

2.

In the detailed view of the selected business object, each customizable field is marked with an
 Edit icon on the right. Choose this icon to enter the Edit <Field Uname> dialog box.
For more information about how to set up UDVs, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872],
Customizing Field Values with a Filtered List [page 835], and Customizing Field Values with a
Formula [page 837].

3. After you finish the setup, choose OK to apply the setup to the selected field and exit the dialog

box.

• To edit an existing UDVs setup for a field, proceed as follows:

1. Go to the Business Object tree column in the User-Defined Values table, expand all the child nodes
of a single root-level business object node, select a single third-level line item of UDVs setup, and
then choose Edit to enter the UDVs editing dialog box.

2. After you finish editing, choose OK to apply the setup to the selected field and exit the dialog box.

3.

In the detailed view of the selected business object, continue to create or edit UDVs setups for other
customizable fields.

4. After you finish UDVs setups for all desired fields, choose Finish Edit in the toolbar in the top right corner to

exit edit mode.

5. Save or cancel other changes to the open business object.

Your UDVs settings are saved regardless of whether you choose Finish Edit to exit edit mode, or whether
you create or update the open business object.

6. Go back to the User-Defined Values app. You can see the new setups listed below the selected business

object.

1. From other Web client apps than the User-Defined Values app, create or edit an individual business object

in the detailed view, such as a sales order.

2. Choose Edit User-Defined Values in the top right corner in the detailed view of the selected business object

to enter edit mode.
Once you enter edit mode, this button switches to Finish Edit.
In edit mode, each customizable field is marked with an  Edit icon on the right. Choose this icon to start
creating or editing UDVs in the Edit <Field Uname> dialog box.
After you finish editing, choose OK to apply the setup to the selected field and exit the dialog box.
For more information about how to set up UDVs, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872],

[page 837].

4.

In the detailed view of the selected business object, continue to create or edit UDVs setups for other

5. After you finish UDVs setups for all desired fields, choose Finish Edit in the toolbar in the top right corner to

exit edit mode.

6. Save or cancel other changes to the open business object.

Your UDVs settings are saved regardless of whether you choose Finish Edit to exit edit mode, or whether
you create or update the open business object.

7. Go to the User-Defined Values app. You can see the new setups listed below the selected business object.

Showing Indicator for UDVs

To identify which fields already have custom values, proceed as follows:

1. Navigate to the user actions menu.

2. Go to the  Settings General Settings  tab and then select Show Indicator for User-Defined Values.

After enabling this option, fields that have existing UDVs will be enclosed in orange brackets in edit mode. The
specific position of the brackets varies according to the field type:

• Input field, including text area, date picker, and time picker:

The label of an input field will be surrounded by orange brackets. For example, [ Posting Date ].

• Checkbox:

• If a checkbox has its label on the left side, only the checkbox itself (the square box) will be surrounded

by orange brackets.

• If the label of a checkbox is immediately to the right of the checkbox, the entire checkbox field,

including both the label and the square box, will be surrounded by orange brackets.

• If checkboxes are placed within rows of the same column in a table (there is a separate checkbox for

each row), only the column header will be surrounded by orange brackets.

1.19.2.4.2.1  Customizing Field Values with a Filtered List

In this topic, we provide an example to illustrate how to use a filtered list to tailor the visible options for a field
with a dropdown list.

Prerequisites

1. Navigate to the user actions menu.

2. Go to the  Settings General Settings  tab and then select Show Indicator for User-Defined Values.

Context

In the User-Defined Fields - Management window in the SAP Business One client, you chose the menu

Marketing Document Title  and added a Colors dropdown list, in order to show all valid product colors in

stock in the Product table of sales orders. You specified the following information:

• Title: SOH_Colors
• Description: Colors

You only want to sell Blue and White colors in the coming week. In SAP Business One, Web client, when you
create a new sales order and add items to it, you only want to see these two options in the dropdown list.

In this topic, we'll walk you through how to use a filtered list to narrow down to a specific selection of User-
Defined Values (UDVs), thereby avoiding irrelevant choices and helping you to increase your productivity.

Procedure

1. Enter the UDVs editing dialog box.

Follow the steps in Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833] to enter the UDVs
editing dialog box for the Colors dropdown list within the detailed view of a sales order.

The dialog box is titled Edit User-Defined Values for U_SOH_Colors, where the variable <U_SOH_Colors>
represents the uname of the Colors field.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

835

2. Specify customization method.

Choose the Filtered List segmented button for the Customization Method field.

3. Select visible values.

In the Values to Include dropdown list, choose Blue and White.

If you don't want to display any value in the dropdown menu, you can choose None.

Use the checkbox Allow to View All Values to determine whether to provide options in the dropdown menu
for toggling between displaying all values and filtered values.

4. Save your changes.

Choose OK to save your changes and exit the setup dialog box.

Your settings are saved regardless of whether you choose Finish Edit to exit edit mode or continue creating
or updating the sales order.

Results

The Colors field appears enclosed in orange brackets as [ Colors ].

The available options in the Colors dropdown menu vary according to your selection for the checkbox Allow to
View All Values in Step 3:

• If you deselect this checkbox, in the Colors dropdown menu, you can only see two options: Blue and White.

To view all the values, choose the  Edit icon again to enter the UDVs setup dialog box.

• If you select this checkbox, an additional Display All Values option will appear at the bottom of the

dropdown menu. Choosing this option will cancel the filtered list setup, showing all values in the dropdown
menu. To revert to the filtered list setup, choose Display Filtered Values at the bottom of the dropdown
menu.

This UDVs setup applies to all sales orders.

When editing this setup, if you choose the None option for the Customization Method field and then choose OK
to confirm and exit the setup dialog box, the existing UDVs setup will be permanently cleared and cannot be
restored.

1.19.2.4.2.2  Customizing Field Values with a Formula

You can define mathematical formulas for input fields, including text areas, date pickers, and time pickers. You
can define logical formulas for checkboxes.

A formula can include fixed text, mathematical and logical expressions, and reference fields (as variables).

When you reference fields in your formula to retrieve their values for calculations, the fields can derive from the
detailed view User Interface (UI) of the document where you set up custom values, or from other documents or
objects in the SAP Business One database.

You can customize values for User-Defined Fields; however, you cannot do so for fields in User-Defined Tables
and User-Defined Objects.

In this section, we will provide examples with procedural steps for customizing and refreshing field values with
mathematical and logical formulas, as well as general guidelines for effective formulas.

Customizing Header Field with a Mathematical Formula [page 838]

In this topic, we provide an example to show you how to use a simple mathematical formula to
customize the value of a date type field in the header area of a tab within the detailed view of a sales
order. This formula includes a variable and a constant.

Customizing Table Field with a Mathematical Formula [page 840]

This topic provides an example demonstrating how to use a mathematical formula to customize the
values of an input field in a table on a tab within the detailed view, such as the Product table on the
Contents tab within sales orders. This formula includes variables and arithmetic operators.

Customizing with a Mathematical Formula That References a Database Field [page 843]

This topic provides an example of using a mathematical formula to customize the value of a field in
sales orders. This formula includes fixed text and a reference to another field from other documents in
the SAP Business One database.

Customizing Checkbox Selection with a Logical Formula [page 848]

In this topic, we provide an example to explain how to use a logical formula to customize the selection
of a checkbox in sales orders. This formula contains a logical operator, a constant, and a reference to
another field from other documents in the SAP Business One database.

Guidelines for Effective Formulas [page 852]

Constants, operators, variables, and functions are essential elements in creating effective formulas for
calculations and logical operations. This topic is useful for understanding and implementing formulas
for User-Defined Values (UDVs) in the Web client for accurate and efficient data processing.

1.19.2.4.2.2.1  Customizing Header Field with a Mathematical

Formula

In this topic, we provide an example to show you how to use a simple mathematical formula to customize the
value of a date type field in the header area of a tab within the detailed view of a sales order. This formula
includes a variable and a constant.

Prerequisites

1. Navigate to the user actions menu.

2. Go to the  Settings General Settings  tab and then select Show Indicator for User-Defined Values.

Context

When you enter a posting date in a sales order, you may need the Web client to automatically set the Delivery
Date to one week later, or you may want to manually refresh the Delivery Date value to one week later.

Procedure

1. Enter the UDVs editing dialog box.

Follow the steps in Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833] to enter the UDVs
editing dialog box for the Delivery Date field in the Document Details section on the General tab within the
detailed view of a sales order.

The dialog box is titled Edit User-Defined Values for DeliveryDate, where the variable <DeliveryDate>
represents the uname of the Delivery Date field.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

2. Specify the customization method.

In the setup dialog box, choose the Formula segmented button for the Customization Method field.

3. Select Refresh Type.

Choose one of the following:

• Automatic Refresh:

The Delivery Date value will be automatically updated with the result of your formula.

• Manual Refresh:

The Delivery Date value will be manually updated.
If you choose this option, skip Step 4.

4. Set triggers.

In the Triggers dropdown list, choose the  Value Help icon to open a new Triggers dialog box.

838

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Search for and select the uname of each field that triggers the formula application, which will automatically
refresh the Delivery Date value. In this example, select PostingDate, the uname of the Posting Date field.

Choose OK to exit the Triggers dialog box and return to the UDVs setup dialog box.

5. Name the formula.

In the Formula Name field, use the default name or enter a descriptive name of your own.

6. Deselect the checkbox Formula Includes Database Fields.

7. Enter the formula.

In the Formula text area, enter PostingDate + 7, where the variable <PostingDate> represents the
posting date of the sales order, and the numerical value 7 is a constant that does not change.

The variable name <PostingDate> takes the uname of the Posting Date field on the sales order User
Interface (UI).

While typing in the text area, you can type the first letters of the uname and use the auto-complete
dropdown list to select the desired result. You can also type the namespace ui. to show a list of all
available unames and select the full form ui.PostingDate. Both the short form and the full form have the
same effect.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

8. Verify the formula.

Choose Test Formula. The posting date of the current sales order is retrieved and applied in the formula.

Verify the formula outcome in the Test Result field.

9.

In the Description filed, enter descriptive text to clarify the formula's purpose or to annotate the formula for
better understanding.

10. Save your changes.

Choose OK to save your changes and exit the setup dialog box.

Your settings are saved regardless of whether you choose Finish Edit to exit edit mode or continue creating
or updating the sales order.

Results

The Delivery Date field appears enclosed in orange brackets as [ Delivery Date ].

The field value is refreshed according to the type you select in Step 3:

• Automatic Refresh:

The field value updates automatically when you enter or change a posting date. For example, entering the
posting date January 17, 2025 will set the delivery date to January 24, 2025.

• Manual Refresh:

Choose the  Refresh icon next to the Delivery Date field to update the field value.

This UDVs setup applies to all sales orders.

When editing this setup, if you choose the None option for the Customization Method field and then choose OK
to confirm and exit the setup dialog box, the existing UDVs setup will be permanently cleared and cannot be
restored.

1.19.2.4.2.2.2  Customizing Table Field with a Mathematical

Formula

This topic provides an example demonstrating how to use a mathematical formula to customize the values of
an input field in a table on a tab within the detailed view, such as the Product table on the Contents tab within
sales orders. This formula includes variables and arithmetic operators.

Prerequisites

1. Navigate to the user actions menu.

2. Go to the  Settings General Settings  tab and then select Show Indicator for User-Defined Values.

Context

In the User-Defined Fields - Management window in the SAP Business One client, you chose the menu

Marketing Document Rows  and added a User-Defined Field (UDF) Coupon %, in order to input the
discount percentage for items in the Coupon % column of the Product table on the Contents tab of sales
orders. You specified the following information :

• Title: SOR_Coupon
• Description: Coupon %

You continued to add another UDF Price After Coupon and specified the following information in order to
calculate the final price after applying the coupon discount for each sales order item:

• Title: SOR_PriceAfterCoupon
• Description: Price After Coupon

In SAP Business One, Web client, you create a new sales order with 10 items in the Product table on the
Contents tab, each with a different unit price. When you enter a coupon discount for an item, you might need
the Web client to automatically calculate the final price and fill in the Price After Coupon field, or you might want
to manually refresh the Price After Coupon value with the final price.

840

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

If you set up user-defined values (UDVs) for any field in a table on a tab, the table scroll bar will be disabled.
To restore the table scroll bar, you need to delete all UDVs settings for the fields in the table.

We recommend applying UDVs settings to tables with 20 or fewer rows; otherwise, the response time may
be significantly longer.

Procedure

1. Enter the UDVs editing dialog.

Follow the steps in Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833] to enter the UDVs
editing dialog box for the Price After Coupon field within the detailed view of a sales order.

The dialog box is titled Edit User-Defined Values for Product_Item.U_SOR_PriceAfterCoupon, where the
variable <Product_Item.U_SOR_PriceAfterCoupon> represents the uname of the Price After Coupon
field.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

2. Specify the customization method.

In the setup dialog box, choose the Formula segmented button for the Customization Method field.

3. Select Refresh Type.

Choose one of the following:

• Automatic Refresh:

The values in the Price After Coupon column will be automatically updated with the results of your
formula.

• Manual Refresh:

The values in the Price After Coupon column will be manually updated.
If you choose this option, skip Step 4.

4. Set triggers.

In the Triggers dropdown list, choose the  Value Help icon to open a new Triggers dialog box.

Search for and select the uname of each field that triggers the formula application, resulting in the
automatic refreshing of the Price After Coupon values.

In this example, we use the Coupon field as the trigger. Since it comes from the Product table header,
choose the Table Fields segmented button in the upper-right corner, and then search for and select
Product_Item.U_SOR_Coupon, the uname of the Coupon field.

Choose OK to exit the Triggers dialog and return to the UDVs setup dialog box.

5. Name the formula.

In the Formula Name field, use the default name or enter a descriptive name of your own.

6. Deselect the checkbox Formula Includes Database Fields.

7. Enter the formula.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

841

In the Formula text area, enter Product_Item.UnitPrice*(1-Product_Item.U_SOR_Coupon/100,
where the variable <Product_Item.UnitPrice> represents the unit price of each item, and
<Product_Item.U_SOR_Coupon> represents the coupon discount percentage of each item.

The variable name <Product_Item.UnitPrice> takes the uname of the Unit Price field in the Product
table, while <Product_Item.U_SOR_Coupon> takes the uname of the Coupon field.

While typing in the text area, you can type the first letters of a uname and use the auto-complete dropdown
list to select the desired result. You can also type the namespace ui.Product_Item. to show a list of
all available unames from the Product table and select the full forms, ui.Product_Item.UnitPrice and
ui.Product_Item.U_SOR_Coupon. Both the short form and the full form have the same effect.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

8. Verify the formula.

Choose Test Formula. The unit price and coupon discount of the first row in the Product table of the current
sales order are retrieved and applied in the formula.

Verify the formula outcome in the Test Result field.

9.

In the Description filed, enter descriptive text to clarify the formula's purpose or to annotate the formula for
better understanding.

10. Save your changes.

Choose OK to save your changes and exit the setup dialog box.

Your settings are saved regardless of whether you choose Finish Edit to exit edit mode or continue creating
or updating the sales order.

Results

The Price After Coupon field appears enclosed in orange brackets as [ Price After Coupon ].

The field value is refreshed according to the type you selected in Step 3:

• Automatic Refresh:

Each Price After Coupon field value is updated automatically for an individual item when you enter or
change a coupon discount for the item in the Coupon % input field in the same row. For example, when
the unit price for item A is 60 dollars, entering the coupon discount 10 will set the price after coupon to 54
dollars.
If the automatic refreshing of the Price After Coupon field values is triggered by a field from a tab header,
instead of from the Product table, the values in the entire Price After Coupon column will be automatically
updated all at once.

This topic provides an example of using a mathematical formula to customize the value of a field in sales

Business One database.

Prerequisites

1. Navigate to the user actions menu.

2. Go to the  Settings General Settings  tab and then select Show Indicator for User-Defined Values.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

843

Context

When you change the customer code in a sales order, you want the Remarks field in the Customer Details
section on the General tab to automatically display the customer's account balance.

Procedure

1. Enter the UDVs editing dialog box.

Follow the steps in Creating, Editing, and Identifying User-Defined Values [page 833] to enter the UDVs
editing dialog box for the Remarks field within the detailed view of a sales order.

The dialog box is titled Edit User-Defined Values for Remarks, where the variable <Remarks> represents the
uname of the Remarks field.

For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

2. Specify the customization method.

In the setup dialog box, choose the Formula segmented button for the Customization Method field.

3. Select Refresh Type.

Choose Automatic Refresh. The Remarks field value will be automatically updated with the result of your
formula.

4. Set triggers.

In the Triggers dropdown list, choose the  Value Help icon to open a new Triggers dialog box.

Search for and select the uname of each field that triggers the formula application, resulting in the
automatic refreshing of the Remarks value. In this example, select CustomerCode, the uname of the
Customer Code field.

Choose OK to exit the Triggers dialog box and return to the UDVs setup dialog box.

5. Name the formula.

In the Formula Name field, use the default name or enter a descriptive name of your own.

6. Set lookup conditions.

Each Account Balance amount comes from its associated Business Partner document, instead of the
sales order where you are currently setting up UDVs. To reference the Account Balance field of a specific
customer and retrieve its value for calculation, you need the Web client to access the table for business
partners in the SAP Business One database. This table stores structured data records of all Business
Partner documents, including the Account Balance amount associated with each customer. By using the
customer code from the current sales order, you can look up the corresponding business partner record
in the database. You can then reference the Account Balance field and use the retrieved value from the
business partner record in your formula.

To do this, proceed as follows:

1. Select the checkbox Formula Includes Database Fields. A lookup table appears on the right of the

checkbox.

When setting conditions in the lookup table, ensure that any rules and limitations set on the lookup field
also apply to the UI field or the constant being compared with the lookup field. Examples include:

• If the lookup field value is a boolean and you want to compare it with a constant value, the constant

value should be either Y (Yes) or N (No).

constraints must also apply to the constant value.

field value can be either C (which stands for the customers group) or S (which stands for the
vendors group). When comparing this field with a constant to look up all the business partners only
in the vendors group, you need to enter S in the Value / Field Name field.

1.19.2.4.2.2.5  Guidelines for Effective Formulas

Constants, operators, variables, and functions are essential elements in creating effective formulas for
calculations and logical operations. This topic is useful for understanding and implementing formulas for
User-Defined Values (UDVs) in the Web client for accurate and efficient data processing.

A formula typically includes a combination of the following elements:

• Constants:

Fixed numerical values (such as "3"), text values or strings (such as "Hello"), or boolean values (such as
"true" or "false") that do not change.

• Arithmetic Operators:

Symbols that indicate a mathematical operation to be performed on one or more operands (values):
• + (addition)
• − (subtraction)

 Note

When you type it in a formula, please use the minus sign "−". Do not use the en dash ("–"), em dash
("—"), or hyphen ("-").

• * (multiplication)
• / (division)

 Example

100 + quantity * amount / 10

852

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Parentheses:

Symbols used to control the order of operations within a formula. For example: (a + b) * c ensures that
the addition is performed before the multiplication.

• Relational Operators:

Relational operators are used to compare one operand (usually a value or a data point) with another.
These operators are fundamental for setting conditions or creating certain rules within the application. The
evaluation result is a boolean: true or false. Examples of relational operators include:
• == (equal to)
• != (not equal to)
• > (greater than)
• < (less than)
• >= (greater than or equal to)
• <= (less than or equal to)

 Example

1+2 >= 3

CardCode != CardName

• Logical Operators:

Logical operators are used to compare two boolean expressions or values to return a boolean result. They
are essential for constructing complex conditional expressions.
• AND: The logical AND (&&) operator returns true only if both operands are true.
• OR: The logical OR (||) operator returns true if either of the operands is true.
• NOT: The logical NOT (!) operator reverses the result of an expression, returning false if the

expression is originally evaluated as true and vice versa.

 Example

1 == 1 && CardCode != CardName

 Note

In a logical formula, you only need to specify the field name, without comparing it to true or false.
For example, to set a value to a checkbox based on the AND operator of two boolean fields, you can
simply write the formula as <Field 1> && <Field 2>.

While you can explicitly check their values, it's not necessary. In such cases, for a field from the detailed
view User Interface (UI) where you currently set up UDVs, you need to compare it with true or false,
and for a field from the SAP Business One database, compare it with Y or N. For example, if Field A
is from the UI and Field B is from the database, the formula would be: (<Field A> == true) &&
(<Field B> == 'Y').

• Functions:

Predefined operations or calculations that take inputs (arguments) and return a result:
• String functions
• Date and time functions
• Mathematical functions
• Logical functions

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

853

• Utility functions

• Variables:

Placeholders within a formula that can hold different values. Variables can represent any type of value,
such as numbers, strings, boolean, or more complex data types like dates or objects.
Variables are useful, particularly when you want to do computations or transformations of values that you
might not know ahead of time, or that might change each time you run your program or script. They are
fundamental tools for storing, labeling, and manipulating data.
You can use both global variables and reference fields as variables in your formula. When you use a field
variable in a formula for UDVs in the Web client, it typically refers to the uname property of a UI control, or a
field name in a lookup object within the SAP Business One database.
For more information about uname, see Finding the uname for a UI Field [page 872].

In this section, we will provide examples of effective formulas that utilize variables and mathematical and
logical functions and expressions.

Basic Expressions [page 855]

This topic introduces basic expressions that you can use in your formulas, including numeric
and alphanumeric values, string concatenation, and calculations. These expressions are useful for
manipulating both text and numeric data.

Global Variables [page 858]

Global variables are variables that are declared in a global scope, meaning they are accessible from
any apps, views, and pages of the Web client. Unlike local variables, which are accessible only within
the function or block in which they are defined, global variables can be accessed and modified by any
function available in the application.

String Functions [page 860]

With string functions, you can manipulate and analyze strings, which are sequences of characters.
These functions are crucial for processing, presenting, and storing textual data efficiently.

Date Functions and Expressions [page 863]

This topic provides examples of how to use date functions and expressions in your formulas to
manipulate and extract date values. This is useful for calculating and displaying dates in specific
business contexts.

Time Functions and Expressions [page 865]

Time functions and expressions are used to facilitate effective handling of time data, whether it's for
scheduling, logging, or displaying time-sensitive information.

Mathematical Functions [page 868]

With mathematical functions, you can perform a wide range of numerical calculations. These functions
enable you to build complex and dynamic formulas that can process data efficiently and effectively.

Logical Functions [page 870]

Logical functions are operations that evaluate expressions and return boolean values. They are used to
perform decision-making tasks, control flow, and facilitate conditional expressions.

Utility Functions [page 871]

Utility functions are helper functions designed to perform common tasks or operations that can be
reused throughout different parts of the Web client application.

1.19.2.4.2.2.5.2  Global Variables

Global variables are variables that are declared in a global scope, meaning they are accessible from any apps,
views, and pages of the Web client. Unlike local variables, which are accessible only within the function or
block in which they are defined, global variables can be accessed and modified by any function available in the
application.

The naming of global variables follows this pattern: app.<variable name>, whereas app is the namespace
name, which stands for the Web client application. Here is a list of all available global variables:

1.19.2.4.2.3  Finding the uname for a UI Field

Context

On the detailed view User Interface (UI) in the Web client, each field is assigned a unique name (uname). This
uname is used to uniquely identify and reference an individual field.

The uname of a field looks similar to its UI label. You can find the uname for a specific field on the UI with Web
Client Inspector, a standard extension available in both the Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers.

Procedure

To find the uname of a specific field, proceed as follows:

1. Follow the instructions in Installing Web Client Inspector to install Web Client Inspector.

2. Follow the instructions in Working with Web Client Inspector to open the Properties tab for a specific field.

3. On the Properties tab, find the uname property value.

1.19.2.4.3  Importing User-Defined Values

Context

You can import a JSON file that contains setups for User-Defined Values (UDVs) from an existing company to
your current company within the same SAP Business One localization.

Procedure

1.

In the Web client, open the User-Defined Values app in one of the following ways:

• On the Home page, choose the User-Defined Values tile in the Administration group.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Administration User-Defined Values .

2. Choose Import in the table toolbar to open the Import User-Defined Values page.

3. On the Setting tab, next to the Import from File field, choose Browse.

4. Select and upload a local JSON file that contains a set of UDVs setup data.

A new Preview tab appears with a Results table, showing general pre-check information about all the UDVs
setups extracted from the file. Eligible setups are marked as Ready in the Status column.

5. Choose the Business Object column header in the table to open the sort menu. Choose either Sort

Ascending or Sort Descending to sort business objects alphabetically.

6. Select one or more UDVs setups for fields within the same business object, for example, sales orders, and

then choose Test from the table toolbar.

When you choose Test for the first time, you are prompted with the following additional message: This
page contains unsaved data. Are you sure you want to leave the page? Choose OK to
leave the current page. Despite your confirmation, all uploaded setup data is saved.

 Note

• If you select multiple setups across different types of business objects, the Test button is grayed

out.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

873

• It is highly recommended that you test all setups before starting the import process. While you can
proceed without testing, you need to manually test the setups afterward to ensure accuracy and
reliability.

7. You are directed to the testing pages, where the system automatically tests the validity of the selected

UDVs setups and their applicability to the target fields in the corresponding business object. Please wait
for the test process to complete. Once finished, you are navigated back to the Import User-Defined Values
page.

The results previously shown in the Status column changes from Ready to one of the following:

• Test Successful:

This status indicates that the corresponding setup passes the test and is ready for import.

• Test Failed:

This status indicates that the corresponding setup doesn't pass the test and cannot be imported. You
can see an error category in the Error Message column. Please troubleshoot the issues first and then
attempt to import again. For more information, see Troubleshooting Test Errors During Import [page
875].

To delete unwanted UDVs setup records, select them and choose Delete from the table toolbar.

8. Choose Import at the page bottom.

This action imports all eligible UDVs setups with the Test Successful status, regardless of their selection
status. It does not import any tested setups with the Test Failed status or untested setups with the Ready
status.

However, if you do not choose Test in the previous step to verify any setups, all untested setups with the
Ready status will be imported. Please manually test the setups afterward to ensure accuracy and reliability.

Choose OK when you are prompted to confirm the message: After you choose "Import", the
system automatically applies all setups following successful imports. Do you
want to continue?

9. Check the import results in the Status column:

• Import Successful:

This status indicates that the corresponding UDVs setup is successfully imported and applied in the
Web client.
• Import Skipped:

This status indicates that the corresponding UDVs setup already exists in the Web client and is,
therefore, skipped during the import.

• Import Failed:

This status indicates that an error occurs during the import of the corresponding UDVs setup. You can
see more details in the Error Message column.

10. Choose Exit to go back to the Manage User-Defined Values list view.

Related Information

Managing User-Defined Values [page 830]

874

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

1.19.2.4.3.1  Troubleshooting Test Errors During Import

When importing setups for User-Defined Values (UDVs) on the Import User-Defined Values page, you may
encounter test errors. If a UDVs setup doesn't pass the test before you import it, you will see an error category
in the Error Message column of the Results table. These categories include the following:

• Setup validity errors.
• Formula applicability errors.
• Internal errors.

In this topic, we provide checklists to help you identify and troubleshoot potential issues in each category more
effectively.

Setup Validity Errors

These errors often arise due to the following issues:

• The formula name is missing in a UDVs setup created based on a formula.
• The formula name is duplicated in a UDVs setup created based on a formula.
• The formula name exceeds the maximum character limit for a UDVs setup based on a formula.
• Formula content is missing in a UDVs setup created based on a formula.
• Trigger fields for automatic refreshing are either missing or invalid in a UDVs setup created based on a

formula.

• Trigger fields for automatic refreshing are duplicated in a UDVs setup created based on a formula.
• More than five trigger fields are specified for automatic refreshing in a UDVs setup created based on a

formula.

• One or more trigger fields specified for automatic refreshing in a UDVs setup created based on a formula

are involved in circular dependency.

• Values are missing in a UDVs setup created based on a filtered list.
• The imported data is invalid.
• The customization method is either missing or invalid.
• The view GUID is either missing or invalid.
• The control uname is missing.

Formula Applicability Errors

Formula applicability errors may occur when a UDVs setup is created based on a formula. These errors are
usually caused by the following factors:

• The formula result is not of date type, yet the applied control is a date picker.
• The formula result is not of time type, yet the applied control is a time picker.
• The formula result does not match "Y", "N", or other acceptable values representing true or false for a

checkbox.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

875

• The formula result does not match "Y", "N", or other acceptable values representing selected or deselected

states for a radio button.

• The formula result exceeds the maximum character limit for an input field.
• The formula result exceeds the maximum character limit for a text area.

Internal Errors

Internal errors may occur under the following conditions:

• Conflict errors occur when multiple users simultaneously edit or save the same UDVs setup.
• Errors occur when calling the UI Framework API setValueByUname.
• Errors occur when calling the UI Framework API getValueByUname.
• Values set for a control do not meet its constraints.
• Errors occur when attempting to retrieve a control instance using a UI Framework API.
• Errors occur when calling the UI Framework API setShowAllData for the table control.
• Errors occur when calling the Service Layer API to retrieve a list of lookup objects for a UDVs setup based

on a formula.

• Errors occur when calling the Service Layer API to retrieve a list of lookup fields for a UDVs setup based on

a formula.

• Errors occur when calling the Service Layer API serverTimeFromSL to retrieve values for time-related

application variables within the app. namespace.

• Errors occur when saving a UDVs setup data using the change path API.
• Errors occur when calling the formula parser API evaluate to test a formula.
• Errors occur when calling the formula parser API addDataSet to utilize auto-complete for filling variables

within predefined namespaces in the formula input field.

1.19.2.4.4  Copying User-Defined Values

Context

You can use the following two methods to copy User-Defined Values (UDVs) setups for fields between different
business objects:

• Copy:

Use this method to copy one or more UDVs setups from a single source business object to multiple targets
within the same business module or group without automatic testing.
For example, you can copy UDVs setups from sales orders to deliveries and A/R invoices within the same
Sales module, but not to goods receipt POs or A/P invoices in the Purchasing module. After the copying,
you need to manually test the setup's validity and its applicability to the corresponding fields in the target
business objects.

876

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Copy After Test:

Use this method to copy one or more UDVs setups from a single source business object to a single target
within the same business module or group after automatic testing.
For example, you can copy UDVs setups from sales orders to deliveries within the same Sales module, but
not to both sales orders and A/R invoices. The system manually tests the validity and applicability of the
selected setups before executing the copying. Only setups that pass the test are eligible for copying.

 Note

This function is unavailable for purchase requests due to the incompatibility of their document structure
with other business objects.

Procedure

1.

In the Web client, open the Manage User-Defined Values list view in one of the following ways:

• On the Home page, choose the User-Defined Values tile in the Administration group.
• On the Home page, choose  Main Menu Administration User-Defined Values .

2. Find the source business object from the root-level nodes in the Business Object tree column of the table.

3. Choose the  Expand/Collapse icon next to the business object to reveal all its child nodes.

4. Choose the  Expand/Collapse icon next to the Body Area and Table Section submenus to reveal all their

child nodes.

5. Select one or more UDVs setups under the Body Area and Table Section submenus of the same business

object.

6. From the table toolbar, choose Copy, or choose the  Open Menu icon and then choose Copy After Test.

7. Proceed as follows according to your previous choice:

• If you choose Copy, proceed as follows in the Copy dialog box that appears:

1. Select one or more targets from a dropdown list of all available business objects within the same

business module or group.

2. Choose OK.

3. An Information dialog box appears. Review the copying results in the dialog box.

4. Choose OK to exit.

• If you choose Copy After Test, proceed as follows in the Copy After Test dialog box that appears:

1. Select one target from a dropdown list of all available business objects within the same business

module or group.

2. Choose Test.

3. You are directed to the testing pages, where the system automatically tests the validity of the
selected UDVs setups and their applicability to the corresponding fields in the target business
object. Please wait for the test process to complete. Once finished, you are navigated back to
the previous Manage User-Defined Values page, where an Information dialog box shows the test
results. Review the test results.

4. Choose Copy Successful Setups to copy setups that pass the test to the target business object.

5. An Information dialog box appears. Review the copying results in the dialog box.

6. Choose OK to exit.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

877

Results

If a UDVs setup is copied successfully, it is added as an inline item under the Body Area or Table Section
submenu of the target business object menu, and highlighted with a visual indicator (a blue bar) on the far left.

If you choose to copy a UDVs setup without automatic testing, follow the steps below to manually test the
setup afterwards:

1.

In the Manage User-Defined Values list view, select the setup and choose Edit from the table toolbar.

2. The editing dialog box for the customized field opens in the detailed view of the corresponding business

object. The user interface (UI) varies according to the selected customization method.

3.

In the editing dialog box, review the filtered list items or choose Test Formula to verify the formula.

 Note

same group, an automatic match will be applied. For example, copying a UDVs setup for the Delivery Date

A/R invoices.
