Customizable Fields

The customizable fields within a business object can vary depending on several factors, including data
dependencies and user interface (UI) control types. For instance, you cannot customize a dropdown list with
a filtered list if it uses the combo box control with dynamic binding, nor can you customize a UI field with a
formula if it uses the HBox control, where "H" stands for "Horizontal".

A typical use case for the HBox control is the Item Description column within the detailed views of sales orders.
Here's how you can identify this control:

Go to the Contents tab of a sales order. In the upper right corner of the Product table in the Details section,
choose the  Settings icon to open the Select Columns dialog box, and then select the Type option to make this

880

column visible in the Product table. When you work with the Product table and set the Type of a row to Regular,
you will see an input box in the Item Description column. When the row type is Text, you will find a line text
editor in the Item Description column instead.

The Item Description column is non-customizable because it employs the HBox control and incorporates two
different types of child controls.

To identify whether the control type of a specific field is HBox, proceed as follows:

1. Follow the instructions in Finding the uname for a UI Field to open the Properties tab for the field.

2. On the Properties tab, look for the value of the ctrlType property.

 Example

The ctrlType value for the Item Description column is HBox.

1.19.3  Importing from Microsoft Excel

Prerequisites

Prepare a Microsoft Excel file with the data you want to import. Make sure the file meets the following
requirements:

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

881

• The file must not contain any blank rows.
• The file must be saved as TXT, xlsx, and csv files. SAP Business One, Web client supports the following TXT

formats for import:
• Tab-delimited
• MS-DOS
• Macintosh

• The number of characters in the columns of the Microsoft Excel table must not be greater than the length

of the corresponding fields in SAP Business One, Web client.

Context

You can import certain data from a Microsoft Excel file to a company in SAP Business One, Web client. The data
is copied from the columns of the Microsoft Excel file and added to the corresponding fields the in the SAP
Business One, Web client system.

Use this method to add new records or to update existing records.

Procedure

1. Open an SAP Business One, Web client app where the Import from Microsoft Excel feature is enabled. The
entry point to this feature may vary across different apps. For more information about specific apps, see
the help links in the Related Information section.

2.

In the Import from Microsoft Excel settings page, enter the required information. If your file contains
a header row, which typically includes the names of the object fields, select the File Contains Header
checkbox.

3. On the right of the File to Import field, choose Browse to upload your prepared file. Once uploaded, the

columns of your file will be visible in the Preview section.

 Note

If you make changes to your local Microsoft Excel file and want to see the updates in the Preview
section, simply choose the browse button again, select your file, and upload it. This will refresh the data
in the Preview section. To ensure a successful file reload, the fields in the system should match the
columns in your local Microsoft Excel file.

4. Choose Map Fields to map your columns to the system fields. You cannot proceed with the import without

mapping the fields.

 Note

It is recommended to map all columns to proceed with the import process. All mandatory fields must
be mapped to proceed with the import process.

You can also add or remove fields in this dialog box.

882

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

 Note

Mandatory fields cannot be removed.

5. Once the mapping is complete, choose OK. You can view the mapped columns of your file in the Preview

section along with their status (Ready or Invalid). Once the mapping is complete, choose OK. You can view
the mapped columns of your file in the Preview section along with their status (Ready or Invalid).

6.

If you are satisfied with the records, choose Import. If there are errors (Failed or Skipped), review the data
in the records and attempt the import again. To update records, upload the file again with the modified
data. If a field in the Microsoft Excel file is left empty, the system doesn't alter the existing data for that field
in the business object and it remains unchanged. However, if you enter #clr# in one of the cells of your
Microsoft Excel file and upload it, the system interprets this as a command to clear the existing data for
that field in the business object. This effectively makes it empty after the import process.

1.19.3.1  Working with Import from Microsoft Excel

Use this feature to import data from Microsoft Excel files.

 Note

This topic documents fields and other elements that either are not self-explanatory or require additional
information. Availability of these options depends on the app you are using.

Settings Tab

Import
Options

When utilizing the Import from Microsoft Excel feature, you can choose to import the main
record, known as the parent object, which holds the core information necessary for your business
operations. Alternatively, you can opt to import the associated entities, referred to as child objects,
which provide additional details or functionalities that enhance the parent object.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

883

For example, if you're working with Business Partners, the Import from Microsoft Excel option lets
you import business partner records (parent objects). You can also import specific details required
in a business partner record, such as contact persons, ship-to addresses, and bill-to addresses.
These are referred to as child objects and enrich the business partner's profile with comprehensive
information.

 Note

When importing a child object, you must include the parent key in the child object to identify
the parent record. This parent key field is mandatory, and without it, the import will fail,
whether you are adding new records or updating existing ones. This ensures that the child
objects are correctly linked to their respective parent objects, maintaining the integrity and
structure of your data.

File Contains
Header

If your file includes a header row, which typically contains the object field names, select this
checkbox to ensure the system treats the first row as a header. If you do not select this
checkbox, the system will treat the header row as a regular data row.

Import
Method

Error
Handling
Method

Choose one of the following methods to import data from a Microsoft Excel file:

• To import all data and update existing records, select the option Add New Records and Update

Existing Records.

• To import all data except for records that already exist, select the option Add New Records

Without Updating Existing Records. The system will not add any duplicate records.

• To update existing records without adding new ones, select Update Existing Records Without

Adding New Records.

You can choose from two ways to handle errors:

• Ignore all errors and process valid records: the system proceeds with processing all valid

records, regardless of the number of errors.

• Ignore up to <number> errors and process valid records: the system ignores a certain

number of errors, which you set using the Error Threshold option, and proceeds to process
valid records.

Error
Threshold

Choose the number of errors the system can ignore. If errors exceed this threshold, the
import process stops, and the status of the record is marked as Skipped. You must review
the data and attempt the import again.

Preview Tab

The Preview area is designed to provide a user-friendly interface that simulates the functionality of a Microsoft
Excel sheet, allowing you to interact with your data efficiently. This area offers several generic capabilities to
enhance user experience and streamline data management:

• Edit Cells: You can directly modify the content within individual cells, ensuring that data can be corrected

or updated as needed.

884

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

• Add/Remove Rows: You have the flexibility to insert new rows or delete existing ones, facilitating the

organization and customization of data according to their specific requirements.

 Note

To update existing records without adding new ones, select Update Existing Records Without Adding
New Records.

• Tooltip for Columns: Each column has a tooltip feature that provides additional information or guidance

related to the column's content and valid values, enhancing understanding and usability.

• Reorder Columns: Use the form settings icon to rearrange columns to suit your preferences or workflow

needs.

• Message Strip: This feature dynamically changes its content based on the current phase of the import

process, indicating the number of records successfully mapped and those that remain unmapped. It offers
essential information and progress updates to ensure that you stay informed and can take necessary
actions at each stage of the import.

• Map Fields: Choose Map Fields to open the Mapping Data Fields dialog box, where you can map your file

columns to the system fields.

The Preview area distinguishes between user operations conducted before and after the import process in the
following manner:

Before Import:

• Field Mapping: You can map fields to ensure that data is correctly aligned with the intended structure,

facilitating a smooth import process.

• Filter by Mapped/Unmapped Columns: You can apply filters to view only mapped or unmapped columns,

aiding in the identification and resolution of any discrepancies prior to import.

After Import:

• Filter by Status: You can filter the data based on its status, such as Error, Skipped, Added, or Updated,

allowing for targeted troubleshooting and review.

• Export Filter Results: You also have the option to export the filtered results to a Microsoft Excel file,
providing a convenient method for further analysis and problem-solving outside the platform.

Mapping Data Fields

Mapping Method

Choose how to align file columns with system fields, either manually or using a saved template:

• Manual: You can manually map the file columns to the system fields.
• Saved Template: Utilize a saved mapping template to automatically align your file columns with the system

fields.

• Use Predefined Template: Automatically map fields using a predefined template. You can also download

the template, enter your data in the required format, upload the file, and select this option to map the file
columns to your system fields automatically.

Field Name

You can choose the following options:

• Field Name: Only the field names will be visible in the Field in Object dropdown.
• Database Name: Only the database name will be visible in the Field in Object dropdown.

Save Template

to save your current mapping as a template. This feature allows you to avoid manually mapping fields and
columns repeatedly. Once saved, you can easily apply the same mapping to any new file by selecting Saved
Template in the Mapping Method and choosing your saved template.

1.19.4  Job Monitor

With the app Job Monitor, the job service primarily monitors tasks executed in the Web client and can also
display job initiated from the SAP Business One client.

The app enables real-time tracking of job status, scheduled time, actual execution time, and progress.
Notifications are automatically delivered in the Web client whenever a job is triggered or its status changes.

Before using Job Monitor to monitor jobs, ensure that you have fulfilled the following prerequisites:

• You have installed the Job Service component and the status of the alert service is RUNNING.

You can start the alert service from the Job Service Web page.

• You have enabled the alert service for company databases.

You can enable the alert service for companies from the System Landscape Directory (SLD) control center.

For more information about starting the alert service and enabling the alert service for company databases,
see Alert and Scheduling Settings (SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA) or Alert Settings (SAP Business
One).

 Note

In this initial release, DATEV Export is the only supported job type.

1.20  Multiple Branches

If you have enabled multiple branches in SAP Business One, the multi-branch feature is visible and functional in
Web client.

The multi-branch option allows businesses that operate branches or multiple business units to record the
activity of the various units in one database and generate reports per unit/branch. This obviates the need to
maintain multiple databases, simplifies reporting and supports data consistency. For example:

• A department store can maintain separate units for furniture, housewares, clothing, books, cosmetics and

so on.

• An exclusive jewelry brand operates four stores only, so the activity of the four branches is recorded to one

database while referencing each transaction to the respective branch.

At this stage, the multi-branch function is available in the following usages:

• Assigning a branch when creating sales documents
• Analytics by branch

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

887

• Filtering in a marketing document list view
• Managing data ownership by branch

 Note

Data ownership by branches is enabled only when the company manages data ownership by branches (like
the behavior in SAP Business One).

 Note

Web client doesn't support filtering by branch.

For more information about multi-branch capability, see Working with Multiple Branches.

1.21.2  Working with Process Maps

From the Process Maps app, you can access, create, or delete process maps:

• Use the Create button in the upper right corner of the table of the Process Maps app to enter the design

view for creating a new process map.

• When you open a specific process map, you can edit, create, duplicate, or delete it. Only user-defined maps

can be edited or deleted:
• To edit a map, choose Edit. You can change the sequence of steps and choose a new position, or delete

a step by clicking the   on the given step.

• To create a new map, choose New.
• To create a copy of a map, choose Duplicate. You can customize the copy of the map as per your needs.
• To delete a map, choose Delete.

• Delete from the list view in the Process Maps app.
• Delete from the Process Map view of the specific map.

Editing or creating a new map consists of the following:

• Add a business step.

business objects are supported:

1.21.3  Predefined Process Maps

The Process Maps group contains two predefined process maps, Quote to Cash and  Procure to Pay. These
maps enable you to perform the sales and purchasing processes more efficiently without any further
customization.

The predefined maps consist of business steps that reflect the generic end-to-end sales and purchasing
processes in the Web client.

The badge on each step in the maps refreshes when any authorized user makes changes in the database. For
example: With reference to the predefined process map Quote to Cash, if you copied sales quotations into sales
orders, the number that appears on the badge of both Process Sales Quotations and Process Sales Orders is
updated. If you closed several sales quotations, the number appearing on the Process Sales Quotations step is
reduced accordingly.

If an approval process is defined for any documents in the process maps, it is supported.

1.21.3.1  Quote to Cash

The Quote to Cash process map’s end-to-end business logic consists of the following business steps:

1. Create Sales Quotation

This launches the Sales Quotation detailed view in create mode.
On adding a sales quotation, all relevant KPIs in the respective steps are refreshed.

2. Process Sales Quotations

This launches the Sales Quotations list view with the view My Open Sales Quotations. Here you can copy
selected sales quotations into sales orders or perform other actions as required.
On completion of a task, the value in the badge of the respective steps and apps is updated.

3. Process Sales Orders

This launches the Sales Orders list view with the view My Open Sales Orders.

4. Process Deliveries

This launches the Deliveries list view with the view My Open Sales Deliveries.

5. Pay A/R Invoices

This launches the A/R Invoices list view with the view My Open A/R Invoices.

This launches the Purchase Requests detailed view in create mode.

2. Process Purchase Requests

This launches the Purchase Requests list view with the view My Open Purchase Requests. Here you can
copy selected purchase requests into purchase quotations or perform other actions as required.
On completion of a task, the value in the badge of the respective steps and apps is updated.

3. Process Purchase Quotations

This launches the Purchase Quotations list view with the view My Open Purchase Quotations.

1.22  Extensibility

Web client supports Tile Links and Extensions using various technologies (for example, Fiori/SAPUI5, React,
Vue and Angular), manage the applications in a unified life cycle management, and interact with the Web client
API and the Service Layer in a straightforward and intuitive manner.

These extensions will appear as new tiles in the Web client Fiori Launch Pad, and blend seamlessly with the
existing UI.

Web client UI API is available for you to create UI extensions on top of Web client, so that you can customize
and diversify UI pages to suit your individual business needs.

For more information, see:

• How to Develop Web Client Extensions
• Service Layer API Reference
• Web Client Extensibility Videos
• Web Client Extensibility Trainings

1.23  Setting Up SAP Business One App for Microsoft Teams

As system administrators, you can set up the SAP Business One app in Microsoft Teams for your organization
to make SAP Business One, Web client directly accessible to your organization members in Microsoft Teams.

Your organization members can use all the supported functions of the Web client through Microsoft Teams.
They can collaborate through chats and manage work easily and seamlessly without changing systems,
thereby increasing productivity and performance, especially when working remotely. By leveraging the popular
chat-based enterprise collaboration platform, this app can facilitate business processes and communication.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

895

The Web client UI is in SAP Fiori style, enabling business tasks to be carried out in a responsive, interactive, and
collaborative manner.

This app is only available when SAP Business One is deployed on-premise with version 10.0 FP 2111 or later.

Prerequisites [page 896]

Installing the App [page 896]

Upgrading the App [page 899]

Uninstalling the App [page 900]

Using the App in Microsoft Teams [page 901]

1.23.1  Prerequisites

Before you set up the SAP Business One app, make sure you have acquired the following:

• A Microsoft Teams admin account

This account is required for you to upload, install, upgrade, and uninstall the app for your organization.

• SAP Business One, Web client

The Web client is presented in tabs in Microsoft Teams. Due to security requirements, make sure that the
certificate of your Web client is trusted in your organization's environment.

• SAP Business One Service Layer

The Service Layer works primarily as a back-end data service. For security concerns, make sure that its
certificate is trusted in your organization's environment.

• SAP Business One System Landscape Directory (SLD)

Since the SLD is involved in the login process, make sure that its certificate is trusted in your organization's
environment.

1.23.2  Installing the App

Context

The SAP Business One app for Microsoft Teams is delivered along with the SAP Business One products. It is a
lightweight package in a zip format, which is comprised of a manifest file and several image files.

As this app is designed for enterprises, it is not published to the Teams' app store due to business and technical
requirements. Only IT administrators or other roles with the same authorizations in an enterprise are allowed
to upload and install this app. For more details about the app distribution, check out the guidance
Microsoft.

 from

As an IT admin, you already have the SAP Business One product package in place. Let's go through the
following steps to install the app.

and the following two image files in this package:
• color.png
• outline.png

Assuming you already have a working Web client. Its domain name and port number are

"validDomains": [

representation of your organization domains. For more details about how to specify a valid domain
name, see the guidance

 from Microsoft.

In the SAPBusinessOne folder, compress the above three files into a new zip file.

1.24  Working with Best Practices for Intelligent Automation

for SAP Business One

The best practices for intelligent automation for SAP Business One is a set of best practice templates for
business processes automation solutions and Artificial Intelligence (AI) services that allow users to automate
most of their time-consuming, repetitive tasks. The aim of the intelligent automation offerings is to enable
employees to focus more on advanced tasks while more basic or repetitive tasks can be automatically fulfilled
by the respective bots.

910

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Key Benefits

• Reduce time-consuming, manual activities by using ready-to-use automation bots and processes that

support error-free, scalable tasks and help users focus on high-value processes.

• Bring a new level of operational speed and efficiency to respond to customer needs proactively and

augment resources to address more high-value tasks.

• Optimize business processes and workflows for maximum efficiency and take advantage of intelligent

automations to make more intelligent decisions.

For more information on SAP Build Process Automation, see What Is SAP Build Process Automation? in the
online help for SAP Business One.

Related Information

How to Work with Best Practices for Process Automation for SAP Business One [page 911]

1.24.1  How to Work with Best Practices for Process
Automation for SAP Business One

During their daily work, users need to handle many small, monotonous, administrative tasks that are time-
consuming. Documents such as invoices, purchase orders, and proof of delivery notes are sent to the Inbox.
The user then needs to open the document, read it, and manually enter the data into the ERP system.

But what if users don't have to complete all these tasks themselves? The best practices for process automation
for SAP Business One give you access to software bots and process automations that are designed to mimic
humans by replacing manual clicks, interpreting text-heavy communications, and automating other tedious
business processes. You can use the automations out of the box or adapt them to your needs.

For more information on setting up the best practices for process automation, see the following topics in the
online help for SAP Business One:

• Setting Up Windows Generic Credentials
• Configuring and Orchestrating SAP Build Process Automation

1.24.1.1  Activity Creation for Business Partners

This bot creates activities for new business partner leads and automatically schedules a reminder for the
follow-up of new leads in the user’s Outlook calendar.

You can find the Activity Creation for Business Partners project template in the SAP Business Accelerator
Hub

.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

911

1.24.1.1.1  Business Case

Problem

Company representatives meet new leads at events or during their daily work. Based on their meetings,
business users create new business partner leads in SAP Business One and manually schedule activities to
follow up with the leads. This manual process is time-consuming and is also often prone to error.

Solution

The Activity Creation for Business Partners bot, developed to run in unattended mode, automatically creates
activities for new business partner leads. The bot automatically schedules a reminder for the follow-up with
new leads in the user’s Outlook calendar. Users can schedule this bot to run depending on their specific
requirements.

Business Benefits

• Reduces user effort
• Reduces the risk of manual errors
• Improves work efficiency

1.24.1.1.2  Technical Specification

Content and Strategic Intent

Following up on new business partner leads is a time-consuming activity that is prone to errors when
performed manually. The Activity Creation for Business Partners bot automates this process by creating
activities for new business partner leads and automatically scheduling a reminder for the follow-up of new
leads in the user’s Outlook calendar.

Watch this video about the setup and use of the Activity Creation for Business Partners bot.

912

PUBLIC

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

Technical Details

Overview

This bot can be set up in unattended mode using SAP Process Automation.

Attended

No

Unattended

Yes

Screen Scraping

Yes

For information on how to set up the bot in SAP Process Automation, see How to Set Up the Best Practices for
Process Automation for SAP Business One in the online help for SAP Business One.

Input/Output

As a prerequisite for running this bot, you have performed the following:

• In SAP Business One client, in  Business Partners Activity , you have defined a new activity Subject
(for example, “Created by SPA bot”) (an activity Subject in SAP Business One corresponds to an activity
Subcategory in Web client). The bot requires a unique activity subcategory to avoid duplications in
activities. The activity subject codes that are automatically created by the system for the activity subject
correspond to the values entered in the “Activity Subcategory Code” column in the configuration file.
• In SAP Business One, Web client, in  Analytics User-Defined Queries , you have created a user-defined
query with “Business Partner” as the Category and “New Lead” as the Name. Example SQL and SAP HANA
queries are provided in the configuration file on the “DB Query” sheet. To create a tile for the user-defined
query on the home page, set the Default Tile switch to Yes.

Before running the bot, you have created a local root folder that will be used by the bot to create a log folder to
store the log files.

You have downloaded the configuration Microsoft Excel file available in the Documents section of the project
template and placed it in the local root folder. In the configuration file, you have specified the "Business
Object" ("BP Activity") and "Company Code" values. The "Company Code" can be an arbitrary value (consisting
of numbers, letters, or both) to identify the company, or the branch identification number if you are using
branches for the SAP Business One company. In the “Activity Subcategory Code” column, you have entered
the activity Subject codes from SAP Business One. The activity subject codes are primary key values that you
can find in the OCLS table.

The remaining columns in the configuration file contain the rules for the activity creation and notifications in
the user’s Outlook account.

The name of the configuration file must be specified in the Application Development as the variable
“WorkSheetName”.

After running the bot, you can find the log files for the bot in the "Logs" folder. If the configuration file is set to
send a reminder about the activity in the user’s Outlook account, reminders are created in the specified user’s
Outlook calendar.

Constraints

This bot can only work with the Microsoft Windows operating system.

913

Security

Protecting User Credentials

In certain configuration scenarios, a technical user is required. In such cases, every natural person needs a
separate technical user (for example, a separate communication arrangement). The user must not share their
credentials with any other natural person.

 Remember

Some of the best practices for process automation for SAP Business One use OData for the back-end
connection to SAP Business One. These services use basic authentication (user name and password). We
designed our template bots to use the Windows Credential Manager for storing users and passwords for
the bots (regardless of whether the bot is using the front end or back end); however, you can adapt the
bot to use other similar secure storage systems. Also, regardless of whether the bot is designed to use
the front-end UI or back-end services, we highly recommend that you create individual technical users
(communication arrangement) for each “bot + business user / business scenario” pair. This enables you to
distinguish whether the action was carried out by a physical business user or by a robot, and to achieve full
traceability of the bots and human actions individually. As per any other best practices, the user must not
share their bot credentials with anyone else.

For security-relevant information that applies to SAP Process Automation, see Security in the application help
for SAP Process Automation (EN only).

Further Information

For more information, see the Technical Specification available in the Intelligent RPA Store.

1.25.2.1  DATEV Export

Context

The DATEV export function can be used to transform financial data in SAP Business One into the DATEV format
and create an export file for you to send to your tax advisor. Your tax advisor can import this file into the DATEV
system and use the data to carry out period-end, quarter-end, or year-end closing.

 Note

To use the function on Web client, you need to install and start the DATEV add-on on the SAP Business One
client.

Apps

When working with DATEV export, you can find the following apps in the Accounting group:

• DATEV Export
• Create DATEV Export

Tasks

You can carry out the following tasks with these apps:

• Search and filter DATEV export runs with filters such as run number, description, or date.
• View and manage different views of DATEV export runs.
• Create, edit, run and schedule DATEV export runs to export journal entries in the DATEV format.

 Note

You need full authorization for DATEV Export to access both apps and carry out the tasks described above.
For more information about authorization settings, see How to Define Authorizations in SAP Business One
10.0.

1.25.2.1.1  Managing DATEV Export

To open the Manage DATEV Export list view, choose the DATEV Export tile on the home page.

List views in the Web client allow you to search for specific data records, use filters to restrict the data records
currently displayed in the table area, and perform various actions with the records. The list view is also your
entry point to navigate to a detailed view of a specific data record. To open a detailed view of a specific data
record, choose the  Details icon on the row of the relevant record or choose anywhere on the record's row. By
default, the existing record is displayed in view mode.

For more information on the detailed view for DATEV export, see Working with DATEV Export [page 917].

Selecting Views

Web client list views provide you with multiple views of the dataset of DATEV export records. The views store
filter settings and parameters according to a relevant category (for example, All, Finished, Scheduled) to
determine which records are displayed in the list view. You can select one of the predefined views available in
the views menu in the top-left corner of the header area:

• All DATEV Export Runs displays all DATEV export of the company.

This view is displayed by default.

• Finished DATEV Export Runs displays all DATEV export runs with the status of Finished.
• DATEV Export Runs in Preparation displays all DATEV export runs with the status of In Preparation.
• Scheduled DATEV Export Runs displays all DATEV export runs with the status of Scheduled.

You can also change the parameters of a predefined view to create a custom view. For more information, see
Views [page 54].

Setting Filters

You can use the filter bar to search or set filters such as Run No., Start Date, and End Date to narrow down the
list of export runs. By specifying these criteria, you can quickly find and manage specific export runs based on
your needs.

For more information about the filter bar functions, see Filter Bar [page 54].

1.25.2.1.2.1  Creating and Running DATEV Export

Prerequisites

• The DATEV add-on has been installed and started on the SAP Business One client.
• The alert service is enabled for the current company in System Landscape Directory, and the alert and

scheduling service is started on Job Service. For more information, see the Administrator’s Guide provided
with SAP Business One or SAP Business One, version for SAP HANA.

• The option for Split Journal Entry Posting by Document Lines under  Administration Configuration

Accounting Accounting Settings  has been set to Split.

• The default folder for attachments, which is defined under  Administration Configuration General

Attachment Settings , can be accessed by Service Layer.

• You have full authorization for DATEV Export.

Procedure

1. To create a new DATEV export, choose the Create DATEV Export tile.

2.

In the General Data section, enter a description for the export run.

 Note

Export Path displays the location where export files are saved. The path uses the default attachments

folder, which is defined under  Administration Configuration General Attachment Settings .

For DATEV export runs with the status of In Preparation, the export path updates if the default
attachments folder is changed. For all other statuses, the export path remains unchanged.

3.

In the DATEV Master Data section, provide the following details about the DATEV export.

Advisor Number and
Advisor Name

Specify the number and name of the tax advisor. You can ask your tax
advisor for the information.

Client Number

Specify the client number. You can ask your tax advisor for the information.

User Guide for SAP Business One, Web Client
SAP Business One, Web Client

PUBLIC

919

DFV Code Enter a code that DATEV uses to differentiate users. You can customize the code, for example,

by entering your initials.

Account
Number Length

Specify the number of digits in the account number. For general ledger accounts, enter
a value between 4 and 8. For subledger accounts, enter a value between 4 and 9.

DATEV Interim
Account

Specify the interim account to be used for balancing an m:n relationship. The account
number must contain between 4 and 8 digits.

 Example

9999

DATEV Format Version

Specify the version of the DATEV format. The default value is 700.

4.

In the Journal Entry Selection section, define the selection criteria for journal entries to be exported. You
can select to export all journal entries or selected journal entries, such as those generated from A/R and
A/P invoices and credit memos, or manual journal entries.

5. To add the new DATEV export to the company database, choose one of the following: Add & View, Add &

New, Add & Back.

6. Choose Run on the right side of the header. Then the Preview window opens.

7. When there's data to be exported, choose Run Now to run the export, or choose Schedule for Later to

schedule the export run.

Results

You can track the progress in the message strip below the tab title or in notifications. Once the run is complete,
you can view results and related data in the Summary tab, and download the exported files.

 Note

To get notifications for the DATEV export run, you need to enable the notification for Wizard Tasks. For more
information, see Notifications [page 50].
